title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
皇上臨御之八年為正德癸酉天
下當鄉試時山東濱池孽猜
武僈文興而士之藏器抱藝
者亦嚮光是監察御史李〔□〕
奉
命來按茲土首以科目得人為己
===
任屆期適
欽命司禮監太監賴〔義〕刑部左侍
郎黄〔珂〕錦衣衛都指揮使陸
宣〔□〕有事
藩府欣逢盛典鎮守太監畢〔真〕
雅重斯文巡撫右僉都御史
趙〔璜〕加意作興士類總理河
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

皇上臨御之八年，為正德癸酉，天下當鄉試。時山東濱池孽猜，武僈文興，而士之藏器抱藝者亦嚮光。是監察御史李〔□〕奉命來按茲土，首以科目得人為己任。屆期，適欽命司禮監太監賴〔義〕、刑部左侍郎黄〔珂〕、錦衣衛都指揮使陸宣〔□〕有事藩府，欣逢盛典。鎮守太監畢〔真〕雅重斯文，巡撫右僉都御史趙〔璜〕加意作興士類，總理河
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The eighth year of His Majesty’s reign was the guiyou year of the Zhengde era [1513], when the Provincial Examination was due to be held throughout the empire. At that time, in Shandong, [the passage 濱池孽猜 is obscure], military affairs were neglected [?] and literary culture flourished. Scholars who harbored talents and cultivated learning likewise turned toward the light. Investigating Censor Li〔□〕came by imperial command to inspect this territory and made recruiting worthy men through the examinations his foremost responsibility.

When the appointed time arrived, Lai Yi, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial; Huang Ke, Left Vice Minister of Justice; and Lu Xuan〔□〕, Regional Military Commissioner of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, happened to be attending to business at the princely establishment by imperial command, and were delighted to encounter this grand occasion. The Regional Command Eunuch Bi Zhen had long esteemed literary culture. Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, devoted particular attention to encouraging the scholars. The director-general of river …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
道右副都御史劉〔愷〕又力捐
之總兵官右都督劉〔顯〕巡鹽
監察御史徐〔贊〕胥贊厥成於
是〔檄〕與訓導吳〔彰德〕膺聘爲
考試官而同考則教授陳〔鍚〕
學正林〔汝舟〕〔魏謐〕教諭楊〔數〕
李〔秦〕張〔邦教〕陳瑞至則左布
===
政使〔白璘〕右布政使〔秦金〕爲
提調按察使吳〔學〕副使王〔金〕
爲監試而左參政張〔潛〕張〔官〕
右參政房〔塤〕副使王〔士昭〕王
〔良臣〕朱〔埜〕〔鄒尚義〕李〔充嗣〕蔣
〔曙〕林〔廷茂〕左參議閔〔楷〕右參
議徐〔永〕僉事盛〔儀〕呂〔和〕潘〔珍〕
punctuated: 道右副都御史劉〔愷〕又力捐之，總兵官右都督劉〔顯〕、巡鹽監察御史徐〔贊〕胥贊厥成。於是〔檄〕與訓導吳〔彰德〕膺聘爲考試官，而同考則教授陳〔鍚〕、學正林〔汝舟〕、〔魏謐〕、教諭楊〔數〕、李〔秦〕、張〔邦教〕、陳瑞。至則左布政使〔白璘〕、右布政使〔秦金〕爲提調，按察使吳〔學〕、副使王〔金〕爲監試，而左參政張〔潛〕、張〔官〕、右參政房〔塤〕、副使王〔士昭〕、王〔良臣〕、朱〔埜〕、〔鄒尚義〕、李〔充嗣〕、蔣〔曙〕、林〔廷茂〕、左參議閔〔楷〕、右參議徐〔永〕、僉事盛〔儀〕、呂〔和〕、潘〔珍〕
translation_en:
…waterways, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Kai, also contributed generously to this undertaking. Regional Commander and Right Chief Military Commissioner Liu Xian and Investigating Censor for Salt Administration Xu Zan both helped bring it to fruition. Accordingly, Xi [?] and Assistant Instructor Wu Zhangde accepted invitations to serve as Examiners. The Associate Examiners were Prefectural School Instructor Chen Yang; Subprefectural School Instructors Lin Ruzhou and Wei Mi; and County School Instructors Yang Shu, Li Qin, Zhang Bangjiao, and Chen Rui.

Upon arrival [?], Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Bai Lin and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Qin Jin served as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Wu Xue and Vice Surveillance Commissioner Wang Jin served as examination monitors. Meanwhile, Left Vice Administration Commissioners Zhang Qian and Zhang Guan; Right Vice Administration Commissioner Fang Xun; Vice Surveillance Commissioners Wang Shizhao, Wang Liangchen, Zhu Ye, Zou Shangyi, Li Chongsi, Jiang Shu, and Lin Tingmao; Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Min Kai; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Yong; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Sheng Yi, Lü He, and Pan Zhen…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
蔡〔芝 甯〕許〔湾 達〕牛〔鸞 王〕〔棟〕谷
以分地防範于外至於百執
事皆慎簡以充御史〔璣〕寔監
臨之凡故事畢行惟謹視往
歲有加焉乃合提學副使陳
〔琳〕所選士而三試之如
制拔其尤七十有五人第其氏
===
名梓其文之優者為錄以
獻〔楠〕宜序諸首粵自唐虞三代
用人之典弗傳而後世科舉
之途啓焉唐宋以來得人盛
矣我
太祖高皇帝即位之初首詔開科
求賢圖治之心懇切誠至
punctuated:
蔡〔芝 甯〕、許〔湾 達〕、牛〔鸞 王〕〔棟〕、谷，以分地防範于外。至於百執事，皆慎簡以充。御史〔璣〕寔監臨之。凡故事，畢行惟謹，視往歲有加焉。乃合提學副使陳〔琳〕所選士，而三試之如制，拔其尤七十有五人，第其氏名，梓其文之優者為錄以獻。〔楠〕宜序諸首。
粵自唐虞三代用人之典弗傳，而後世科舉之途啓焉。唐宋以來，得人盛矣。我太祖高皇帝即位之初，首詔開科，求賢圖治之心懇切誠至。
translation_en:
…Cai〔Zhi Ning〕, Xu〔Wan Da〕, Niu〔Luan Wang〕〔Dong〕, and Gu [?] were assigned separate areas to guard outside. All those serving in the various subordinate capacities were carefully selected for their duties. The Censor, Ji〔璣〕, served as Supervising Official. Every established procedure was carried out with the utmost care, exceeding that of previous years. They then assembled the candidates selected by Chen Lin 陳琳, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions according to the regulations. They selected the seventy-five most outstanding candidates, ranked their names, and printed their superior compositions as a record to be presented to the throne. It falls to me, Nan 楠, to place a preface at its beginning.
The institutions for employing worthy men under Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties ceased to be transmitted; in later ages, the path of recruitment through civil-service examinations opened. From the Tang and Song onward, it yielded worthy men in abundance. At the beginning of his reign, our Emperor Taizu Gao first decreed the opening of examinations. His desire to seek worthy men and achieve good government was earnest and utterly sincere…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承懋篤前烈迨我
皇上運撫盈成益慎養賢取士之
法是故賫序之所甄陶風聲
之所鼓舞
深仁厚澤之所覃被者既久至
於今雖少阨戎寇而弦誦之
聲不絶人才之盛宜哉昔人
===
有云太上立德其次立功其
次立言若以言爲下者然考
之語曰有德者必有言書曰
敷奏以言明庶以功則曰德
曰功又未甞不資於言也是
以皐陶邁種德而陳謨伊尹
本一德而作訓卒之明刑弼
punctuated:
列聖相承，懋篤前烈。迨我皇上運撫盈成，益慎養賢取士之法。是故賫序之所甄陶、風聲之所鼓舞、深仁厚澤之所覃被者既久，至於今，雖少阨戎寇，而弦誦之聲不絶，人才之盛宜哉！
昔人有云：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」若以言爲下者。然考之，《語》曰：「有德者必有言。」《書》曰：「敷奏以言，明庶以功。」則曰德、曰功，又未甞不資於言也。是以皐陶邁種德而陳謨，伊尹本一德而作訓，卒之明刑弼
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors carried on the achievements of their predecessors, diligently strengthening their legacy. When our present Emperor came to preside over this flourishing and accomplished realm, he exercised still greater care in the methods of nurturing worthy men and selecting scholars. Thus, scholars have long been molded by the schools [?], inspired by the influence of exemplary conduct, and touched by far-reaching benevolence and generous favor. Even now, although somewhat afflicted by armed raiders, the sounds of strings and recitation have never ceased. How fitting that men of talent should flourish!
An ancient saying declares: “Highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievements; next is establishing words of lasting worth.” This seems to place words lowest. Yet, on examination, the Analects says: “Those who possess virtue invariably have words of worth.” The Book of Documents says: “Have them present their statements in words, and assess them all through their achievements.” Thus neither virtue nor achievement has ever dispensed with words. Accordingly, Gao Yao vigorously cultivated virtue and presented his counsels; Yi Yin grounded himself in single-minded virtue and composed his instructions. Ultimately, they clarified punishments to support …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
教成四方風動之休而致君
澤民格天之功懋著茲科取
士亦求之於是而已矣況山
東古鄒魯之邦吾夫子著書
明道以淑人心以垂世教以
上承堯舜禹湯文武周公之
統千載之下聞遺風而興起
===
者顧豈少哉今觀中式之文
皆渾厚爾雅庶幾乎前所謂
立言而發明吾道者固在也
諸士往哉繇是而上春官奉
廷對自一命以至服大僚與有
事君之責宇宙間事皆吾分
內其將何以副之是必崇道
punctuated:
教，成四方風動之休，而致君澤民格天之功懋著。茲科取士，亦求之於是而已矣。況山東，古鄒魯之邦，吾夫子著書明道，以淑人心，以垂世教，以上承堯舜禹湯文武周公之統。千載之下，聞遺風而興起者，顧豈少哉？今觀中式之文，皆渾厚爾雅，庶幾乎前所謂立言而發明吾道者，固在也。

諸士往哉！繇是而上春官，奉廷對，自一命以至服大僚，與有事君之責。宇宙間事，皆吾分內，其將何以副之？是必崇道
translation_en:
…instruction, achieving the splendid result of transforming all four quarters as though moved by the wind; thus their achievements in guiding the ruler, benefiting the people, and reaching Heaven were eminently manifest. In selecting men through this examination, we seek precisely these qualities, and nothing more. Moreover, Shandong is the ancient land of Zou and Lu. Our Master wrote books and elucidated the Way to improve people’s hearts, transmit instruction to later generations, and carry forward the tradition of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. More than a thousand years later, can those who hear of his enduring influence and are inspired to emulate him be few? Looking now at the writings of those who passed, all are substantial and classically elegant. Among them there surely are works approaching what was described above as establishing enduring words and illuminating our Way.

Go forward, gentlemen! From here you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites for examination and submit your responses at court. From your first appointment to service in high office, you will share responsibility for serving the ruler. All affairs within the universe fall within our proper responsibilities: how will you meet them? You must surely exalt the Way…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
德礪名節以成正大光明之
業斯不負
列聖作育之恩吾夫子孚秀之地
而科目亦與有榮已矣其或
淟涊脂韋旅進旅進而於身
心天下漫焉無補豈直諸士
之羞也哉記曰事君先資其
===
言令日事也又曰拜自獻其
身以成其信於他日有望焉
錄成敢申告以勵其初
直隸保定府滿城縣儒學教
諭徐㮚謹序
punctuated:
德，礪名節，以成正大光明之業，斯不負列聖作育之恩、吾夫子孚秀之地，而科目亦與有榮已矣。其或淟涊脂韋，旅進旅進，而於身心天下漫焉無補，豈直諸士之羞也哉？《記》曰：「事君先資其言。」令日事也。又曰：「拜自獻其身，以成其信。」於他日有望焉。錄成，敢申告以勵其初。
直隸保定府滿城縣儒學教諭徐㮚謹序。
translation_en:
…virtue and temper your reputation and integrity, so as to accomplish upright and honorable deeds. Only thus will you prove worthy of the nurturing grace of the successive sage emperors and of the land that brought forth our Master’s excellence [?]; the examination system, too, will share in the honor. If, instead, you remain mired in baseness and pliant accommodation, advancing with the crowd, advancing with the crowd [?], while contributing nothing to the cultivation of your own persons and minds or to the world, would the disgrace fall upon you gentlemen alone?
The Record of Rites says: “In serving a ruler, first offer one’s words as a pledge.” This is the task of the present day [?]. It also says: “Bow and offer yourself in person, thereby fulfilling your pledge.” There are expectations for you in the days to come. Now that this record is complete, I venture to reiterate these admonitions to encourage you at the outset.
Preface respectfully written by Xu Li 徐㮚, Instructor of the Confucian School of Mancheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
正德八年山東鄉試
監臨官
巡按山東監察御史李璣〔天儀直隸徐州蕭縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使白圻〔輔之直隸武進縣人甲辰進士〕
山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使秦金〔國聲直隸無錫縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
山東等處提刑按察司按察使吳學〔遜之直隸無錫縣人甲辰進士〕
山東等處提刑按察司副使王金〔白良河南臨潁縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
直隸保定府滿城縣儒學教諭徐楠〔良用直隸武進縣人辛酉貢士〕
浙江湖州府歸安縣儒學訓導吳彰德〔昌符福建莆田縣人壬子貢士〕
同考試官
浙江寧波府儒學教授陳鑑〔特教福建候官縣人乙卯貢士〕
直隸河間府景州儒學學正林汝舟〔濟川福建閩縣人丁卯貢士〕
陝西西安府同州儒學學正魏謐〔邦寧河南汝寧所人丁卯貢士〕
福建邵武府邵武縣儒學教諭楊斆〔學文江西豐城縣人辛酉貢士〕
河南汝寧府汝陽縣儒學教諭李泰〔定夫直隸無錫縣人甲子貢士〕
punctuated:
正德八年山東鄉試。

監臨官：巡按山東監察御史李璣〔天儀，直隸徐州蕭縣人，戊辰進士〕。

提調官：山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使白圻〔輔之，直隸武進縣人，甲辰進士〕。山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使秦金〔國聲，直隸無錫縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：山東等處提刑按察司按察使吳學〔遜之，直隸無錫縣人，甲辰進士〕。山東等處提刑按察司副使王金〔白良，河南臨潁縣人，壬戌進士〕。

考試官：直隸保定府滿城縣儒學教諭徐楠〔良用，直隸武進縣人，辛酉貢士〕。浙江湖州府歸安縣儒學訓導吳彰德〔昌符，福建莆田縣人，壬子貢士〕。

同考試官：浙江寧波府儒學教授陳鑑〔特教，福建候官縣人，乙卯貢士〕。直隸河間府景州儒學學正林汝舟〔濟川，福建閩縣人，丁卯貢士〕。陝西西安府同州儒學學正魏謐〔邦寧，河南汝寧所人，丁卯貢士〕。福建邵武府邵武縣儒學教諭楊斆〔學文，江西豐城縣人，辛酉貢士〕。河南汝寧府汝陽縣儒學教諭李泰〔定夫，直隸無錫縣人，甲子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shandong Provincial Examination, eighth year of Zhengde (1513).

Supervising Official:
Li Ji, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Shandong. His courtesy name was Tianyi; he was from Xiao County, Xuzhou, in Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuchen year.

Proctors:
Bai Qi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong. His courtesy name was Fuzhi; he was from Wujin County in Zhili and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Qin Jin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong. His courtesy name was Guosheng; he was from Wuxi County in Zhili and was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examination Supervisors:
Wu Xue, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong. His courtesy name was Xunzhi; he was from Wuxi County in Zhili and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Wang Jin, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Shandong. His courtesy name was Bailiang; he was from Linying County in Henan and was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.

Examiners:
Xu Nan, Instructor at the Confucian school of Mancheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Liangyong; he was from Wujin County in Zhili and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinyou year.
Wu Zhangde, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian school of Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Changfu; he was from Putian County in Fujian and was a tribute student of the renzi year.

Associate Examiners:
Chen Jian, Professor at the Confucian school of Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Tejiao [?]; he was from Houguan County [?] in Fujian and was a tribute student of the yimao year.
Lin Ruzhou, Instructor at the Confucian school of Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Jichuan; he was from Min County in Fujian and was a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Wei Mi, Instructor at the Confucian school of Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Bangning; he was from the Runing Guard Station in Henan and was a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Yang Xiao, Instructor at the Confucian school of Shaowu County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Xuewen; he was from Fengcheng County in Jiangxi and was a tribute student of the xinyou year.
Li Tai, Instructor at the Confucian school of Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Dingfu; he was from Wuxi County in Zhili and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
浙江温州府永嘉縣儒學教諭張邦敎〔天子前隸宜興縣人戊午貢士〕
河南開封府洧川縣儒學教諭陳瑞〔舜祥應天府江浦縣人壬子貢士〕
印卷官
山東等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷趙祥〔廷瑞直隸隆慶州人吏員〕
山東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷喬磨〔宗徽河南河內縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
濟　南　府　知　府　章宦之〔道充四川嘉定州壬戌進士〕
東　昌　府　知　府　吴大有〔元亨直隸曲山縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
===

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
古者言之不出耻躬之不逮也
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千待其人而後行
夫君子所過者化所存者神上下與天地
同流豈曰小補之哉
易
酒食貞吉以中正也
===
益動而巽日進无疆天施地生其益无方
天一地二天三地四天五地六天七地八
天九地十天數五地數五五位相得
而各有合天數二十有五地數三十
凡天地之數五十有五此所以成變
化而行鬼神也
推而行之存乎通
書
無教逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日萬幾
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

古者言之不出，耻躬之不逮也。

洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千，待其人而後行。

夫君子所過者化，所存者神，上下與天地同流，豈曰小補之哉？

易

酒食貞吉，以中正也。

益，動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。

天一，地二；天三，地四；天五，地六；天七，地八；天九，地十。天數五，地數五，五位相得而各有合。天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數五十有五，此所以成變化而行鬼神也。

推而行之，存乎通。

書

無教逸欲有邦，兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The ancients were reluctant to speak, ashamed lest their conduct fall short of their words.”

“How abundant! It brings forth and nurtures the myriad things and towers to the utmost height of Heaven. How ample and great! The three hundred ceremonial rules and the three thousand rules of deportment await the right person before they can be put into practice.”

“Wherever the gentleman passes, transformation follows; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. How could one say that he offers only a small benefit?”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“Amid wine and food, steadfast correctness brings good fortune, because of centrality and correctness.”

“Increase: movement joined with yielding brings daily progress without limit. Heaven bestows and Earth brings forth; their increase knows no bounds.”

“To Heaven belongs one, to Earth two; to Heaven three, to Earth four; to Heaven five, to Earth six; to Heaven seven, to Earth eight; to Heaven nine, to Earth ten. There are five heavenly numbers and five earthly numbers. The five positions accord with one another, and each has its counterpart. The heavenly numbers total twenty-five, and the earthly numbers total thirty. Together, the numbers of Heaven and Earth total fifty-five. Through these, changes and transformations are accomplished, and ghosts and spirits act.”

“Extending it and putting it into practice depend upon thorough understanding.”

Book of Documents (Shujing)

“Do not teach those who rule states to indulge in ease and desire. Be vigilant and conscientious: in a single day or two, ten thousand incipient affairs arise.”

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
其爾克紹乃辟于先王永綏民說拜稽首
曰敢對揚天子之休命
官不必備惟其人
乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典折民惟刑
禹平水土主名山川稷降播種農殖
嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民士制百姓
于刑之中以教祗德
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉萋萋黃鳥于飛
===
集于灌木其鳴喈喈葛之覃兮施于
中谷維葉莫莫是刈是濩為絺為綌
服之無斁言告師氏言告言歸薄汚
我私薄澣我衣害澣害否歸寧父母
有酒湑我無酒酤我坎坎鼓我蹲蹲舞我
迨我暇矣飲此湑矣
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
文王既勤止我應受之敷時繹思我徂維
求定
punctuated:
其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。」說拜稽首，曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」

官不必備，惟其人。

乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。

詩

葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉萋萋。黃鳥于飛，集于灌木，其鳴喈喈。葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉莫莫。是刈是濩，為絺為綌，服之無斁。言告師氏，言告言歸。薄汚我私，薄澣我衣。害澣害否？歸寧父母。

有酒湑我，無酒酤我。坎坎鼓我，蹲蹲舞我。迨我暇矣，飲此湑矣。

追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。

文王既勤止，我應受之。敷時繹思，我徂維求定。
translation_en:
…May you enable your sovereign to carry on the example of the former kings and bring lasting peace to the people.” Yue bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”

Official posts need not all be filled; what matters is finding the right people.

Then he commanded the three lords to devote their efforts to the people. Boyi promulgated the statutes and guided the people by proper standards. Yu regulated the waters and the land and took charge of the principal mountains and rivers. Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The three lords accomplished their work, abundantly benefiting the people. The Director of Trials restrained the common people through the balanced application of punishments, teaching them to revere virtue.

Book of Odes

How the kudzu vines stretch out, spreading into the valley’s midst, their leaves luxuriant! Yellow birds fly and settle in the shrubs, their calls harmonious. How the kudzu vines stretch out, spreading into the valley’s midst, their leaves thick! I cut them and boil them, making fine cloth and coarse cloth, which I never tire of wearing. I tell my governess; I tell her I will return home. I will wash my everyday garments and cleanse my robes. Which should be washed, and which need not? I will return home to visit my parents.

If you have wine, strain it for me; if you have none, buy it for me. Beat the drums for me with resounding strokes; dance for me with measured steps. While I have leisure, let us drink this strained wine.

Carved and polished is his patterned adornment; gold and jade are his substance. Tirelessly our king labors, ordering and regulating the four quarters.

King Wen has already labored diligently; I should receive and carry on his work. I set forth these thoughts and ponder them; I go forward seeking only to bring stability.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
公及鄭伯盟于越〔桓公元年〕
冬公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十三年〕冬十有
二月會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許
男滑伯滕子同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕
荊敗蔡師于莘以蔡侯獻舞歸〔莊公十年〕
公及楚人秦人宋人陳人衛人鄭人
齊人曹人邾人薛人鄫人盟于蜀〔成
公二年〕
===
秋入衛〔閔公二年〕城楚丘〔僖公二年〕〔公如〕
晉〔昭公十五年〕公至自晉〔昭公十六年〕
禮記
大臣法小臣廉
賓入大門而奏肆夏示易以敬也卒爵而
樂闋孔子屢歎之奠酬而工升歌發
德也歌者在上匏竹在下貴人聲也
樂由陽來者也禮由陰作者也陰陽
和而萬物得
punctuated:
春秋
公及鄭伯盟于越〔桓公元年〕。冬，公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十三年〕。冬十有二月，會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕。
荊敗蔡師于莘，以蔡侯獻舞歸〔莊公十年〕。
公及楚人、秦人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人、齊人、曹人、邾人、薛人、鄫人盟于蜀〔成公二年〕。
秋，入衛〔閔公二年〕。城楚丘〔僖公二年〕。〔公如〕晉〔昭公十五年〕。公至自晉〔昭公十六年〕。
禮記
大臣法，小臣廉。
賓入大門而奏肆夏，示易以敬也。卒爵而樂闋，孔子屢歎之。奠酬而工升歌，發德也。歌者在上，匏竹在下，貴人聲也。
樂由陽來者也，禮由陰作者也。陰陽和而萬物得。
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Yue. 〔First year of Duke Huan.〕 In winter, the duke met the Marquis of Qi and made a covenant at Ke. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In winter, in the twelfth month, a meeting was held with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng, and they jointly made a covenant at You. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Jing defeated the army of Cai at Shen and returned with Xianwu, Marquis of Cai, as a captive. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

The duke and men of Chu, Qin, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Qi, Cao, Zhu, Xue, and Zeng made a covenant at Shu. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕

In autumn, an incursion was made into Wei. 〔Second year of Duke Min.〕 Fortifications were built at Chuqiu. 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕 〔The duke went to〕 Jin. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The duke returned from Jin. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites

The great ministers observe the rules; the lesser ministers maintain integrity.

When the guest enters the main gate, the music of the Four Xia is played, expressing ease together with reverence. When he has drained his cup, the music ends; Confucius repeatedly praised this. When the cup offered in return is set down, the musicians ascend and sing, making virtue manifest. The singers are above in the hall, and the gourd and bamboo instruments below: this accords honor to the human voice.

Music comes from yang; ritual arises from yin. When yin and yang are in harmony, all things attain their proper condition.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮樂刑政其極一也所以同民心而出治
道也
夫義者所以濟志也諸德之發也
第貳場
論
堯舜所以爲聖
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢遣博士大等六人分循行天下詔
〔狩六年〕
擬唐以蘇頲進同紫微黃門平章事脩國
===
史誥〔開元四年〕
擬宋以李綱爲江西安撫制置大使兼知
洪州謝表〔紹興五年〕
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
僧道拜父母
男女婚姻
老幼不拷訊
punctuated:
禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。
夫義者，所以濟志也，諸德之發也。
第貳場
論：堯舜所以爲聖。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕：擬漢遣博士大等六人分循行天下詔〔狩六年〕；擬唐以蘇頲進同紫微黃門平章事、脩國史誥〔開元四年〕；擬宋以李綱爲江西安撫制置大使兼知洪州謝表〔紹興五年〕。
判語〔五條〕：制書有違；僧道拜父母；男女婚姻；老幼不拷訊。
translation_en:
Rites, music, punishments, and government have one ultimate purpose: to unite the people’s hearts and bring forth the way of good government.
Righteousness is that by which one fulfills one’s aspirations; it is the expression of all virtues.
Second Session
Discourse: What made Yao and Shun sages.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔one topic from among these [?]〕:
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor dispatching the Erudite Da [?] and five others to make inspection tours throughout the empire, each in an assigned region. 〔Sixth year of Shou [?]〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor promoting Su Ting to Joint Manager of Affairs of the Secretariat and Chancellery, with responsibility for compiling the dynastic history. 〔Fourth year of Kaiyuan〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the voice of the Song official Li Gang upon his appointment as Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Military Control in Jiangxi, concurrently serving as Prefect of Hongzhou. 〔Fifth year of Shaoxing〕
Legal judgments 〔five topics〕:
Violation of an imperial decree.
Buddhist monks and Daoist priests bowing to their parents.
Marriage between men and women.
Exemption of the elderly and the young from interrogation under torture.
…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
毆受業師
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之學與章布不同固也錦觀往古
聖遠言湮危微精一之訓時幾喜起之
歌既不可復得後世漢唐宋諸君間有
作焉雖工無補其餘不足觀也已洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖膺
===
天命之歸萬幾之暇作爲文章
睿藻天施昭回雲漢蓋嘗伏讀
御製文集而知其梗槩矣如南郊
即位之詔發自淵衷中都
皇陵之碑特揮宸翰
太祀禮成則有勑以諭夫中書丞相拜除則有
誥以勉其功業記則有閱江樓滕新營
感舊西征等作說則有堯湯水旱伐宋
澄清黄河良馬等篇甘露祥雪論議雄
punctuated:
毆受業師。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王之學與章布不同，固也。錦觀往古，聖遠言湮，危微精一之訓、時幾喜起之歌，既不可復得，後世漢唐宋諸君間有作焉，雖工無補，其餘不足觀也已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以天縱之聖，膺天命之歸，萬幾之暇，作爲文章，睿藻天施，昭回雲漢。蓋嘗伏讀御製文集，而知其梗槩矣。如南郊即位之詔，發自淵衷；中都皇陵之碑，特揮宸翰。太祀禮成，則有勑以諭夫中書；丞相拜除，則有誥以勉其功業。記則有《閱江樓》《滕新營》《感舊》《西征》等作；說則有《堯湯水旱》《伐宋》《澄清黄河》《良馬》等篇。《甘露》《祥雪》，論議雄
translation_en:
Striking the teacher under whom one studies.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: The learning of emperors and kings differs from that of literary scholars [?]: this is certainly so. Surveying antiquity [?], we find that the sages are distant and their words have fallen into obscurity. The admonition concerning the precarious human mind, the subtle moral mind, refinement, and single-mindedness, and the song concerning the myriad affairs and joyful exertion can no longer be recovered. Among later rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, some occasionally produced writings; although accomplished, these offered no benefit, and the remainder scarcely merit consideration.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, received Heaven’s Mandate. In moments of leisure from the myriad affairs of government, he composed literary works. His august compositions spread like Heaven’s bounty, shining like the Milky Way. Having reverently read the Collected Imperial Writings, we have gained some understanding of their broad outlines. The edict announcing his accession at the southern suburban altar issued from the depths of his heart; for the inscription at the imperial mausoleum in Zhongdu, he personally wielded the imperial brush. Upon completion of the great sacrificial rites, he issued an injunction instructing the Central Secretariat; upon appointing chief councilors, he issued a proclamation urging them to achieve meritorious deeds.

Among his records are such works as ‘Yuejiang Tower,’ ‘Teng xinying’ [?], ‘Reflections on the Past,’ and ‘The Western Expedition.’ Among his explanations are such pieces as ‘The Floods and Droughts of Yao and Tang,’ ‘The Campaign against Song,’ ‘The Clearing of the Yellow River,’ and ‘Fine Horses.’ In ‘Sweet Dew’ and ‘Auspicious Snow,’ the arguments are grand …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
偉天時聖學策問淵源至於神龍丹芝
嘉瓜之有贊萌賢啓忠省碩之有文鶯
囀皇州四瀆潦水諸賦何麗則也孝慈
昭鑒建言格式等序何明正也其他辯
誌題跋書傳詩歌連篇累牘一揮而成
宏詞奥義未易窺測是豈文儒墨士拘
拘于尋章摘句而巧爲駢四儷六耶抑
聖學天成不煩繩削而筆端造化自露也當時
侍從之臣有編錄以成帙者有作序以
贊頌者又有固請鋟梓以貽後者豈無
見歟
===
聖子
神孫是訓是則迨我
皇上踐祚以來間嘗游心翰墨寫懷有詩以賜
臣工會典有序以垂世範因文以考德
脩德以立政法
祖圖治之心固在也諸士子樂育
聖化欽仰
punctuated:
偉。天時、聖學，策問淵源。至於神龍、丹芝、嘉瓜之有贊，萌賢、啓忠、省碩之有文，鶯囀皇州、四瀆、潦水諸賦，何麗則也！孝慈昭鑒、建言格式等序，何明正也！其他辯、誌、題跋、書傳、詩歌，連篇累牘，一揮而成。宏詞奥義，未易窺測。是豈文儒墨士拘拘于尋章摘句，而巧爲駢四儷六耶？抑聖學天成，不煩繩削，而筆端造化自露也。當時侍從之臣，有編錄以成帙者，有作序以贊頌者，又有固請鋟梓以貽後者，豈無見歟？
聖子神孫，是訓是則。迨我皇上踐祚以來，間嘗游心翰墨，寫懷有詩以賜臣工，會典有序以垂世範。因文以考德，脩德以立政，法祖圖治之心固在也。諸士子樂育聖化，欽仰
translation_en:
…majestic. His policy questions on the Seasons of Heaven and Sagely Learning reach to the very sources of their subjects. As for his encomia on the Divine Dragon, Cinnabar Fungus, and Auspicious Melon; his compositions on Encouraging the Worthy [?], Inspiring Loyalty, and Examining the Eminent [?]; and his rhapsodies, Orioles Singing in the Imperial Capital, the Four Waterways, and Floodwaters—how beautiful and exemplary they are! How lucid and upright are his prefaces to the Illustrious Mirror of Filial Piety and Parental Kindness, the Forms for Presenting Proposals, and other works! His other disputations, commemorative records, inscriptions and postscripts, letters and biographies, poems and songs fill page upon page, all completed at a sweep of the brush. Their grand language and profound meanings are not easily fathomed. Could these possibly be the work of a literary scholar narrowly occupied with picking out passages and phrases, cleverly fashioning parallel clauses of four and six characters? Rather, his sagely learning is Heaven-given: without the trouble of correction and trimming, creative transformation reveals itself naturally at the tip of his brush. Among his attendant officials at the time, some compiled and recorded these writings in volumes, some wrote prefaces in praise of them, and others repeatedly petitioned to have them carved on printing blocks for posterity. Surely they had grounds for doing so?
His sagely sons and divine grandsons took these as their instruction and model. Since Our Emperor ascended the throne, he has from time to time turned his thoughts to writing. He has expressed his feelings in poems bestowed upon his officials and written a preface to the Collected Statutes to transmit a model to succeeding ages. Through his writings one may examine his virtue; by cultivating virtue he establishes his government. His resolve to emulate his ancestors and seek good governance is assuredly manifest therein. You candidates have been happily nurtured under his sagely transforming influence and reverently admire…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖製蓋有年矣其敬陳之毋忽
問我
國家一統之盛度越前代多矣洪惟
太祖高皇帝創業於前
太宗文皇帝繼統於後溥海內外罔不歸心四
夷之遠亦皆向化若初為箕子之國其
主表賀即位而有金印誥命之頒古為
肅慎之地其主悉境歸附而有都司衛
所之建有遣使朝貢累受冊封者有國
===
分為三朝貢不絕者有詔至京受職置
五衛門建官賜印者有率所部男婦五
百人來歸詔賜印誥者有為西戎部落
通貢方物者有為韃靼別部貢獻弓刀
者有封為忠順王者有號為火州城者
有遣員外郎陳誠等出使其國者有遣
滿剌哈非思等來貢駝馬者有遣使賜
以織金文綺者有遣使來貢玉璞等物
者有率先歸附仍賜王印者有朝貢不
punctuated:
聖製蓋有年矣，其敬陳之，毋忽。
問：我國家一統之盛，度越前代多矣。洪惟太祖高皇帝創業於前，太宗文皇帝繼統於後，溥海內外罔不歸心，四夷之遠亦皆向化。若初為箕子之國，其主表賀即位，而有金印誥命之頒；古為肅慎之地，其主悉境歸附，而有都司衛所之建；有遣使朝貢、累受冊封者；有國分為三、朝貢不絕者；有詔至京受職、置五衛門、建官賜印者；有率所部男婦五百人來歸、詔賜印誥者；有為西戎部落、通貢方物者；有為韃靼別部、貢獻弓刀者；有封為忠順王者；有號為火州城者；有遣員外郎陳誠等出使其國者；有遣滿剌哈非思等來貢駝馬者；有遣使賜以織金文綺者；有遣使來貢玉璞等物者；有率先歸附、仍賜王印者；有朝貢不
translation_en:
…the imperial compositions for many years now. Respectfully set forth your account of them, without negligence.
Question: The splendor of our dynasty’s unified rule far surpasses that of previous ages. We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao founded the enterprise, and Emperor Taizong Wen subsequently succeeded to the throne. Throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, none failed to turn their allegiance toward us; even the distant peoples of the four quarters all turned toward our civilizing influence. There was the country that was originally Jizi’s domain: its ruler submitted a memorial congratulating the emperor on his accession and received a gold seal and an imperial patent. There was the land anciently occupied by the Sushen: its ruler submitted with his entire territory, and Regional Military Commissions, guards, and battalions were established there. Some dispatched envoys to present tribute at court and repeatedly received formal investiture. There was a country divided into three whose tribute missions continued without interruption. Some were summoned by imperial decree to the capital to receive office; five guards were established [?], officials appointed, and seals bestowed. One led five hundred men and women under his authority to submit and was granted a seal and patent by imperial decree. Some were tribes of the western Rong who presented tribute of local products. Some were separate branches of the Dada who offered bows and sabers as tribute. One was invested as King of Loyalty and Obedience. One was known as the city of Huozhou. To one country, Vice Director Chen Cheng and others were dispatched as envoys. One sent Manla Hafeisi and others to offer camels and horses as tribute. To some, envoys were sent bearing gifts of patterned silks woven with gold. Some sent envoys to offer unworked jade and other objects as tribute. One took the lead in submitting and was also granted a royal seal. Some presented tribute at court without…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
絶請命兩封者有詔賜大統曆列女傳
者有納元所授宣勅二道者有自率其
妻子來朝而卒謚恭順者有各率其妻
子來朝而幷貢方物者有奉金字表幷
獻其土地圖者有遣其臣來貢麒麟等
物者合四夷而納欵萃萬姓之歸心與
圖之廣極天窮地較之北方無燕雲中
世有金元者蓋萬萬不侔矣凡此皆我
祖宗柔遠之仁覆幬無外御夷之道備悉不遺
不偶然也其事昉於何年其詳載於何
典方今
聖明在上四夷嚮風統馭之方安在韋悉心以
對
===
問心爲人一身之主宰萬殊之宗會也心
之說古人嘗言之矣曰道心曰人心曰
良心曰本心曰天地之心曰赤子之心
又有所謂欲心私心者矣然則心果有
不同與而又有以天君言者有以嚴師
punctuated:
絶，請命兩封者；有詔賜大統曆、列女傳者；有納元所授宣勅二道者；有自率其妻子來朝而卒，謚恭順者；有各率其妻子來朝而幷貢方物者；有奉金字表幷獻其土地圖者；有遣其臣來貢麒麟等物者。合四夷而納欵，萃萬姓之歸心，與圖之廣極天窮地，較之北方無燕雲、中世有金元者，蓋萬萬不侔矣。凡此皆我祖宗柔遠之仁，覆幬無外，御夷之道備悉不遺，不偶然也。其事昉於何年？其詳載於何典？方今聖明在上，四夷嚮風，統馭之方安在？韋悉心以對。

問：心爲人一身之主宰，萬殊之宗會也。心之說，古人嘗言之矣：曰道心，曰人心，曰良心，曰本心，曰天地之心，曰赤子之心，又有所謂欲心、私心者矣。然則心果有不同與？而又有以天君言者，有以嚴師
translation_en:
…without interruption, requesting imperial authorization for two investitures; there were those granted by imperial decree the Great Concordance Calendar and the Biographies of Exemplary Women; those who surrendered two patents bestowed by the Yuan; one who personally brought his wife and children to court and, upon his death, received the posthumous name Gongshun; those who each brought their wives and children to court and also presented local products as tribute; those who submitted memorials in gold lettering and presented maps of their territories; and those who sent their ministers to offer qilin and other things as tribute. All the peoples of the four quarters submitted in allegiance, and the hearts of the myriad families converged in loyalty. The breadth of the realm [?] reached the limits of heaven and earth. Compared with those who lacked Yan and Yun in the north, and in whose intervening ages there were the Jin and Yuan [?], the difference was immeasurable. All this arose from our imperial ancestors’ benevolence in cherishing distant peoples: their sheltering care excluded none, and their methods of governing foreign peoples were comprehensive, omitting nothing. These achievements were no accident. In what years did these events begin? In what authoritative records are their details recorded? Now that our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above and the peoples of the four quarters turn toward his influence, wherein lies the proper method of governing them? Apply your whole mind in replying [?].

Question: The heart-mind is the ruler of a person’s entire being and the central meeting point of all diverse things. The ancients have spoken of the heart-mind: they called it the mind of the Way, the human mind, the good mind, the original mind, the mind of Heaven and Earth, and the mind of an infant. There are also what are called the desiring mind and the selfish mind. Does this mean that there truly are different heart-minds? Moreover, some speak of it as the Heavenly Lord, and some as a stern teacher…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
言者有以主帥言者有以靈臺言者有同
其爲名之多端也治心之說古人嘗言
之矣曰盡心曰存心曰正心曰養心曰
以此洗心曰以禮制心又有所謂委心
無心者矣然則功亦有殊致與而又有
以靜坐言者有以涵養言者有以克念
言者有以主敬言者何其爲訓之紛紛
也既曰人心必有所止矣而又曰人心
不得有所繫既曰心要在腔子裏矣而
===
又曰未嘗有在亦無不在玩物則喪志
矣何取乎博奕之賢令色則鮮仁矣何
貴乎其儀之一或山木以喻其養或朝
訟以示其意或曰心欲大或又曰心欲
小豈皆於經有見與或曰有主則實或
又曰有主則虛豈皆於理無背與諸士
子積學有待他日經綸事業固皆自心
上起也必有一定之說矣慎毋徒以心
齋坐忘爲對
punctuated: 言者，有以主帥言者，有以靈臺言者，有同其爲名之多端也。治心之說，古人嘗言之矣：曰盡心，曰存心，曰正心，曰養心，曰以此洗心，曰以禮制心，又有所謂委心、無心者矣。然則功亦有殊致與？而又有以靜坐言者，有以涵養言者，有以克念言者，有以主敬言者，何其爲訓之紛紛也！既曰人心必有所止矣，而又曰人心不得有所繫；既曰心要在腔子裏矣，而又曰未嘗有在，亦無不在。玩物則喪志矣，何取乎博奕之賢？令色則鮮仁矣，何貴乎其儀之一？或山木以喻其養，或朝訟以示其意，或曰心欲大，或又曰心欲小，豈皆於經有見與？或曰有主則實，或又曰有主則虛，豈皆於理無背與？諸士子積學有待，他日經綸事業，固皆自心上起也，必有一定之說矣。慎毋徒以心齋、坐忘爲對！
translation_en:
…some speak of it as a stern teacher, some as a commander, and some as the spirit terrace. How numerous its designations are! [The wording 有同 is doubtful.] The ancients also spoke of governing the mind: fully realizing the mind, preserving the mind, rectifying the mind, nourishing the mind, “cleansing the mind by this,” and regulating the mind through ritual. There are also what are called “letting the mind go” and “having no mind.” Does the work of cultivation, then, likewise lead to different ends? Further, some speak of quiet sitting, some of nurturing, some of mastering one’s thoughts, and some of maintaining reverent attentiveness. How diverse these teachings are!

It is said that the human mind must have a place at which to rest, yet also that it must not be attached to anything. It is said that the mind must remain within the bodily frame, yet also that it has never occupied any particular place and is nowhere absent. If toying with things destroys one’s resolve, why commend playing board games as the better course? If an ingratiating expression seldom accompanies benevolence, why esteem consistency of demeanor? Some use the trees of a mountain to illustrate the mind’s nurture; others use attendance at court and the pursuit of lawsuits to show its inclinations [?]. Some say the mind should be expansive; others say it should be small and cautious. Do all these statements reflect insights into the Classics? Some say that having a master within makes the mind full; others say that having a master within makes it empty. Are all these statements consistent with principle?

You examination candidates have accumulated learning in readiness for service. Your future undertakings in ordering and governing the realm will assuredly all begin in the mind. You must therefore have a settled explanation. Take care not to answer merely in terms of “fasting of the mind” and “sitting in forgetfulness”!

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
問讀書而尚友古之人亦當論其世也其
心其事不無可言若事君結憤而六月
飛霜事親投誠而三冬出笋吹玉律而
寒谷發春陽之氣唱迴風而夏景變秋
殺之天因解牛而悟養生之理見舞劒
而得草書之法覩石壇而探天地升降
之理指湯瓶而識陰陽消長之機有弈
丸而解楚王之難者有戲偶而脫漢帝
之圍者有秉忠誠而蛟鱷逃形者有守
===
正直而鬼神破膽者有搠虱而談當世
之務者有裸體而輕當世之人者恤緯
憂公與食芹思君者何如蹊田奪牛與
覆羹逐婦者何類邪不干正古有以正
止邪如馬少保狄梁公之輩者誰與妖
不勝德古有以德勝妖如魏元忠韋叔
堅之徒者誰與寧相賀弄璋而寫璋爲
麞學士書露布而曳布爲布何其闇也
老瞞悟絶妙好辭之題晉公解獨眠孤
punctuated: 問：讀書而尚友古之人，亦當論其世也。其心其事，不無可言。若事君結憤而六月飛霜，事親投誠而三冬出笋，吹玉律而寒谷發春陽之氣，唱迴風而夏景變秋殺之天，因解牛而悟養生之理，見舞劒而得草書之法，覩石壇而探天地升降之理，指湯瓶而識陰陽消長之機，有弈丸而解楚王之難者，有戲偶而脫漢帝之圍者，有秉忠誠而蛟鱷逃形者，有守正直而鬼神破膽者，有搠虱而談當世之務者，有裸體而輕當世之人者。恤緯憂公與食芹思君者何如？蹊田奪牛與覆羹逐婦者何類？邪不干正，古有以正止邪，如馬少保、狄梁公之輩者，誰與？妖不勝德，古有以德勝妖，如魏元忠、韋叔堅之徒者，誰與？寧相賀弄璋而寫璋爲麞，學士書露布而曳布爲布，何其闇也！老瞞悟絶妙好辭之題，晉公解獨眠孤
translation_en:
Question: When reading books and seeking friendship with the ancients, one should also consider the age in which they lived. Their intentions and deeds offer much to discuss. Consider those whose pent-up indignation in serving their ruler brought falling frost in the sixth month; whose wholehearted sincerity in serving their parents brought forth bamboo shoots in deepest winter; whose blowing on jade pitch pipes brought the warmth of spring sunshine to a cold valley; and whose singing of “Returning Wind” transformed a summer day into the killing weather of autumn. Consider understanding the principles of nourishing life through cutting up an ox; acquiring the technique of cursive calligraphy by watching a sword dance; investigating the principles of the ascent and descent of Heaven and Earth by observing a stone altar; and discerning the workings of the waxing and waning of yin and yang by pointing to a vessel of hot water.

There were those who relieved the king of Chu’s predicament by juggling balls [?], who freed the Han emperor from encirclement by means of a puppet performance, whose steadfast loyalty and sincerity made water dragons and crocodiles disappear, and whose adherence to uprightness terrified ghosts and spirits. There were those who picked lice [?] while discussing the affairs of their day, and those who went naked to express contempt for their contemporaries. What should we make of those who worried about the weft yet were concerned for their lord, or who ate celery and thought of their ruler? To what category belong those who seized an ox for trampling a field, or expelled a wife for spilling soup?

The perverse cannot prevail against the upright. Among the ancients, who checked perversity through uprightness, as did Junior Guardian Ma and Di, Duke of Liang? The uncanny cannot overcome virtue. Among the ancients, who overcame uncanny manifestations through virtue, as did Wei Yuanzhong and Wei Shujian?

Chancellor Ning [?], in congratulating someone on the birth of a son—the occasion of “playing with a jade tablet”—wrote zhang 璋, “jade tablet,” as zhang 麞, “water deer”; an Academician, in writing a public proclamation, “dragged bu 布 into bu 布” [?]. How obtuse they were! Old Man Man understood the inscription’s hidden meaning, “a superbly ingenious and beautiful expression,” and the Duke of Jin deciphered the characters “sleeping alone in a solitary …”

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
館之字何其慧也雖覽謬呼金根妄改
非智者不能辨之越景絶塵昂霄聳壑
惟國士足以當之凡此皆具載方策可
攷也其間物理之有無人品之高下吾
心之取舍繫於此焉可定矣諸士子能
詳辨而深究之亦格物致知之一端也
幸毋曰夫我則不暇
問識時務者在俊傑爲
國計者當安民當入謂保民如保赤子〔不過〕
===
爲之就利避害而已山東時事利害之
所當興除者多矣姑舉其重且急者與
諸士子商之夫黄河之害自古已然地
平天成禹功盛矣由漢以來其役不常
有建治河之三策者有議治河之三法
者歷代所行果有得於是乎往歲河決
安平
朝廷遣内外大臣董其工役合數省之財力
而河始安流頃因黄陵岡之故埽被衝
punctuated:
館之字，何其慧也！雖覽謬呼，金根妄改，非智者不能辨之。越景絶塵，昂霄聳壑，惟國士足以當之。凡此皆具載方策，可攷也。其間物理之有無、人品之高下，吾心之取舍繫於此焉，可定矣。諸士子能詳辨而深究之，亦格物致知之一端也。幸毋曰：「夫我則不暇。」

問：識時務者在俊傑，爲國計者當安民。當入謂保民如保赤子，〔不過〕爲之就利避害而已。山東時事，利害之所當興除者多矣，姑舉其重且急者，與諸士子商之。夫黄河之害，自古已然。地平天成，禹功盛矣。由漢以來，其役不常。有建治河之三策者，有議治河之三法者，歷代所行，果有得於是乎？往歲河決安平，朝廷遣内外大臣董其工役，合數省之財力，而河始安流。頃因黄陵岡之故埽被衝
translation_en:
…the characters for “inn”—how perceptive he was! The mistaken pronunciation of “雖覽” [?] and the arbitrary alteration of “golden wheel hubs”: only the discerning can distinguish such errors. “Outstripping shadows and leaving the dust behind,” “towering into the heavens and rising above ravines”—only outstanding men of the realm merit such descriptions. All these matters are fully recorded in the written sources and can be examined. Whether the principles attributed to things actually exist, and whether people’s character is lofty or base, can thus be determined; upon this depend the choices our minds make to accept or reject. If you candidates can distinguish these matters carefully and investigate them deeply, this too is one aspect of investigating things and extending knowledge. Pray do not say, “I have no time for this.”

Question: Those who understand the needs of the times are men of outstanding talent; those who plan for the state should bring peace to the people. It has been said [?] that protecting the people is like protecting a newborn infant: 〔it amounts to no more than〕 securing benefits for them and averting harm. Among Shandong’s present affairs, there are many benefits that ought to be promoted and harms that ought to be eliminated. Let us select the weightiest and most urgent for discussion with you candidates. The harm caused by the Yellow River has existed since antiquity. The land was brought into order and Heaven’s work accomplished: great indeed were Yu’s achievements! Since the Han, the works undertaken on the river have varied. Some proposed three strategies for regulating the river; others discussed three methods of regulating it. Did the measures implemented under successive dynasties truly derive any benefit from these proposals? In a previous year, the river breached its banks at Anping. The imperial court dispatched high officials from within and outside the capital to supervise the works. Only after the financial and material resources of several provinces had been combined did the river begin to flow safely. Recently, because the old brushwood revetment at Huanglinggang was battered by the current…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
河臺寺之新堤就鬣恐前日之患復作
也特
勑大臣以總理添設府佐以專治復諭各省撫
巡以協謀共濟焉所以禦災捍患者至
矣然古之害在民今之害在運道勢尤
有不可忽者不知若何行之可以一勞
永逸邪盜賊之害自古必有明刑弼教
皐陶兼之自秦而後其方不一有言弭
盜之四事者有論平盜之二弊者歷代
===
所行果有鑒於是乎近年盜起山東
朝廷命內外大臣提督機務合京邊之人馬
而盜始伏誅特以民兵之脆弱莫支民
生之憔悴已極恐前日之徒復騁也添
設兵備之官屢舉賑恤之典又留大將
領邊兵以鎮守調發焉所以防微杜漸
者悉矣然古之戍在邊今則移戍內地
勢固有不能久者不知若何處之可以
有備無患邪此固當道者急於欲聞而
punctuated:
河臺寺之新堤就鬣，恐前日之患復作也。特勑大臣以總理，添設府佐以專治，復諭各省撫巡以協謀共濟焉，所以禦災捍患者至矣。然古之害在民，今之害在運道，勢尤有不可忽者。不知若何行之，可以一勞永逸邪？

盜賊之害，自古必有。明刑弼教，皐陶兼之。自秦而後，其方不一，有言弭盜之四事者，有論平盜之二弊者，歷代所行，果有鑒於是乎？近年盜起山東，朝廷命內外大臣提督機務，合京邊之人馬，而盜始伏誅。特以民兵之脆弱莫支，民生之憔悴已極，恐前日之徒復騁也，添設兵備之官，屢舉賑恤之典，又留大將領邊兵以鎮守調發焉，所以防微杜漸者悉矣。然古之戍在邊，今則移戍內地，勢固有不能久者。不知若何處之，可以有備無患邪？此固當道者急於欲聞而
translation_en:
…the new dike at Hetai Temple has become compromised [?], raising fears that the former calamity may recur. An imperial order specifically charged high officials with overall management, additional assistant prefects were appointed to take special responsibility for the work, and the grand coordinators and regional inspectors of the various provinces were further instructed to plan jointly and cooperate in addressing the difficulty. Measures to ward off disaster and avert harm have thus been carried to the utmost. Yet in antiquity the harm fell upon the people; today it threatens the grain-transport route, making the situation especially impossible to neglect. What measures, then, could secure lasting relief through a single effort?

The scourge of banditry has existed since antiquity. Gao Yao combined the clarification of punishments with the support of moral instruction. Since the Qin dynasty, however, approaches have varied. Some have spoken of four measures for suppressing banditry; others have discussed two failings in its suppression. Have the measures adopted by successive dynasties truly drawn lessons from these? In recent years bandits arose in Shandong. The court ordered high officials from the central and regional administrations to direct military affairs, combining troops and horses from the capital and the frontiers; only then were the bandits brought to justice. Yet the militia were too weak to hold out, and the people’s livelihoods had been reduced to utter destitution, prompting fears that the former bands might again run rampant. Additional military defense officials were therefore appointed, relief measures were repeatedly undertaken, and senior commanders were retained with frontier troops under their command for garrison duty and deployment. Measures to forestall trouble at its first signs and prevent its growth have thus been exhaustive. Yet in antiquity garrisons were stationed on the frontiers; now they have been transferred into the interior, a situation that surely cannot be sustained indefinitely. How, then, should this be managed so that preparedness may avert calamity? This is indeed what those in authority urgently wish to hear, and …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text: 議行者諸士子其試陳之
punctuated: 議行者。諸士子其試陳之。
translation_en: …to deliberate upon and put into effect. Let the candidates attempt to set forth their views on this.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名陳文昭　濮州學生　詩
第二名胡鏜　濟南府學生　禮記

第六名李錫　臨邑縣學生　詩
第七名靳廷寶　濟南府學生　易

第八名劉隅　東阿縣學增廣生　詩

punctuated:
中式舉人七十五名。

第二名胡鏜，濟南府學生，禮記。
第三名張相，臨清州學生，易。
第四名桑溥，濮州學生，春秋。
第五名于思睿，青城縣學生，書。
第六名李錫，臨邑縣學生，詩。
第七名靳廷寶，濟南府學生，易。
第八名劉隅，東阿縣學增廣生，詩。
第九名馬經，泰安州學生，書。
第十名丁忠，霑化縣學生，易。

translation_en:
Seventy-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Chen Wenzhao, a student of the Puzhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Second: Hu Tang, a student of the Jinan Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.
Third: Zhang Xiang, a student of the Linqing Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Fourth: Sang Pu, a student of the Puzhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Fifth: Yu Sirui, a student of the Qingcheng County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Sixth: Li Xi, a student of the Linyi County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Seventh: Jin Tingbao, a student of the Jinan Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Eighth: Liu Yu, an added-quota student of the Dong'e County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
古者言之不出恥躬之不逮也
桑溥
同考試官學正魏　批〔詞以理發而且莊重嚴密令人咀嚼雋永非嘗用力於體驗之功者不能〕
用是錄出以式多士
考試官訓導吳　批〔言之不出朱傳甚明白作者多主范氏不易之註用戾本旨是篇能獨得〕
之宜錄以警世之多言者
===
考試官教諭徐　批〔論語義是如此作〕
聖人論古人之謹於言必原其欲謹之心也蓋
行不及言可恥甚矣古人所以欲謹其言者顧
不為是也哉吾夫子警世立教之意如此蓋謂
言行君子之樞機不可不慎也吾嘗觀諸古人
矣是故出乎身而加乎民不能以無言也乃口
焉若訥遲回於念慮之間而心聲之所露由乎
中而應乎外不能以不言也乃藐焉若愚慎密
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「古者言之不出，恥躬之不逮也。」
桑溥

同考試官學正魏，批〔詞以理發，而且莊重嚴密，令人咀嚼雋永，非嘗用力於體驗之功者不能〕用是錄出，以式多士。
考試官訓導吳，批〔言之不出，朱傳甚明白。作者多主范氏不易之註，用戾本旨。是篇能獨得〕之，宜錄以警世之多言者。
考試官教諭徐，批〔論語義是如此作〕

聖人論古人之謹於言，必原其欲謹之心也。蓋行不及言，可恥甚矣。古人所以欲謹其言者，顧不為是也哉？吾夫子警世立教之意如此。蓋謂言行，君子之樞機，不可不慎也。吾嘗觀諸古人矣。是故出乎身而加乎民，不能以無言也，乃口焉若訥，遲回於念慮之間，而心聲之所露；由乎中而應乎外，不能以不言也，乃藐焉若愚，慎密
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The ancients did not readily speak, for they were ashamed lest their conduct fall short of their words.”
Sang Pu

Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “The language develops from principle and is dignified, rigorous, and closely reasoned, leaving a rich savor for the reader to ponder. Only someone who has devoted effort to understanding through personal experience could achieve this. Accordingly, it is selected for inclusion as a model for the candidates.”

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Zhu Xi’s commentary is very clear on ‘did not readily speak.’ Writers mostly rely on Master Fan’s gloss concerning ‘not speaking lightly,’ thereby departing from the original meaning. This essay alone succeeds in grasping it and should be included to admonish those in the world who speak too much.”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “This is how an essay on the meaning of the Analects should be written.”

When the Sage discusses the ancients’ caution in speech, he necessarily traces it to the intention that made them wish to be cautious. For it is deeply shameful when conduct falls short of words. Was this not precisely why the ancients wished to be cautious in speaking? Such was our Master’s purpose in admonishing the world and establishing his teaching. His meaning was that words and deeds are the pivotal mechanisms of the gentleman’s conduct and must be treated with care. I have examined this among the ancients.

Thus, when something proceeds from oneself and affects the people, one cannot dispense with words. Yet their mouths seemed slow to speak; they lingered in thought and reflection, and the expression of the mind’s voice [?]. When something arises within and responds to what is outside, one cannot remain silent. Yet they appeared as though simple-minded, cautious and meticulous …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
於擬議之頃而口說之不騰理有所聞宜其
言矣則專靜自處括坤之囊而不出其言似
不足焉事有所知宜其言矣則沉默自持含
姤之章而不吐有若不能言焉若此者何爲
哉蓋言貴乎行也身之所履一或不逮其口
之所言適以速空言無當之累恥莫加焉行
貴踐言也體之厥躬一或不副其言之所出
祇以召尚口乃窮之譏愧孰甚焉忸怩之念
展轉於行不顧言之前雖欲言而自不輕也
===
羞愧之心感切於言不顧行之始雖欲言而
自不放也夫古人之不出其言慮力行之不
及甚言如此則言行之相顧可知矣胡今人
之不然哉大抵人莫愚於大言之不慚莫貴
於力行之能篤蓋言之非艱而行之惟艱也
試觀子如愚而造卓爾之地宰予能言而來
觀行之警言行之不可忽也如此後之有志
於學者可不養辯於訥以求允蹈其實而立
造道成德之基也哉
punctuated:
於擬議之頃，而口說之不騰。理有所聞，宜其言矣，則專靜自處，括坤之囊而不出，其言似不足焉；事有所知，宜其言矣，則沉默自持，含姤之章而不吐，有若不能言焉。若此者何爲哉？蓋言貴乎行也，身之所履，一或不逮其口之所言，適以速空言無當之累，恥莫加焉。行貴踐言也，體之厥躬，一或不副其言之所出，祇以召尚口乃窮之譏，愧孰甚焉？忸怩之念，展轉於行不顧言之前，雖欲言而自不輕也；羞愧之心，感切於言不顧行之始，雖欲言而自不放也。

夫古人之不出其言，慮力行之不及，甚言如此，則言行之相顧可知矣。胡今人之不然哉？大抵人莫愚於大言之不慚，莫貴於力行之能篤，蓋言之非艱，而行之惟艱也。試觀子如愚而造卓爾之地，宰予能言而來觀行之警，言行之不可忽也如此。後之有志於學者，可不養辯於訥，以求允蹈其實，而立造道成德之基也哉？
translation_en:
…in the moment of deliberation, so that words do not rush forth from their mouths. When they have heard some principle and might fittingly speak, they remain composed and still, tying shut the sack of Kun, the Receptive, and letting nothing out, as though their words were inadequate. When they understand some affair and might fittingly speak, they maintain their silence, keeping their brilliance within, as in Gou, Coming to Meet, and giving it no utterance, as though unable to speak. Why do they act this way? Because speech is valued for its realization in conduct. If what one actually does falls at all short of what one says, this merely brings upon one the burden of empty words without substance: no disgrace could be greater. Conduct is valued for putting words into practice. If one’s personal performance fails at all to match one’s utterances, this merely invites the reproach that esteeming talk leads to an impasse: what shame could be greater? Thoughts of embarrassment turn over in their minds before their conduct can fail to accord with their words; though they wish to speak, they naturally refrain from speaking lightly. A sense of shame touches them deeply at the first prospect of words heedless of conduct; though they wish to speak, they naturally restrain themselves.

The ancients withheld their words because they feared that their efforts in practice would fall short. When this is stated so emphatically, we can understand how speech and conduct must accord with each other. Why do people today fail to act thus? In general, nothing is more foolish than boasting without shame, and nothing is more worthy than steadfast effort in practice. Speaking is not difficult; acting is what is difficult. Consider how Zi [?; apparently Yan Hui] seemed foolish yet attained an outstanding level, whereas Zai Yu’s eloquence prompted the admonition to observe a person’s conduct. Such is the importance of attending to both speech and conduct. Can later students devoted to learning fail to nurture eloquence through reticence, seeking truly to put its substance into practice, and thereby laying the foundation for attaining the Way and perfecting their virtue?

儀三百威儀三千待其人而後行
李堯元
同考試官教諭李　批〔理致文字難於模擬豈以聖賢故有微意於其間哉說理不謬而措詞〕
史順健見此耳
考試官訓導洪　批〔其人之人且宜分說試將聖賢連讀下去則當是何如人自可知矣是篇詞不煩而〕
意獨至中庸義止如此
===
考試官教諭徐　批〔詞理明暢〕
中庸讚美道之所以大結言行之存乎人夫道
雖大小無所不該此道之所以為大也苟非其
人豈虛行哉中庸二十七章言人道之該盡謂
道固極其大矣然果何以見之是故自夫大者
而言洋洋乎流動充滿無在而無不在物雖有
萬也道有以發育之形者形色者色而咸若其
性生者生化者化而各得其所天雖至高也道
有以峻極之磅礴於穹壽之表浩蕩無垠也猶
punctuated:
洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千，待其人而後行。
李堯元
同考試官教諭李批〔理致文字難於模擬，豈以聖賢故有微意於其間哉？說理不謬而措詞〕史順健，見此耳。
考試官訓導洪批〔其人之人，且宜分說。試將聖賢連讀下去，則當是何如人，自可知矣。是篇詞不煩而〕意獨至，《中庸》義止如此。
考試官教諭徐批〔詞理明暢。〕
《中庸》讚美道之所以大，結言行之存乎人。夫道雖大小無所不該，此道之所以為大也。苟非其人，豈虛行哉？《中庸》二十七章言人道之該盡，謂道固極其大矣，然果何以見之？是故自夫大者而言，洋洋乎流動充滿，無在而無不在。物雖有萬也，道有以發育之：形者形，色者色，而咸若其性；生者生，化者化，而各得其所。天雖至高也，道有以峻極之：磅礴於穹壽之表，浩蕩無垠也，猶
translation_en:
“How vast and flowing! It brings forth and nurtures the myriad things and rises to the height of Heaven. How abundant and great! The three hundred rules of ritual and the three thousand rules of deportment await the right person before they are put into practice.”
Li Yaoyuan
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning and writing are difficult to imitate. Could the reference to sages and worthies imply some subtle distinction here? The exposition of principle is sound, and the phrasing is [annotation ends] fluent and vigorous [?]; that is what we see here.”
Examiner Hong, Assistant Instructor, comments: “For the moment, one should distinguish the kinds of person meant by ‘the right person.’ Try reading onward with ‘sages and worthies’ taken together, and it will become clear what sort of person is meant. This essay is concise in wording, yet [annotation ends] its meaning reaches the heart of the matter. This is precisely the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean.”
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The wording and reasoning are clear and fluent.”
The Doctrine of the Mean praises that which makes the Way great, concluding that its practice depends upon the person. The Way encompasses everything, great and small: this is what makes it great. Without the right person, how could it operate on its own? Chapter twenty-seven of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the all-encompassing character of the human Way. It declares that the Way is indeed supremely great; but how can this actually be seen? Thus, speaking of its greatness, it flows abundantly and fills all things, located nowhere in particular yet present everywhere. Although things number in the myriad, the Way brings them forth and nurtures them: those with form acquire their form, those with color acquire their color, and all accord with their nature; those that live live, those that transform transform, and each finds its proper place. Although Heaven is supremely high, the Way reaches its utmost height: spreading beyond the vault of Heaven [?], it is vast and boundless, yet …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
環於沖漠之中瀰漫莫測也蓋極於至大而無
外焉自夫小者而言優優乎充足有餘無有而
無不有朝覲會同宏綱畢備冠婚喪祭畧則具
存禮儀有三百也何者非斯道之著升降揖遜
升然有倫進退周旋燦然可觀威儀有三千也
何者非斯道之行蓋入於至小而無間焉夫道
固至大而無外矣必俟其人有以極夫大者夫
然後洋洋之盛可以會其全道固至小而無間
矣必待其人有以盡夫細者夫然後優優之懿
===
可以周其用得之於我而亦行於我語大而大
天地可位也萬物可育也所謂發育峻極者始
不為虛位矣否則道其孤矣其何以行之哉自
我而具亦自我而行語小而小其儀不忒也動
容中禮也所謂禮儀威儀者始不為虛器矣否
則道其廢矣尚安望其行哉夫聖道甚大而體
之在人如此然則異道之行可終無其人乎識
之君子尚當知所務云抑合下文而通觀之以
凝乎道惟在於脩德要之不越乎存心致知二
punctuated: 環於沖漠之中，瀰漫莫測也。蓋極於至大而無外焉。自夫小者而言，優優乎充足有餘，無有而無不有。朝覲會同，宏綱畢備；冠婚喪祭，畧則具存。禮儀有三百也，何者非斯道之著？升降揖遜，升然有倫；進退周旋，燦然可觀。威儀有三千也，何者非斯道之行？蓋入於至小而無間焉。夫道固至大而無外矣，必俟其人有以極夫大者，夫然後洋洋之盛可以會其全。道固至小而無間矣，必待其人有以盡夫細者，夫然後優優之懿可以周其用。得之於我，而亦行於我，語大而大，天地可位也，萬物可育也，所謂發育峻極者始不為虛位矣。否則道其孤矣，其何以行之哉？自我而具，亦自我而行，語小而小，其儀不忒也，動容中禮也，所謂禮儀威儀者始不為虛器矣。否則道其廢矣，尚安望其行哉？夫聖道甚大，而體之在人如此，然則異道之行可終無其人乎？識之君子，尚當知所務云。抑合下文而通觀之，以凝乎道，惟在於脩德，要之不越乎存心致知二
translation_en:
… encircles the realm of emptiness and stillness, spreading everywhere beyond all fathoming. Thus it reaches the utmost greatness, with nothing outside it. Speaking of its smallness, it is abundantly sufficient, with more than enough to spare: it has no tangible existence, yet there is nothing in which it does not exist. In court audiences and assemblies of rulers, its grand framework is fully provided; in cappings, marriages, funerals, and sacrifices, its general rules are all present. There are three hundred rules of ceremony: which of them is not a manifestation of this Way? Ascending and descending, bowing and yielding, all proceed in due order [?]; advancing and withdrawing, turning and moving about, all are splendid to behold. There are three thousand rules of deportment: which of them is not an enactment of this Way? Thus it penetrates the utmost minuteness, leaving no interval unfilled.

The Way is indeed supremely great, with nothing outside it; yet it must await the person capable of reaching the full extent of its greatness. Only then can its overflowing abundance be apprehended in its entirety. The Way is indeed supremely minute, leaving no interval unfilled; yet it must await the person capable of exhausting its subtleties. Only then can its abundant excellence be brought fully into operation. It is attained within oneself and also put into practice through oneself. Speak of greatness, and it is great: Heaven and Earth can take their proper places, and the myriad things can be nourished. Only then do what are called its nourishing activity and towering height cease to be empty positions. Otherwise, the Way would stand alone: how could it be put into practice? It is fully present in oneself and likewise enacted through oneself. Speak of smallness, and it is small: one’s deportment does not err, and every movement and expression accords with ritual. Only then do what are called ceremonies and rules of deportment cease to be empty instruments. Otherwise, the Way would fall into disuse: how could one still hope for its practice?

The Way of the sages is exceedingly great, and its embodiment depends upon human beings in this manner. Could the practice of heterodox ways [?], then, ultimately dispense with the requisite person? Gentlemen who understand this should know where to direct their efforts. Yet, reading this together with the passage that follows and considering the whole, bringing the Way to full realization rests solely upon cultivating virtue. In essence, this does not go beyond the two pursuits of preserving the mind and extending knowledge …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
是而已蓋存心則極乎道體之大致知則盡乎
道體之細德無不備而我亦其人矣道其有不
凝乎彼謂不必備德而可以凝道者佛老焉爾
是豈知子思契聖之意哉噫
夫君子所過者化所存者神上下與天地
同流豈曰小補之哉
陳文昭
同考試官教諭季　批〔此題以過化存神與天地同流言王道之大其義精矣而能發其義蘊悉無遺者則未之見真切詳明得於季〕
===
考試官訓導吳　批〔王道□□□□□□□□之可錄〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
大賢論王道同造化之大而與霸功之小也蓋
神化莫大於天地而王道之所以為大者實與
之同焉豈霸功所敢伍哉昔孟子之意謂夫王
霸之民不同蓋其道固不同也夫君子具大而
化之之聖躋聖不可知之神其德則曰皇曰帝
punctuated:
是而已。蓋存心則極乎道體之大，致知則盡乎道體之細，德無不備，而我亦其人矣，道其有不凝乎？彼謂不必備德而可以凝道者，佛老焉爾，是豈知子思契聖之意哉？噫！
夫君子所過者化，所存者神，上下與天地同流，豈曰小補之哉？
陳文昭
同考試官教諭季，批〔此題以過化存神與天地同流言王道之大，其義精矣，而能發其義蘊悉無遺者，則未之見。真切詳明，得於季〕
考試官訓導吳，批〔王道□□□□□□□□之可錄〕
考試官教諭徐，批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
大賢論王道同造化之大，而與霸功之小也。蓋神化莫大於天地，而王道之所以為大者，實與之同焉，豈霸功所敢伍哉？昔孟子之意謂夫王霸之民不同，蓋其道固不同也。夫君子具大而化之之聖，躋聖不可知之神，其德則曰皇曰帝
translation_en:
…these alone. For preserving the mind reaches the full greatness of the substance of the Way, while extending knowledge exhausts its finest details. With no virtue lacking, I too become such a person: how could the Way fail to be firmly established? Those who claim that one can establish the Way without possessing virtue in full are merely followers of Buddhism and Laozi. How could they understand Zisi’s intention in according with the sage? Ah!
“Wherever the gentleman passes, transformation occurs; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. How could one call this a mere minor contribution?”
Chen Wenzhao
Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: “This topic speaks of the greatness of the Kingly Way through transformation wherever the gentleman passes, spiritual influence wherever he abides, and his flowing together with Heaven and Earth. Its meaning is subtle indeed; yet I have not seen anyone able to bring out all its implications without omission. Genuine, precise, detailed, and clear; attained from Ji [?].”
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The Kingly Way [eight illegible characters] merits inclusion [?].”
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “[Twelve illegible characters.]”
The great worthy discusses how the Kingly Way shares the greatness of the creative transformations of nature, and how the achievements of a hegemon are small [?]. For nothing surpasses Heaven and Earth in spiritual transformation, and what makes the Kingly Way great is precisely that it shares in this. How could a hegemon’s achievements presume to rank alongside it? Mencius’s meaning was that the people under a true king and those under a hegemon differ because their ways of governing are fundamentally different. The gentleman possesses the sageliness of one whose greatness brings transformation and ascends to the spirituality of a sage who is beyond comprehension. In virtue, he is called an august sovereign, called an emperor…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
曰王而先後一揆其業則以道以德以功而古
今一轍故其身所經歷之處雖不期其民之化
也而教之所漸被人皆遷善而斂德風聲之所
鼓動俗皆淳龐而熙皞所過有不化乎心所存
主之處雖不必其幾之神也恩深而功不露天
下相忘於帝力何有之鄉恩溥而民不知四海
同歸於無思無為之境所存何其神乎王者之
德業如是而可以易名哉彼乾坤成而庶類
咸若其性天地之化也王者之化舉一世而歘
===
陶之莫化之上下與天地而同運矣夫奚翼陽
嘘陰吸而一元默運其機天地之神也王者之
裨合萬有而鑪錘之其神之上下與天地而並
行矣夫何殊王道之大固如此若夫霸者竊仁
義以愚民雖獲一時之驩虞去淳龐之俗已遠
是不過沾沾之惠以補其罅隙而已視皇帝與
王真珷玞之於美玉也烏能彷彿其萬一哉挾
智力以欺世雖苟目前之功利去熙皞之俗已
遠亦不過小小之恩以塞其滲漏而已視道德
punctuated:
曰王，而先後一揆；其業則以道、以德、以功，而古今一轍。故其身所經歷之處，雖不期其民之化也，而教之所漸被，人皆遷善而斂德；風聲之所鼓動，俗皆淳龐而熙皞。所過有不化乎？心所存主之處，雖不必其幾之神也，恩深而功不露，天下相忘於帝力何有之鄉；恩溥而民不知，四海同歸於無思無為之境。所存何其神乎！

王者之德業如是，而可以易名哉？彼乾坤成，而庶類咸若其性，天地之化也。王者之化，舉一世而歘陶之，莫化之上下，與天地而同運矣，夫奚翼？陽嘘陰吸，而一元默運其機，天地之神也。王者之裨，合萬有而鑪錘之，其神之上下，與天地而並行矣，夫何殊？王道之大固如此。

若夫霸者竊仁義以愚民，雖獲一時之驩虞，去淳龐之俗已遠，是不過沾沾之惠以補其罅隙而已。視皇帝與王，真珷玞之於美玉也，烏能彷彿其萬一哉？挾智力以欺世，雖苟目前之功利，去熙皞之俗已遠，亦不過小小之恩以塞其滲漏而已。視道德
translation_en:
…or called kings, yet those who came before and those who came after followed a single standard. Their achievements rested on the Way, on virtue, or on meritorious deeds, yet antiquity and the present followed the same course. Thus, wherever such a ruler personally passes, even without intending to transform the people, all whom his teaching gradually reaches turn toward goodness and cultivate virtue; wherever the influence of his reputation stirs them, their customs become simple, generous, harmonious, and joyful. Can any place through which he passes remain untransformed? Wherever his mind rests and directs itself, even without seeking spiritual efficacy in its incipient workings, his beneficence is profound while his achievements remain unseen: all under Heaven forget his agency, dwelling in a realm where they ask, “What has the emperor’s power to do with us?” His beneficence extends everywhere, yet the people are unaware of it; all within the Four Seas arrive together at a state without deliberation or deliberate action. How spiritual is the influence of what he holds within!

Such are the virtue and achievements of a true king: could they be given any other name? Heaven and Earth take form, and all kinds of beings follow their own natures: this is the transforming power of Heaven and Earth. The true king’s transforming power suddenly molds an entire age; its transformation above and below [?] moves in concert with Heaven and Earth. How could it differ [?]? Yang exhales and yin inhales, while the primal unity silently sets their workings in motion: this is the spiritual efficacy of Heaven and Earth. The true king’s assistance [?] brings together all that exists and shapes it as in a furnace and under a hammer; his spiritual efficacy above and below proceeds alongside Heaven and Earth. How is it different? Such indeed is the greatness of the Kingly Way.

As for the hegemon, he appropriates benevolence and righteousness to delude the people. Although he wins their pleasure for a time, he remains far removed from customs of simplicity and generosity. This amounts merely to petty favors used to patch his gaps. Compared with the august sovereigns, emperors, and kings, he is truly like a stone resembling jade beside fine jade: how could he approximate even one ten-thousandth of their worth? He relies on cleverness and force to deceive the world. Although he contrives to gain immediate results and advantages, he remains far removed from harmonious and joyful customs. This, too, amounts merely to trifling kindnesses used to plug his leaks. Compared with the Way and virtue…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
與功猶菽粟之於糠粃也安能彷彿其一二哉
是則王道之所以為大此王者之民宜其畢異於
霸者之民也歟抑論之天地惟一誠也故其生
物不測子思曰天地之道可一言而盡也王者
惟一誠也故其神化不測孟子曰以德行仁者
王乃若霸者則假之而已是以功烈如彼其卑
也荀子曰粹而王駁而霸王者固粹矣霸者豈
獨駁云乎哉要之王霸之辨當以孟氏之言為
正後之學者盍亦於誠偽焉觀之
===
易
酒食貞吉以中正也
張相
同考試官教諭楊　批〔此作善體貼需之正意〕
〔且文象明白是用錄出〕
同考試官教授陳　批　酒食象爾不遊假之
以明時方當需不容更有所為之意作者往
往認真講去大舛經旨此作剖析明白而氣
脉豐偉宜冠本房
punctuated:
與功，猶菽粟之於糠粃也，安能彷彿其一二哉？是則王道之所以為大，此王者之民宜其畢異於霸者之民也歟！抑論之，天地惟一誠也，故其生物不測。子思曰：「天地之道，可一言而盡也。」王者惟一誠也，故其神化不測。孟子曰：「以德行仁者王。」乃若霸者，則假之而已，是以功烈如彼其卑也。荀子曰：「粹而王，駁而霸。」王者固粹矣，霸者豈獨駁云乎哉？要之，王霸之辨，當以孟氏之言為正。後之學者，盍亦於誠偽焉觀之？

易
酒食貞吉，以中正也。
張相

同考試官教諭楊　批〔此作善體貼需之正意，〕〔且文象明白，是用錄出。〕

同考試官教授陳　批：酒食象爾，不遊假之，以明時方當需，不容更有所為之意。作者往往認真講去，大舛經旨。此作剖析明白，而氣脉豐偉，宜冠本房。
translation_en:
…and achievement, it is like beans and grain in relation to chaff [?]. How could it resemble even a fraction of them? This, then, is what makes the royal Way great. Surely it is fitting that the people of a true king should differ entirely from those of a hegemon!

To consider the matter further: Heaven and Earth possess sincerity alone, and thus their generation of living things is unfathomable. Zisi said, “The Way of Heaven and Earth can be exhausted in a single word.” A true king possesses sincerity alone, and thus his wondrous transforming influence is unfathomable. Mengzi said, “One who practices benevolence through virtue becomes a true king.” A hegemon, however, merely borrows benevolence; hence his achievements are so lowly. Xunzi said, “Purity leads to kingship; admixture leads to hegemony.” A true king is certainly pure, but can a hegemon be described merely as mixed? Ultimately, in distinguishing kingship from hegemony, Master Meng’s words should be taken as authoritative. Should not later scholars also examine the distinction in terms of sincerity and falsity?

Book of Changes

“Good fortune through perseverance amid wine and food: this is because of centrality and correctness.”

Zhang Xiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔This composition perceptively grasps the proper meaning of the hexagram Waiting (Xu).〕〔Its expression and imagery are also clear; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Professor: Wine and food are merely images. They are only borrowed [?] to explain that, when the time calls for waiting, one cannot undertake any further action. Writers often expound these literally, greatly misconstruing the classic’s purport. This composition analyzes the matter clearly, and its flow and force are abundant and imposing. It deserves first place in this examining room.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導吳　批　講酒食與中正處都不
類他作殆深於易者
考試官教諭徐　批　體認本義最真
聖人舉需爻象占之善而申其備處需之德也
蓋德莫貴於中正也九五居尊而有是德則其
需之正而獲善不亦宜哉周公繫需九五爻辭曰
需于酒食貞吉吾夫子象傳舉而申之意謂天下
有事固不可以不為時方當需亦不可以妄為
九五以陽剛之爻居至尊之位彼其萬幾裁制
===
之餘事固有當需者矣當需而復有所為則非
需也故惟酒食焉以自樂而相安於無事之天
百揆經營之後事固有當待者矣當待而復有
所事則非待也故惟宴享焉以自娛而安處於
無為之地其象如此占者如之誠能貞以自守
而無妄動之非則不急於需而所需有必至之
理正以自待而無多事之擾則不躁於待而所
待有必應之機其吉也何如哉所以然者蓋胃
進每主於柔邪而能需必本於有德九五居上
punctuated:
考試官訓導吳批：講酒食與中正處，都不類他作，殆深於易者。
考試官教諭徐批：體認本義最真。
聖人舉需爻象占之善，而申其備處需之德也。蓋德莫貴於中正也，九五居尊而有是德，則其需之正而獲善，不亦宜哉？周公繫需九五爻辭曰：「需于酒食，貞吉。」吾夫子象傳舉而申之，意謂天下有事，固不可以不為；時方當需，亦不可以妄為。九五以陽剛之爻，居至尊之位，彼其萬幾裁制之餘，事固有當需者矣。當需而復有所為，則非需也，故惟酒食焉以自樂，而相安於無事之天。百揆經營之後，事固有當待者矣。當待而復有所事，則非待也，故惟宴享焉以自娛，而安處於無為之地。其象如此，占者如之。誠能貞以自守，而無妄動之非，則不急於需，而所需有必至之理；正以自待，而無多事之擾，則不躁於待，而所待有必應之機。其吉也何如哉？所以然者，蓋胃進每主於柔邪，而能需必本於有德。九五居上
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: His treatment of food and drink, and of centrality and correctness, is entirely unlike other compositions. He seems to possess a deep understanding of the Book of Changes.
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: His grasp of the original meaning is most accurate.
The sage cites the favorable image and prognostication of the line in Waiting (Xu), and elaborates upon its full possession of the virtue needed to conduct oneself while waiting. For among virtues, none is more precious than centrality and correctness. The nine in the fifth place occupies the honored position and possesses this virtue. Is it not fitting, then, that it waits correctly and obtains a favorable outcome? The Duke of Zhou appended this statement to the nine in the fifth place of Waiting: “Waiting amid food and drink; constancy brings good fortune.” Our Master cites and elaborates upon this in the Commentary on the Images. His meaning is that when there are affairs to be attended to in the world, one certainly cannot leave them undone; yet when the time calls for waiting, one must likewise not act rashly.
The nine in the fifth place, a line of firm yang, occupies the most exalted position. After deciding and directing the myriad affairs of government, there are certainly matters in which one ought to wait. To undertake further action when one ought to wait would be no waiting at all. Thus one simply takes pleasure in food and drink, resting at ease in a world free of affairs requiring action. After managing the hundred duties of government, there are certainly matters that must await their time. To undertake further business when one ought to wait would be no waiting at all. Thus one simply finds enjoyment in feasting, dwelling peacefully in a state requiring no action.
Such is its image, and the one consulting the oracle should follow it. If one can truly remain constant in self-discipline, free of the fault of rash action, one will not be impatient while waiting, and there is a principle by which what one awaits must arrive. If one maintains correctness while awaiting events, free of the disturbance of needless activity, one will not be impetuous while waiting, and circumstances will assuredly bring a response to what one awaits. How auspicious this is! The reason is that rash advancement [?] generally arises from weakness and perversity, whereas the ability to wait must be rooted in the possession of virtue. The nine in the fifth place occupies the upper position…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
得之中其德中也中則無過不及而所以處夫
需者自安貞而能待居陽位之正其德正也正
則無反無側而所以需於事者自貞固而有恒
體坤之靜而無事於宵旰之勤一中正以爲之
持循止艮之歸而不萌夫欲速之念一中正以
爲之運用于事以能需爲善德以中正爲美此
九五所以有酒食之象貞吉之占也歟抑論君
之道時爲而已人君固貴乎察其時以爲張弛
闔闢之機使不當需而需則優游不斷者失之
===
靡當需而不需則好大喜功者失之躁皆非也
然則如之何哉體也而經綸有事體需而宴樂
無爲則動靜以時與易道相爲消息而君人之
道庶乎其盡矣
天一地二天三地四天五地六天七地八
天九地十天數五地數五五位相得而各
有合天數二十有五地數三十凡天地之
數五十有五此所以成變化而行鬼神也
靳廷寶
punctuated:
得之中，其德中也。中則無過不及，而所以處夫需者，自安貞而能待。居陽位之正，其德正也。正則無反無側，而所以需於事者，自貞固而有恒。體坤之靜，而無事於宵旰之勤，一中正以爲之持循；止艮之歸，而不萌夫欲速之念，一中正以爲之運用。于事以能需爲善，德以中正爲美，此九五所以有酒食之象、貞吉之占也歟！抑論君之道，時爲而已。人君固貴乎察其時，以爲張弛闔闢之機。使不當需而需，則優游不斷者失之靡；當需而不需，則好大喜功者失之躁，皆非也。然則如之何哉？體也而經綸有事，體需而宴樂無爲，則動靜以時，與易道相爲消息，而君人之道庶乎其盡矣。
「天一，地二；天三，地四；天五，地六；天七，地八；天九，地十。天數五，地數五，五位相得而各有合。天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數五十有五。此所以成變化而行鬼神也。」
靳廷寶
translation_en:
…attains the central position: its virtue is centrality. Centrality entails neither excess nor deficiency, so in dealing with Waiting one naturally rests in constancy and can await the proper moment. It occupies the correct yang position: its virtue is correctness. Correctness entails neither deviation nor partiality, so in waiting upon affairs one is naturally steadfast and persevering. Embodying the stillness of Kun, one has no need for toil from before dawn until late at night, relying entirely on centrality and correctness to guide one’s conduct. Resting where Gen finds its destination [?], one harbors no desire for haste, relying entirely on centrality and correctness in practical action. In affairs, the ability to wait constitutes goodness; in virtue, centrality and correctness constitute excellence. Is this not why the Nine in the Fifth Place has the image of wine and food and the prognostication of good fortune through constancy?
Yet the ruler’s way consists simply in acting at the proper time. A ruler must above all discern the times, making them the basis for tightening or relaxing, closing or opening. If he waits when he ought not to wait, his leisurely indecision errs toward laxity; if he does not wait when he ought to wait, his taste for grand undertakings and delight in achievements err toward impetuosity. Both are wrong. What, then, should he do? Embodying [an unclear reference], he orders affairs through active engagement; embodying Waiting, he enjoys feasting and remains free from action. Then his activity and stillness accord with the times, waxing and waning together with the Way of the Changes, and the way of ruling others may thereby approach fulfillment.
“Heaven is one, Earth two; Heaven three, Earth four; Heaven five, Earth six; Heaven seven, Earth eight; Heaven nine, Earth ten. Heaven has five numbers, and Earth has five numbers. The five positions accord with one another, and each has its partner. Heaven’s numbers total twenty-five, and Earth’s numbers total thirty. Together, the numbers of Heaven and Earth total fifty-five. Through these, change and transformation are accomplished, and ghosts and spirits are brought into operation.”
Jin Tingbao 靳廷寶

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭楊　批　聖人理數之學起於河圖
而是篇措詞整飭發意明白且於行鬼神之理說者
多以數之生者爲神數之成者爲鬼殊失本旨子獨
得之蓋用心於易而卓有定見者歟
同考試官教授陳　批　此題場中作者雖知圖
位之數變化鬼神之妙亦不免失之繁冗可厭是
卷獨能發揮明爭讀之令人歎服
考試官訓導吳　批　詞不費而理完錄之
考試官教諭徐　批　明潔可玩
===
大傳詳河圖之數而必著其功用之妙也蓋數
必有理也河圖具天地之數則其功用之妙自
有不期然而然者矣大傳詳河圖之數意謂天
數奇地數偶河圖之數亦不過一奇一偶而已
故其位一居下而二居上三居左而四居右五
則以奇而居中是天一也地二也天三地四而
天五焉六居下而七居上八居左而九居右十
則以偶而居中是地六也天七也地八天九而
地十焉分而言之一三五七九其數皆奇非天
punctuated:
同考試官教諭楊批：「聖人理數之學起於河圖，而是篇措詞整飭，發意明白。且於行鬼神之理，說者多以數之生者爲神、數之成者爲鬼，殊失本旨。子獨得之，蓋用心於易而卓有定見者歟？」
同考試官教授陳批：「此題場中作者雖知圖位之數、變化鬼神之妙，亦不免失之繁冗可厭。是卷獨能發揮明爭，讀之令人歎服。」
考試官訓導吳批：「詞不費而理完，錄之。」
考試官教諭徐批：「明潔可玩。」
大傳詳河圖之數，而必著其功用之妙也。蓋數必有理也，河圖具天地之數，則其功用之妙自有不期然而然者矣。大傳詳河圖之數，意謂天數奇，地數偶，河圖之數亦不過一奇一偶而已。故其位，一居下而二居上，三居左而四居右，五則以奇而居中，是天一也，地二也，天三地四而天五焉。六居下而七居上，八居左而九居右，十則以偶而居中，是地六也，天七也，地八天九而地十焉。分而言之，一三五七九，其數皆奇，非天
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The sages’ learning concerning principle and number originates in the River Chart. This essay is orderly in its phrasing and clear in expressing its meaning. Moreover, regarding the principle by which the numbers give operation to ghosts and spirits, interpreters mostly identify the generating numbers with spirits and the completing numbers with ghosts, thereby seriously missing the original meaning. You alone have grasped it. Surely you have devoted yourself to the Book of Changes and attained an outstandingly firm understanding?”

Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Although those writing on this topic in the examination hall understand the numbers in the chart’s positions and the subtleties of transformation and of ghosts and spirits, they nevertheless fall into tiresome prolixity. This paper alone develops the subject clearly [?]; reading it inspires admiration.”

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the principles are fully expressed. Include it in the record.”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Clear and cleanly written; worthy of close appreciation.”\nThe Great Commentary details the numbers of the River Chart and necessarily makes manifest the subtlety of their efficacy. For numbers necessarily embody principle. Since the River Chart comprises the numbers of Heaven and Earth, its subtle efficacy naturally operates without any deliberate intention that it should do so. In detailing the numbers of the River Chart, the Great Commentary means that Heaven’s numbers are odd and Earth’s numbers even: the numbers of the River Chart are simply odd and even numbers. Thus, in their positions, one lies below and two above, three to the left and four to the right, while five, being odd, occupies the center. These are Heaven’s one, Earth’s two, Heaven’s three, Earth’s four, and Heaven’s five. Six lies below and seven above, eight to the left and nine to the right, while ten, being even, occupies the center. These are Earth’s six, Heaven’s seven, Earth’s eight, Heaven’s nine, and Earth’s ten. Considered separately, one, three, five, seven, and nine are all odd numbers; are they not Heaven’s …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
扒五乎二四六八十其數皆偶非地數五乎其
其位之間奇之與偶以類相得而生成之功各
專其一矣一奇一偶以兩相合而生成之妙互
為其用矣積而數之一三五七九天數也計之
則二十有五二四六八十地數也計之則三十
合天之數與地之數則五十有五而天地之數
全矣由是一三五之奇變而生水生木生土也
六八十之偶則化而成之焉二四之偶化而生
火生金也七九之奇則變而成之焉〔變生於奇〕
===
而進退之無定化成於偶而離合〔□無常變化〕
雖妙而是數有以成之矣方奇偶生成之始則
自屈而伸自往而來神於是乎著及奇偶生成
之後則自伸而屈自來而往鬼於是乎行妙於
變化而不見其迹運於生成而莫測其機鬼神
雖幽而是數有以行之矣吁河圖數也而造化
之理寓焉宜聖人關之以示人歟抑論人知河
圖之數而不知其具天地之數人知天地之數
而不知其具造化之理蓋理乘乎氣而數寓乎
punctuated: 扒五乎？二四六八十，其數皆偶，非地數五乎？其其位之間，奇之與偶，以類相得，而生成之功各專其一矣；一奇一偶，以兩相合，而生成之妙互為其用矣。積而數之，一三五七九，天數也，計之則二十有五；二四六八十，地數也，計之則三十。合天之數與地之數，則五十有五，而天地之數全矣。由是，一三五之奇，變而生水、生木、生土也；六八十之偶，則化而成之焉。二四之偶，化而生火、生金也；七九之奇，則變而成之焉。〔變生於奇〕而進退之無定，化成於偶而離合〔□無常變化〕雖妙，而是數有以成之矣。方奇偶生成之始，則自屈而伸，自往而來，神於是乎著；及奇偶生成之後，則自伸而屈，自來而往，鬼於是乎行。妙於變化而不見其迹，運於生成而莫測其機，鬼神雖幽，而是數有以行之矣。吁！河圖，數也，而造化之理寓焉，宜聖人關之以示人歟！抑論人知河圖之數，而不知其具天地之數；人知天地之數，而不知其具造化之理。蓋理乘乎氣，而數寓乎
translation_en:
…are there not five [numbers of Heaven; the opening character is garbled, 扒 [?]]? Two, four, six, eight, and ten are all even: are there not five numbers of Earth? Among their respective positions [the transcription repeats 其 [?]], odd and even find their counterparts by kind, each having its particular role in generation and completion. One odd and one even combine as a pair, and in the marvelous process of generation and completion each serves the other. Adding them together, one, three, five, seven, and nine are Heaven’s numbers, totaling twenty-five; two, four, six, eight, and ten are Earth’s numbers, totaling thirty. Combining Heaven’s numbers with Earth’s gives fifty-five, making the full complement of the numbers of Heaven and Earth. Thus the odd numbers one, three, and five undergo change and generate water, wood, and earth; the even numbers six, eight, and ten undergo transformation and complete them. The even numbers two and four undergo transformation and generate fire and metal; the odd numbers seven and nine undergo change and complete them. 〔Change arises in odd numbers〕, advancing and retreating without fixed pattern; transformation achieves completion in even numbers, whose separation and conjunction 〔□ have no constancy. Change and transformation〕, though wondrous, are accomplished through these numbers.

At the beginning of generation and completion through odd and even, contraction gives way to expansion, and departure to arrival: here the spirits (shen) become manifest. After generation and completion through odd and even, expansion gives way to contraction, and arrival to departure: here the ghosts (gui) operate. Wondrous in change and transformation, they leave no visible trace; active in generation and completion, their workings cannot be fathomed. Though ghosts and spirits are hidden, these numbers enable their operation. Ah! The River Chart (Hetu) consists of numbers, yet the principles of creation reside within it. Surely it was fitting that the sage should disclose it [?; transcribed 關] to instruct others! Yet people know the numbers of the River Chart without knowing that they comprise the numbers of Heaven and Earth; people know the numbers of Heaven and Earth without knowing that they embody the principles of creation. For principle rides upon vital force (qi), and numbers reside in…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
理也苟論理而不本乎氣則涉於虛妄之談論
氣而不本乎理則流於術數之學極理數之奋
闡造化之秘此河圖之所以妙也學者究此而
有得焉則知易之為書豈可以淺近窺耶
書
無教逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日萬幾
于思曆
同考試官教諭陳　批〔兢業圖幾正與教有邦一句意思緊屬此篇文有關鎖而旨復縝〕
〔備可承佳製〕
===
迪錄之
寫笏盡其心必素具忠愛欽矣
同考試官教諭張　批〔皐陶陳謨發言賦之意懇〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔典雅謹嚴書義正宜此作〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔詞意俱到錄出允宜〕
大臣告君身先天下之諸侯當心謹天下之庶
務也甚矣君身所係之重也則夫率下以圖幾
者可不謹哉皐陶陳知人之謨至此若謂天下
之治安難保人心之逸欲易生凡故君身舉動
punctuated:
理也。苟論理而不本乎氣，則涉於虛妄之談；論氣而不本乎理，則流於術數之學。極理數之奋，闡造化之秘，此河圖之所以妙也。學者究此而有得焉，則知易之為書，豈可以淺近窺耶？

書
無教逸欲有邦，兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。
于思曆
同考試官教諭陳　批〔兢業圖幾，正與教有邦一句意思緊屬。此篇文有關鎖，而旨復縝〕〔備，可承佳製。〕
迪錄之。
寫笏盡其心，必素具忠愛欽矣。
同考試官教諭張　批〔皐陶陳謨，發言賦之意懇。〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔典雅謹嚴，書義正宜此作。〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔詞意俱到，錄出允宜。〕

大臣告君，身先天下之諸侯，當心謹天下之庶務也。甚矣，君身所係之重也！則夫率下以圖幾者，可不謹哉？皐陶陳知人之謨，至此若謂天下之治安難保，人心之逸欲易生。凡故君身舉動
translation_en:
…principle. If one discusses principle without grounding it in material force, one enters into empty and unfounded discourse; if one discusses material force without grounding it in principle, one lapses into the study of divinatory techniques. To carry the investigation of principle and number to its utmost [?] and reveal the secrets of creation and transformation: this is what makes the River Chart so wondrous. If students investigate this and attain understanding, they will know: how could the Changes, as a book, be fathomed through shallow understanding?

Book of Documents
“Do not teach the rulers of states ease and desire. Be watchful and cautious: in one day or two days there are ten thousand incipient developments.”
Yu Sili
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔“Being watchful and cautious and attending to incipient developments is closely linked in meaning to the clause about teaching the rulers of states. The composition is closely interconnected, and its purport is also meticulous〕〔and comprehensive. It may be accepted as an excellent composition.”〕
Di records it [?].
Writing on his tablet, he fully expresses his heart; surely he has long possessed loyalty, affection, and reverence [?].
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔“In Gao Yao’s presentation of his counsels, the intention expressed in his words is earnest [?].”〕
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“Classical and elegant, careful and rigorous: an exposition of the meaning of the Documents should indeed be written thus.”〕
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Both expression and meaning are fully realized. It is entirely appropriate to select this for inclusion.”〕

A great minister advises his ruler: as the personal exemplar for all the feudal lords under Heaven, he must attend conscientiously to the manifold affairs of the realm. How weighty are the responsibilities bound up with the ruler’s person! Can one who leads his subordinates in attending to incipient developments fail to exercise care?
