At this point in Gao Yao’s presentation of his counsel on discerning men, he seems to say that peace and good order in the realm are difficult to preserve, while ease and desire readily arise in the human heart. Thus, in all the ruler’s personal actions [?]…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
諸侯之所觀瞻帝當勤以自勵端表儀於穆清
之上無曰崇高可以逸樂為也而啓怠荒之門
朝廷將尚方岳之所視效帝當儉以自處立標
準於臨蒞之餘無曰富貴可以縱欲為也而崇
侈靡之習兢兢焉戒謹於得肆之地肅乎天鑒
之在茲使逸欲之莫乘其隙業業焉危懼於燕
閒之所凜乎上帝之臨汝俾勤儉之恒存諸心
彼自朝至暮特天運之一週由昨而今非星霜
之屢易雖曰一日至淺也而事幾萌於一心者
===
或難或易動以萬計之繁苟或忽焉則其事至
矣是可不兢業以圖難於其易乎雖曰二日至
近也而事幾動於一念者若大若細殆有萬端
之多苟或怠焉則其失隨之又可不戒懼以為
大於其細乎呼率下既端夫一身之則而綱事
又謹於一念之微如此則諸侯無不化而君道
烏有不盡者哉嗟夫治莫盛於有虞君莫聖於
帝舜皐陶陳謨而必以戒逸欲崇兢業為言甚
於篇終又曰敬哉有土豈故憂治世而危明主
punctuated: 諸侯之所觀瞻，帝當勤以自勵，端表儀於穆清之上，無曰崇高可以逸樂為也，而啓怠荒之門。朝廷將尚，方岳之所視效，帝當儉以自處，立標準於臨蒞之餘，無曰富貴可以縱欲為也，而崇侈靡之習。兢兢焉戒謹於得肆之地，肅乎天鑒之在茲，使逸欲之莫乘其隙；業業焉危懼於燕閒之所，凜乎上帝之臨汝，俾勤儉之恒存諸心。彼自朝至暮，特天運之一週；由昨而今，非星霜之屢易。雖曰一日至淺也，而事幾萌於一心者，或難或易，動以萬計之繁，苟或忽焉，則其事至矣，是可不兢業以圖難於其易乎？雖曰二日至近也，而事幾動於一念者，若大若細，殆有萬端之多，苟或怠焉，則其失隨之，又可不戒懼以為大於其細乎？呼！率下既端夫一身之則，而綱事又謹於一念之微，如此則諸侯無不化，而君道烏有不盡者哉？嗟夫！治莫盛於有虞，君莫聖於帝舜。皐陶陳謨，而必以戒逸欲、崇兢業為言，甚於篇終又曰：「敬哉，有土！」豈故憂治世而危明主
translation_en:
…are what the feudal lords look to. You, the emperor, should spur yourself to diligence and set an upright example in the august serenity of your court. Do not say that your exalted station permits idle pleasure, thereby opening the door to indolence and neglect. What the court esteems [?] is what the regional lords look to and emulate. You should conduct yourself frugally and establish a standard in the course of exercising authority. Do not say that wealth and rank permit indulgence of desire, thereby encouraging habits of extravagance. Be watchful and cautious where you have freedom to indulge yourself, solemnly mindful that Heaven's scrutiny is here, so that idleness and desire find no opening. Be apprehensive and fearful even in private leisure, awed that the Lord on High looks down upon you, so that diligence and frugality remain constantly in your heart.

From morning to evening is merely one circuit of Heaven's motion; from yesterday to today is no repeated passage of years. Though a single day is a very short span, the incipient affairs arising within one's heart, whether difficult or easy, readily number in the tens of thousands. If you overlook them, the affairs themselves will be upon you. Can you then fail to remain vigilant and address difficulties while they are still easy? Though two days are a very brief interval, the incipient affairs stirred by a single thought, whether great or small, may have myriad ramifications. If you grow negligent, errors follow. Can you then fail to remain cautious and fearful, attending to great matters while they are still small?

Ah! In leading those below, you have already rectified the example set by your own person; in governing affairs, you are also attentive to the subtle beginnings of a single thought. If so, none of the feudal lords will fail to be transformed. How could the Way of the ruler remain unfulfilled? Alas! No government flourished more than that of Youyu, and no ruler was more sagely than Emperor Shun. Yet when Gao Yao presented his counsels, he insisted on warning against idleness and desire and urging vigilance. Indeed, at the chapter's end he further said: "Be reverent, you who possess the land!" Was he deliberately expressing anxiety over a well-governed age and apprehension for an enlightened ruler…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
邪盖敬者君心之所以主於一而所由以適於
治之要也此心一敬則至明足以察天下之幾
而君人之能事畢矣故曰敬者聖學之所以成
始而成終者也說者謂臯陶之學極純粹而孟
子以道統歸之良有以夫
官不必備惟其人
馬經
同考試官教諭陳　批〔周官一題似易實難詞不〕
〔雜而理亦到僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔題本簡淡作者不無剽〕
〔浮蕪二病而有不然者此篇者可以録矣〕
===
考試官訓導吳　批〔寫出三公在得人意自嘉〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔措詞簡□□□□□白別〕
〔是宜録出〕
聖世之建三公也不嫌於虛位而務在於得人夫
三公之在得人也尚矣使徒備其官而不于其
人焉豈建官之意也哉成王訓迪厥官而首及
於此其意蓋謂三公賦任天下之重當極天下
punctuated:
邪？盖敬者，君心之所以主於一，而所由以適於治之要也。此心一敬，則至明足以察天下之幾，而君人之能事畢矣。故曰：敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。說者謂臯陶之學極純粹，而孟子以道統歸之，良有以夫！

官不必備，惟其人。
馬經

同考試官教諭陳，批〔周官一題，似易實難，詞不〕〔雜而理亦到，僅見此篇。〕
同考試官教諭張，批〔題本簡淡，作者不無剽〕〔浮蕪二病，而有不然者，此篇者可以録矣。〕
考試官訓導吳，批〔寫出三公在得人意，自嘉。〕
考試官教諭徐，批〔措詞簡□□□□□白別〕〔是宜録出。〕

聖世之建三公也，不嫌於虛位，而務在於得人。夫三公之在得人也尚矣，使徒備其官而不于其人焉，豈建官之意也哉？成王訓迪厥官，而首及於此，其意蓋謂三公賦任天下之重，當極天下
translation_en:
…? For reverent attentiveness is what enables the ruler’s mind to remain focused on one thing, and is the essential means by which he advances toward good government. Once this mind is reverently attentive, its utmost clarity suffices to discern the incipient developments of all under Heaven, and all the accomplishments of ruling others are fulfilled. Thus it is said: reverent attentiveness is what brings the learning of sages to completion from beginning to end. Commentators say that Gao Yao’s learning was supremely pure, and Mencius placed him within the transmission of the Way. There is indeed good reason for this!

“Offices need not all be filled; what matters is having the right men.”
By Ma Jing 馬經.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “This topic from ‘The Offices of Zhou’ seems easy but is actually difficult. This is the only essay I have seen whose wording is free of clutter and whose reasoning also reaches the point.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is simple and plain. Writers are not free of the two faults of superficiality and verbosity [?]. Yet there are exceptions: this essay may be selected for inclusion.”

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It brings out the idea that appointing the Three Dukes depends on finding the right men. This is commendable in itself.”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise … [five illegible characters; the following wording is unclear: ‘clear, distinct’ (?)]. This ought to be selected for inclusion.”

In a sage-governed age, when the offices of the Three Dukes are established, there is no objection to leaving positions vacant; the overriding concern is to obtain the right men. That the appointment of the Three Dukes depends on obtaining the right men has long been recognized. If one merely filled their offices without attending to the men appointed [?], how could that accord with the purpose of establishing offices? When King Cheng instructed and guided his officials, he addressed this matter first. His meaning was presumably that the Three Dukes are entrusted with the weighty responsibilities of all under Heaven, and that one must draw upon all under Heaven to the utmost …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之選彼六卿九牧官必欲備也而三公非其
擬倫苟非其人則徒擁虛名而無益於治道
矣百司庶府位不可虛也而三公非其儔匹
不得其人則徒享尊位而無裨於治化矣太
師有人矣而保傅之位或虛可也不必等常
俟以求全保傅有人矣而太師一位或闕亦
可也不必拘定員以求備蓋論道經邦三公
之責也必極其裁成輔相之道者而始不孤
燮理陰陽三公之任也必具夫經綸參贊之
===
才者而後克稱登庸之際必慎選擇於百僚
務求其人以置諸左右否則寧虛其位焉是
非難其官也難其人也簡任之時必廣咨詢
於衆論務求其人以置之密勿否則寧兼其
官焉是非重其選也重其位也夫三公之選
既嚴則在位有人而厥職稱矣有周成一代
之治也宜哉抑考三公之制雖始於周而其
義則仰若前代以爲之也得其人皆足以兼
之孰謂師專導以教訓而不傳之德義保專
punctuated: 之選。彼六卿九牧，官必欲備也，而三公非其擬倫；苟非其人，則徒擁虛名而無益於治道矣。百司庶府，位不可虛也，而三公非其儔匹；不得其人，則徒享尊位而無裨於治化矣。太師有人矣，而保傅之位或虛可也，不必等常俟以求全；保傅有人矣，而太師一位或闕亦可也，不必拘定員以求備。蓋論道經邦，三公之責也，必極其裁成輔相之道者而始不孤；燮理陰陽，三公之任也，必具夫經綸參贊之才者而後克稱。登庸之際，必慎選擇於百僚，務求其人以置諸左右，否則寧虛其位焉。是非難其官也，難其人也。簡任之時，必廣咨詢於衆論，務求其人以置之密勿，否則寧兼其官焉。是非重其選也，重其位也。夫三公之選既嚴，則在位有人而厥職稱矣。有周成一代之治也，宜哉！抑考三公之制，雖始於周，而其義則仰若前代以爲之也。得其人，皆足以兼之。孰謂師專導以教訓而不傳之德義，保專
translation_en:
…the finest selection of men in the realm. The offices of the Six Ministers and the Nine Regional Governors must all be filled, but the Three Dukes cannot be ranked alongside them. If suitable men are lacking, their incumbents merely possess empty titles and contribute nothing to good government. The posts of the many officials and administrative offices cannot be left vacant, but the Three Dukes are not comparable to these. Unless suitable men are found, their incumbents merely enjoy exalted positions without helping to govern and transform the people. If a suitable man serves as Grand Preceptor, the posts of Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor may remain vacant; there is no need to follow customary arrangements [?] merely to complete their number. If suitable men serve as Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor, the single post of Grand Preceptor may likewise remain unfilled; there is no need to insist upon a fixed complement merely to fill every post.

To discourse upon the Way and order the state is the responsibility of the Three Dukes. Only men who fully realize the Way of shaping and assisting can avoid betraying that responsibility. To harmonize yin and yang is their charge. Only men endowed with the ability to order affairs and assist the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth can adequately fulfill it. When promoting men to office, one must choose carefully from among the hundred officials, striving to find suitable men to place at the ruler’s side. Otherwise, it is better to leave the posts vacant. The difficulty lies not in the offices themselves, but in finding the men. When selecting and appointing them, one must consult opinion widely, striving to find suitable men to entrust with confidential deliberations. Otherwise, it is better to have their offices held concurrently. This is not to attach weight merely to their selection, but to honor the importance of their positions.

Once selection of the Three Dukes is rigorous, suitable men occupy the posts and discharge their duties fittingly. How fitting that Zhou achieved the good government of an entire age! Yet, on examining the institution of the Three Dukes, although it began under Zhou, its underlying principles were established in reverent imitation of earlier ages. If suitable men are obtained, each is capable of combining these duties. Who could say that the Preceptor exclusively guides through instruction without imparting virtue and righteousness, or that the Guardian exclusively…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
保其身體而不導之以教訓哉故成王以周召
爲師保而太傅無聞周公既没召仍爲保而不
聞師傅之設政以此爾有天下者盍亦以周家
爲法
詩
有酒湑我無酒酤我坎坎鼓我蹲蹲舞我
迨我暇矣飲此湑矣
李錫
同考試官教諭李　批〔小雅義形容親切有〕
===
周王篤友之意居然可見矣
考試官訓導吳　批〔此章本爲燕朋友而發瑯〕
中作是題者類不之及而謾援諸父諸舅之詞且
率以自鼓自舞爲說細玩經傳安有是意聞有
知者亦我暇處掇欠分曉獨此篇心目豁然況
他作又皆稱是孟遂於經者矣用刻是以式
羣髦
考試官教諭徐　批〔典雅精鍊自是大家〕
數文字
punctuated:
保其身體而不導之以教訓哉？故成王以周、召爲師保，而太傅無聞。周公既没，召仍爲保，而不聞師傅之設，政以此爾。有天下者盍亦以周家爲法？
詩
「有酒湑我，無酒酤我。坎坎鼓我，蹲蹲舞我。迨我暇矣，飲此湑矣。」
李錫
同考試官教諭李批〔小雅義形容親切有〕周王篤友之意，居然可見矣。
考試官訓導吳批〔此章本爲燕朋友而發瑯〕中作是題者類不之及，而謾援諸父諸舅之詞，且率以自鼓自舞爲說。細玩經傳，安有是意？聞有知者，亦我暇處掇欠分曉。獨此篇心目豁然，況他作又皆稱是，孟遂於經者矣。用刻是以式羣髦。
考試官教諭徐批〔典雅精鍊自是大家〕數文字。
translation_en:
…protect his person without guiding him through instruction? Thus King Cheng appointed the Dukes of Zhou and Shao as Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian, but no Grand Mentor is recorded. After the Duke of Zhou died, the Duke of Shao remained Grand Guardian, yet no appointment of a Grand Preceptor or Grand Mentor is recorded. It was precisely for this reason. Should those who rule the realm not likewise take the house of Zhou as their model?

Book of Odes
“If you have wine, strain it for me; if you have none, buy it for me. Beat the drums for me with resounding strokes; dance for me with lively steps. While I have leisure, let us drink this strained wine.”

Li Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The meaning of the Lesser Odes is portrayed vividly and aptly; the Zhou king’s devotion to his friends is plainly evident.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: “This stanza was originally composed for a feast for friends. Those who wrote on this topic [?] generally failed to address this, instead indiscriminately invoking the words about paternal and maternal uncles. Moreover, most explained it as beating the drums and dancing oneself. If one carefully studies the classic and its commentary, how could such a meaning be found? I hear that even those who understood it were still insufficiently clear in their treatment of ‘while I have leisure’ [?]. This essay alone brings clarity to the mind’s eye. Moreover, all his other compositions are of comparable quality: he is one who has attained mastery of the classic [?]. Accordingly, this piece is printed to serve as a model for the assembled talents.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Classically elegant and finely honed—truly writing of a master’s caliber.”

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
不計其物以為樂惟乘其時而相樂王者之篤
友也夫友誼篤否顧情之何如爾周之王者不
計有無而但及閒暇以相樂焉可謂知所重矣
此燕朋友故舊之樂歌也意謂乾餱之失既懲
乎人朋舊之情當盡諸我是故非酒無以合歡
于焉或有酒也物其偕矣而燕飲之需既備我
則湑之于以去其糟寧以有而嗇耶或無酒也
瓶之罄矣而勸酬之資偶盡我則酤之于以繼
其乏寧以無而止耶是則湑可也酤亦可也有
===
與無不計矣非樂無以侑食于焉言有鼓也則
鼓我之鼓以應以田而樂工備司其職坎坎之
在聽一真意之流形乎言有舞也則舞我之舞
以籥以翟而伶官畢獻其能蹲蹲之可觀一至
情之呈露乎是則鼓陳也舞亦陳也音與容並
作矣然是燕也豈限於常期哉但及我明堂肅
退而庶政庸有微閒即於斯焉而一舉豈待於
涉歲哉但追我路寢方臨而萬幾庸有少暇輒
於斯焉而載行今日有閒舉之於今日維兄及
punctuated:
不計其物以為樂，惟乘其時而相樂，王者之篤友也。夫友誼篤否，顧情之何如爾。周之王者不計有無，而但及閒暇以相樂焉，可謂知所重矣。
此燕朋友故舊之樂歌也。意謂乾餱之失既懲乎人，朋舊之情當盡諸我。是故非酒無以合歡，于焉或有酒也，物其偕矣，而燕飲之需既備，我則湑之，于以去其糟，寧以有而嗇耶？或無酒也，瓶之罄矣，而勸酬之資偶盡，我則酤之，于以繼其乏，寧以無而止耶？是則湑可也，酤亦可也，有與無不計矣。非樂無以侑食，于焉言有鼓也，則鼓我之鼓，以應以田，而樂工備司其職，坎坎之在聽，一真意之流形乎！言有舞也，則舞我之舞，以籥以翟，而伶官畢獻其能，蹲蹲之可觀，一至情之呈露乎！是則鼓陳也，舞亦陳也，音與容並作矣。然是燕也，豈限於常期哉？但及我明堂肅退，而庶政庸有微閒，即於斯焉而一舉，豈待於涉歲哉？但追我路寢方臨，而萬幾庸有少暇，輒於斯焉而載行。今日有閒，舉之於今日，維兄及
translation_en:
To take pleasure without reckoning the provisions, and simply seize the occasion to enjoy one another’s company: this is how a king shows devotion to his friends. Whether friendship is deep depends only on the quality of one’s feelings. The kings of Zhou did not reckon what they had or lacked, but simply used their leisure to enjoy their friends’ company. They may indeed be said to have understood what mattered.
This is a song for a banquet entertaining friends and old acquaintances. Its meaning is that, having taken warning from others’ fault over dry provisions, I should fully express my affection for friends of long standing. Thus, without wine there is no means of bringing people together in joy. If there is wine, the provisions are all at hand [?], and the requirements for the banquet are ready. I strain it to remove the lees. Could I have it and yet be stingy? If there is no wine, the vessels are empty and the supply for offering and returning cups has happened to run out. I buy more to make up the shortage. Could I stop merely because there is none? Thus, straining it is acceptable, and buying it is equally acceptable: possession and lack are not reckoned.
Without music there is no means of accompanying the meal. If there are drums, I have my drums beaten, with the ying and tian drums, while the musicians all attend to their duties. The resounding beats that reach the ear—are they not the manifestation of genuine feeling alone? If there is dancing, I have my dances performed, with flutes and pheasant feathers, while the music officials display all their skills. The vigorous dancing before our eyes—is it not the revelation of the deepest affection alone? Thus, drums are presented, and dances too are presented: sound and movement arise together.
Yet must this banquet be confined to fixed occasions? Whenever I have solemnly withdrawn from the Hall of Enlightenment and the many affairs of government afford a little leisure, I hold it then and there. Why wait until another year? Whenever I have just come to the principal palace hall [?] and the myriad affairs of rule afford a brief respite, I proceed to hold it again. If there is leisure today, hold it today: brothers and …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
弟式相好矣有無弗計引壺觴以共酌乾餱之
愆庶幾其能免乎詰旦有暇舉之於詰旦醉乎
與汝亦孔偕矣音容並作飲酒湑以為歡烏烏
之感庶幾其少慰乎吁不計乎其他惟盡其
情此周王所以為篤友也神之聽之豈不終和
而且平哉抑又論之友為五倫之一自天子以
至庶人未有不須友以成者周之王者有見於
此一則曰以速諸父一則曰以速諸舅至於此
則又曰兄弟無遠合尊卑疏戚而咸加之意焉
===
雍熙熙之盛孰謂非職此之由耶厥後角弓
詩作而反覆遠日以不振矣惜哉然則為世道
計者盍亦留情於伐木
求定
陳文昭
同考試官教諭李 批 頌義深得傳註意豈
嘗究心經學者乎可敬可慕
考試官訓導吳 批 周之業文作武述其功
文王既勤止我應受之敷時繹思我徂維
punctuated:
弟，式相好矣。有無弗計，引壺觴以共酌，乾餱之愆，庶幾其能免乎？詰旦有暇，舉之於詰旦，醉乎與汝，亦孔偕矣。音容並作，飲酒湑以為歡，烏烏之感，庶幾其少慰乎？吁！不計乎其他，惟盡其情，此周王所以為篤友也。神之聽之，豈不終和而且平哉？抑又論之，友為五倫之一，自天子以至庶人，未有不須友以成者。周之王者有見於此，一則曰「以速諸父」，一則曰「以速諸舅」，至於此，則又曰「兄弟無遠」。合尊卑疏戚而咸加之意焉，雍熙熙之盛，孰謂非職此之由耶？厥後《角弓》詩作，而反覆遠日以不振矣，惜哉！然則為世道計者，盍亦留情於《伐木》？
求定
陳文昭
同考試官教諭李批：頌義深得傳註意，豈嘗究心經學者乎？可敬可慕。
考試官訓導吳批：周之業，文作武述，其功「文王既勤止，我應受之」，「敷時繹思，我徂維
translation_en:
…younger brothers, showing affection for one another. Without reckoning who has provisions and who has none, we take up pitchers and cups and drink together: might we thus avoid the fault arising from dry provisions? If there is leisure the next morning, hold the feast the next morning. “Drunk together with you”—how closely united we are! Music and dancing commence together; we drink strained wine and make merry. Might this afford some consolation for the feelings stirred by the cries of “wu-wu” [?]? Ah! To reckon nothing else, but simply give full expression to one's affection: this is how the king of Zhou practiced devoted friendship. When the spirits hear it, will they not bring harmony and peace in the end?
To discuss this further: friendship is one of the Five Relationships. From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, none can achieve fulfillment without friends. The kings of Zhou understood this. In one place the poem says, “To invite the paternal uncles”; in another, “To invite the maternal uncles”; and here it further says, “Let no brothers be kept at a distance.” Those of high and low rank, distant and close kin alike, all received their care. Who could say that the flourishing harmony and prosperity [the transcription repeats 熙] did not arise precisely from this? Later, when the poem “Horn Bow” was composed, alienation increasingly prevailed and could no longer be remedied [reading uncertain]. How regrettable! Should those concerned for the moral condition of the age not also give their attention to “Felling Trees”?
“Seeking Settlement”
Chen Wenzhao
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: His exposition of the hymn's meaning thoroughly captures the sense of the commentaries. Surely he has devoted serious attention to the study of the Classics? Worthy of respect and admiration.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: As for Zhou's enterprise, King Wen began it and King Wu carried it forward. Their achievement is expressed in “King Wen has already labored diligently; we should receive it,” and “Extend these reflections; as we proceed, …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
足相配也場中作者徃徃偏重勞非題意此篇
說勤勞處收拾數語迥異尋常而於求定處尤
有歸著蓋飽經之粹者宜取冠本房
考試官教諭徐　批　頌義瑩潔可錄
詩人頌二王之功有勤勞以得天下者有封賞
以安天下者蓋大業之成雖本於文王而大封
之典實舉於武王也詩人並舉而叠頌之其美
盛德告成功之意至矣此頌文武之功而言其
大封功臣之意也謂夫我周之有天下者先之
===
讀而安天下者武之烈爲後王者可不知所自
哉彼不遑暇食而咸和萬民不專遊田而惠鮮
鰥寡多方之誕受得人心於攻崇伐密之餘文
王之勤勞天下可謂至矣區夏之肇造凝天命
於治岐遷豐之日文王之勤勞天下不其至乎
我子孫寵而受之尺地莫非其有也一民莫非
而有之一民莫非其臣固所宜也夫土地之所
在文王功德之所在也我豈敢以自專耶則布
此功德之可繹思者而分茅胙土以大賚有功
punctuated:
足相配也。場中作者徃徃偏重勞，非題意。此篇說勤勞處，收拾數語，迥異尋常，而於求定處尤有歸著，蓋飽經之粹者，宜取冠本房。
考試官教諭徐批：頌義瑩潔，可錄。
詩人頌二王之功，有勤勞以得天下者，有封賞以安天下者。蓋大業之成雖本於文王，而大封之典實舉於武王也。詩人並舉而叠頌之，其美盛德、告成功之意至矣。此頌文武之功，而言其大封功臣之意也。謂夫我周之有天下者，先之讀，而安天下者，武之烈。爲後王者，可不知所自哉？彼不遑暇食而咸和萬民，不專遊田而惠鮮鰥寡，多方之誕受，得人心於攻崇伐密之餘，文王之勤勞天下，可謂至矣。區夏之肇造，凝天命於治岐遷豐之日，文王之勤勞天下，不其至乎？我子孫寵而受之，尺地莫非其有也，一民莫非而有之，一民莫非其臣，固所宜也。夫土地之所在，文王功德之所在也。我豈敢以自專耶？則布此功德之可繹思者，而分茅胙土，以大賚有功
translation_en:
…are fully worthy of being paired. Writers in the examination hall often place undue emphasis on toil, which is not the intent of the topic. Where this essay discusses diligent labor, it gathers the argument into a few phrases, markedly different from the ordinary; its treatment of seeking stability is especially well directed. The writer is evidently steeped in the essence of the Classics and should be ranked first in this examining room.
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: The exposition of the hymn’s meaning is lucid and pure; it merits selection.
The poet praises the achievements of the two kings: one labored diligently to obtain All under Heaven, and the other bestowed fiefs and rewards to bring peace to All under Heaven. Although the completion of the great undertaking had its foundation in King Wen, the grand ceremony of enfeoffment was actually carried out by King Wu. The poet presents both together and praises them in succession, fully expressing his intention to extol their abundant virtue and proclaim their accomplished work. This hymn praises the achievements of Wen and Wu and explains their purpose in generously enfeoffing meritorious servants. It declares that our Zhou’s possession of All under Heaven was preceded by [unclear text: 先之讀][?], while bringing peace to All under Heaven was Wu’s achievement. Could succeeding kings fail to understand whence this arose?
He had no leisure even to eat, yet brought harmony to all the people; he did not devote himself to roaming and hunting, but showed kindness to widowers and widows. In receiving the many regions into his dominion, he won the people’s hearts after attacking Chong and campaigning against Mi. King Wen’s diligent labors for All under Heaven may indeed be called consummate. In founding the realm of Xia, he secured Heaven’s mandate during his rule at Qi and his removal to Feng. Were King Wen’s diligent labors for All under Heaven not consummate? We, his descendants, have been favored to receive it: not a foot of land is outside his possession, and not a single person [the wording here is garbled and repetitive][?]; not a single person is outside his subjecthood. This is certainly as it should be.
Wherever the land extends, King Wen’s achievements and virtue extend. How could I dare to reserve it exclusively for myself? Thus I spread these achievements and virtues, upon which one may ponder repeatedly, apportioning the sacrificial thatch and granting lands in fief, to reward lavishly those who have rendered meritorious service…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
馬人民之所存文王功德之所存也我豈敢以
自私耶則數此功德之可假令者而析圭儋爵
以大封有功焉是非市恩也于以之□之錫而
往求天下之安使誕受之多方有如盤石之固
也是非私惠也于以維藩維垣而往求天下之
定俾肇造之區夏有如太山之安也是則封賞
之典雖出於武王而開封賞之業實始於文王
二后之功豈不均可頌歟大抵封建者古聖王
公天下之良法也易曰先王建萬國親諸侯書
===
曰學由典常以蕃王室正與此詩同一意焉武
王踐祚之初首及斯典干城藩屏周于天下而
八百年有道之長端在此矣自秦郡縣一置後
世遂沿以爲理而古法無復存者可慨也夫柳
子曰封建非聖人意也勢也是豈至言哉
春秋
冬公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十三年〕冬十有二月
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男滑伯滕
子同盟于幽〔莊公十六年〕
punctuated:
馬。人民之所存，文王功德之所存也，我豈敢以自私耶？則數此功德之可假令者，而析圭儋爵，以大封有功焉。是非市恩也，于以之□之錫，而往求天下之安，使誕受之多方有如盤石之固也。是非私惠也，于以維藩維垣，而往求天下之定，俾肇造之區夏有如太山之安也。是則封賞之典雖出於武王，而開封賞之業實始於文王，二后之功豈不均可頌歟？大抵封建者，古聖王公天下之良法也。《易》曰：「先王建萬國，親諸侯。」《書》曰：「學由典常，以蕃王室。」正與此詩同一意焉。武王踐祚之初，首及斯典，干城藩屏周于天下，而八百年有道之長，端在此矣。自秦郡縣一置，後世遂沿以爲理，而古法無復存者，可慨也夫！柳子曰：「封建非聖人意也，勢也。」是豈至言哉？

春秋

冬，公會齊侯，盟于柯。〔莊公十三年〕冬，十有二月，會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子，同盟于幽。〔莊公十六年〕
translation_en:
…[?]. Wherever the people dwell, King Wen’s achievements and virtue abide. How could I dare to keep these for myself? Thus he enumerated those achievements and virtues that could be conferred [?], divided jade tablets and bestowed noble ranks [?], and generously enfeoffed those who had rendered meritorious service. This was no purchasing of favor: through these grants [?], he sought peace throughout the realm, making the many regions he had received as firm as a great rock. This was no bestowal of private favors: by establishing protective fences and walls, he sought stability throughout the realm, making the central lands he had founded as secure as Mount Tai. Thus, although the institutions of enfeoffment and reward issued from King Wu, the enterprise that made them possible truly began with King Wen. Are not the achievements of both sovereigns equally worthy of praise?

In general, enfeoffment was the excellent means by which the ancient sage kings made the realm common to all. The Book of Changes says: “The former kings established the myriad states and drew the feudal lords close.” The Book of Documents says: “Learn to follow the established norms, so as to protect the royal house.” These express precisely the same meaning as this ode. Upon ascending the throne, King Wu attended first to this institution. Shields, walls, fences, and screens extended throughout the realm; herein lay the very foundation of eight hundred years of enduring, principled rule. Once Qin established commanderies and counties, later generations continued to use them as their system of government, and the ancient institutions ceased to survive. How lamentable! Master Liu said: “Enfeoffment was not the intention of the sages; it arose from circumstances.” Can this truly be an authoritative pronouncement?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, the duke met the Marquis of Qi and concluded a covenant at Ke.” 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang〕 “In winter, in the twelfth month, he met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng, and they jointly concluded a covenant at You.” 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang〕

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
蔡溥
同考試官學正魏　批〔題本正大場中作者詞〕〔多掉晦殊未愜意獨此卷組織明傳不出聖〕
語而莊公得失自見非邃於春秋者其能有
此作耶
考試官訓導吳　批　得聖人稱公諱公之旨
考試官教諭徐　批　甚發傳意
望國始從霸而釋怨也為可予繼從霸而棄信
也為可譏蓋怨可釋而信不可棄也此柯幽之盟
===
書法不同而莊公之得失自明矣慨昔敵國之
剃方興乘車之禍莫測吾聞齊魯之讐蓋無觧
可通也今乎柯之盟外則齊侯畟之內則□□
從之玉帛復講一洗君父之讐盟好再通重□□
蹋舅之好是固忌親之惡也春秋何為予之耶
蓋義者制事之宜也而平怨交隣又國事之大
者可不度之以義乎彼莊公也怨成於囊□□
世讐位傳於桓巳為易世時固可以釋矣況□
於是時仗大義以尊周攘戎狄以安□□□□
punctuated:
蔡溥

同考試官學正魏批：〔題本正大，場中作者詞〕〔多掉晦，殊未愜意。獨此卷組織明傳，不出聖〕語，而莊公得失自見。非邃於春秋者，其能有此作耶？

考試官訓導吳批：得聖人稱公、諱公之旨。

考試官教諭徐批：甚發傳意。

望國始從霸而釋怨也，為可予；繼從霸而棄信也，為可譏。蓋怨可釋，而信不可棄也。此柯、幽之盟書法不同，而莊公之得失自明矣。

慨昔敵國之剃方興，乘車之禍莫測。吾聞齊魯之讐，蓋無觧可通也。今乎柯之盟，外則齊侯畟之，內則□□從之。玉帛復講，一洗君父之讐；盟好再通，重□□蹋舅之好。是固忌親之惡也，春秋何為予之耶？蓋義者，制事之宜也，而平怨交隣，又國事之大者，可不度之以義乎？彼莊公也，怨成於囊□□世讐，位傳於桓，巳為易世，時固可以釋矣。況□於是時，仗大義以尊周，攘戎狄以安□□□□
translation_en:
Cai Pu

Associate Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: 〔The topic itself is upright and weighty. The wording of those writing in the examination hall〕〔was mostly obscure [?] and decidedly unsatisfactory. This paper alone is structured to elucidate the commentary, never departing from the Sage’s〕 words, while Duke Zhuang’s successes and failings become apparent of themselves. Could anyone without a profound understanding of the Spring and Autumn Annals have produced such a work?

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: He grasps the Sage’s intent in explicitly naming the duke and in concealing the duke’s involvement.

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: He brings out the meaning of the commentary very well.

The state [?] initially followed the hegemon and relinquished its resentment: this merits approval. Subsequently it followed the hegemon and abandoned good faith: this merits censure. Resentment may be relinquished, but good faith must not be abandoned. Thus the covenants at Ke and You are recorded differently, and Duke Zhuang’s successes and failings become clear of themselves.

Alas, in former times, violence from the rival state [?] was just arising, and the calamity of riding in the carriage was unforeseeable. I have heard that the enmity between Qi and Lu seemed to admit of no reconciliation through which relations could be restored. Now, at the covenant of Ke, on the external side the Marquis of Qi [acted in an unclear manner], and on the internal side □□ followed him. Ceremonial exchanges of jade and silk were resumed, sweeping away the enmity over the death of ruler and father; friendly covenant relations were renewed, restoring □□ the ties with maternal kin [?]. Surely this was the evil of disregarding one’s own kin [?]. Why, then, do the Spring and Autumn Annals approve it?

Righteousness means judging what is fitting in the conduct of affairs. Settling grievances and maintaining relations with neighboring states are also major affairs of government: can they be left unmeasured by righteousness? As for Duke Zhuang, the grievance arose with Nang □□, a hereditary feud [?]; his position had passed to him from Duke Huan, so a generational succession had already occurred. The time indeed permitted the grievance to be relinquished. Moreover, □ at this time upheld the great principle of righteousness to honor Zhou and repelled the Rong and Di to bring peace to □□□□…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
當從者也苟或脇於強暴危其宗社則戾於義
而不孝矣噫聖人以是制事也君子以義爲尚
也義之於人大矣如之何其不從也故於是役
內則書公外則齊齊蓋予之以示夫義也既而
剽劔之盟已釋汶陽之田又歸吾意齊魯之好
將生平之不替矣今幽之盟也齊桓主之列國
趨之彼倡此應同心協載書之間我率爾從應
誠於約束之下是固同欲之信也春秋何爲諱
公耶蓋信者人君之寶也而從霸事大又國事
===
之重者可不持之以信乎彼齊魯也既協于柯
之盟又勤于鄄之會意固以孚矣況公於是時
陸歃同事鬼神之不可欺壇坫同登盟誓之不
可背信尤所當守者也無何受其逋逃違盟
好則乖於信而不義矣噫聖人以信易食也君
子以信易生也信之於人重矣如之何其可背
也故於是盟內諱我公外書同盟蓋惡之以示
夫信也嗚呼因其從義而予之因其背信而惡之
聖人欲人爲善之意有如此哉抑嘗因幽之盟
punctuated:
當從者也。苟或脇於強暴，危其宗社，則戾於義而不孝矣。噫！聖人以是制事也，君子以義爲尚也。義之於人大矣，如之何其不從也？故於是役，內則書公，外則齊齊，蓋予之以示夫義也。既而剽劔之盟已釋，汶陽之田又歸，吾意齊魯之好將生平之不替矣。
今幽之盟也，齊桓主之，列國趨之，彼倡此應，同心協載書之間，我率爾從，應誠於約束之下，是固同欲之信也。《春秋》何爲諱公耶？蓋信者，人君之寶也，而從霸事大，又國事之重者，可不持之以信乎？彼齊魯也，既協于柯之盟，又勤于鄄之會，意固以孚矣。況公於是時，陸歃同事，鬼神之不可欺；壇坫同登，盟誓之不可背。信尤所當守者也。無何，受其逋逃，違盟好，則乖於信而不義矣。噫！聖人以信易食也，君子以信易生也。信之於人重矣，如之何其可背也？故於是盟，內諱我公，外書同盟，蓋惡之以示夫信也。
嗚呼！因其從義而予之，因其背信而惡之，聖人欲人爲善之意有如此哉！抑嘗因幽之盟，
translation_en:
…was one whom he ought to follow. If, however, he yielded to coercion by a powerful aggressor and endangered his ancestral temples and altars of state, he would violate righteousness and fail in filial duty. Ah! The sage regulates affairs by this principle, and the gentleman esteems righteousness above all. So great is the importance of righteousness to human beings: how could one fail to follow it? Thus, in recording this undertaking, the Spring and Autumn Annals names the duke on the domestic side and records Qi on the external side [?], granting approval to make righteousness manifest. Subsequently, the covenant imposed at sword-point [?] was settled, and the lands of Wenyang were returned. I would have thought that friendship between Qi and Lu would remain undiminished throughout their lives.
Now, at the covenant of You, Duke Huan of Qi presided, and the other states hastened to attend. He took the lead and they responded, united in purpose through the written covenant. Our ruler readily followed, responding sincerely to its stipulations. This surely constituted the good faith of those sharing a common purpose. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals avoid naming the duke? Trustworthiness is a ruler’s treasure; following a hegemon and serving a great state are also weighty affairs of state. Could one fail to uphold them in good faith? Qi and Lu had already reached agreement at the covenant of Ke and had again exerted themselves at the meeting of Juan: their intentions had surely become mutually trustworthy. Moreover, at that time the duke participated with the others in the blood-oath rite [?], serving spirits that could not be deceived; they ascended the covenant altar together, and their sworn pledges could not be broken. Good faith was therefore all the more imperative. Before long, however, he harbored fugitives from Qi and violated their covenant of friendship. In departing from good faith, he acted unrighteously. Ah! The sage would relinquish food for good faith, and the gentleman would relinquish life for good faith. So weighty is the importance of good faith to human beings: how could one betray it? Thus, in recording this covenant, the Annals conceals the name of our duke on the domestic side, while recording externally that the rulers ‘covenanted together.’ It thereby expresses condemnation to make the principle of good faith manifest.
Alas! It approves him for following righteousness and condemns him for betraying good faith. Such was the sage’s desire that people should do good! Yet I have also, on considering the covenant of You…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而有感馬魯莊故盟失信国可甚矣齊桓當列
國分爭之時講尊王攘夷之信明大義而協衆
心雜曰衰世之事然天下賴之以尊中國賴之
以安厥功亦不細矣春秋於幽之盟而書同
美之也齊之九合成功夫子稱其一匡孟子姆
其爲盛桓固五霸之賢莊則春秋之霸者也又
奚深咎其夫信
荆敗蔡師于莘以蔡侯獻舞歸〔莊公十年〕
及楚人秦人宋人陳人衛人鄭人齊人曹
人邾人薛人鄫人盟于蜀〔成公二年〕
鄒奕
同考試官學正魏　批〔君臣夷夏之辨春秋大〕
義甚是明白士子惑於近時孝合之習肆爲
謬說此卷認理真切措詞嚴整春秋之表
表者故録之
考試官訓導吳　批〔得春秋謹嚴之法〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔詞嚴義正〕
===
以下僭上春秋鄙之而正大分以内夏外春秋
punctuated:
而有感馬！魯莊故盟失信，国可甚矣！齊桓當列國分爭之時，講尊王攘夷之信，明大義而協衆心。雜曰衰世之事，然天下賴之以尊，中國賴之以安，厥功亦不細矣。《春秋》於幽之盟而書同，美之也。齊之九合成功，夫子稱其一匡，孟子姆其爲盛。桓固五霸之賢，莊則春秋之霸者也，又奚深咎其夫信？
荆敗蔡師于莘，以蔡侯獻舞歸。〔莊公十年〕
及楚人、秦人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人、齊人、曹人、邾人、薛人、鄫人盟于蜀。〔成公二年〕
鄒奕
同考試官學正魏　批〔君臣夷夏之辨，春秋大〕義，甚是明白。士子惑於近時孝合之習，肆爲謬說。此卷認理真切，措詞嚴整，春秋之表表者，故録之。
考試官訓導吳　批〔得春秋謹嚴之法〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔詞嚴義正〕
以下僭上，《春秋》鄙之而正大分；以内夏外，《春秋》
translation_en:
…and am moved to reflection [?]. Duke Zhuang of Lu broke faith concerning the covenant [?]; this was indeed most reprehensible! When the various states were divided and contending, Duke Huan of Qi upheld the pledge to honor the king and repel the barbarians, clarified the great principles of righteousness, and united the hearts of the multitude. Although these might be called affairs of an age of decline [?], All under Heaven depended upon him for the maintenance of honor, and the Central States depended upon him for security. His achievements were no small matter. In recording the covenant at You, the Spring and Autumn Annals writes “jointly,” thereby commending it. For Qi’s achievement in assembling the lords nine times, the Master praised Huan for having once set the realm in order, and Mencius described his achievement as flourishing [?]. Huan was certainly a worthy member of the Five Hegemons, while Zhuang was a hegemon of the Spring and Autumn period. Why, then, condemn his breach of faith so severely [?]?
“Jing defeated the army of Cai at Shen and returned with Xianwu, Marquis of Cai.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
“Together with men of Chu, Qin, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Qi, Cao, Zhu, Xue, and Zeng, [we] covenanted at Shu.” 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕
Zou Yi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, School Director: 〔“The distinctions between ruler and subject and between barbarians and the Xia are great〕 principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and are exceedingly clear. Examination candidates, misled by the recent practice of accommodating incompatible positions [?], recklessly advance erroneous explanations. This paper grasps principle truly and precisely, and its wording is rigorous and well ordered. It stands out among essays on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and for that reason has been included.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔“It captures the meticulous rigor of the Spring and Autumn Annals.”〕
Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔“Its language is rigorous and its principles correct.”〕
When those below usurp the position of those above, the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns them and rectifies the fundamental distinctions of rank; concerning the Xia within and those outside [?], the Spring and Autumn Annals …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
賊之而立大防此于華而楚以號舉盟蜀而御
以人書聖人於君臣夷夏之間嚴矣慨昔楚以
祝融之裔僻處荆山之陬一旦因息嬀之故與
蔦蔡之師破其國都而入民罹荼毒之苦虜其
君主而朝市蒙犬羊之汚春秋於楚舉號者果
何謂哉蓋以天地間有大名分君臣是也彼楚
子也受子男之封爵寔周家之臣子使其向慕
華風革其僭竊則亦無不可者夫何恥封爵而
不居僭王號以自侈傴然自大於方城漢水之
===
間曾何思以蠻蟻之微擬君父之號其扼分已
踰矣況夫恃强猾夏其惡又可勝誅耶苟不黜
之則君臣之分泯矣故筆之從楚特舉號夲其
僭竊之罪正其蠻狄之名所以深絕之也既而
我成在位之時楚共又肆北圖之暴一旦大會
疑齊之將爰整陽橋之師即蜀地而號召諸侯
執牛耳而約束列卿春秋於是盟皆貶而稱人
又何謂也蓋以天地間有大界限夷夏是也蜀
列國也齊魯爲中國之望鄭許下首夏之兵使
punctuated:
賊之而立大防。此于華而楚以號舉，盟蜀而御以人書，聖人於君臣夷夏之間嚴矣。慨昔楚以祝融之裔，僻處荆山之陬，一旦因息嬀之故，與蔦蔡之師，破其國都而入。民罹荼毒之苦，虜其君主，而朝市蒙犬羊之汚。春秋於楚舉號者，果何謂哉？蓋以天地間有大名分，君臣是也。彼楚子也，受子男之封爵，寔周家之臣子。使其向慕華風，革其僭竊，則亦無不可者。夫何恥封爵而不居，僭王號以自侈，傴然自大於方城漢水之間？曾何思以蠻蟻之微，擬君父之號，其扼分已踰矣！況夫恃强猾夏，其惡又可勝誅耶？苟不黜之，則君臣之分泯矣。故筆之從楚，特舉號，夲其僭竊之罪，正其蠻狄之名，所以深絕之也。
既而我成在位之時，楚共又肆北圖之暴。一旦大會疑齊之將，爰整陽橋之師，即蜀地而號召諸侯，執牛耳而約束列卿。春秋於是盟皆貶而稱人，又何謂也？蓋以天地間有大界限，夷夏是也。蜀列國也，齊魯爲中國之望，鄭許下首夏之兵使
translation_en:
…condemns them as malefactors and establishes a great barrier. In the affair at Hua [?], Chu is designated by its state name; at the covenant at Shu, those involved [?] are recorded as “men.” The sage was strict indeed about the distinctions between ruler and subject, and between the alien peoples and the Xia.
Alas, Chu, descended from Zhurong, once dwelt in a remote corner of Mount Jing. Then, on account of Xi Gui, it suddenly brought an army against Cai [?], breached its capital, and entered it. The people suffered cruel devastation; their ruler was taken captive, and court and marketplace were defiled by dogs and sheep. What, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals mean by referring to Chu by its state name? There is a great distinction of status under Heaven: that between ruler and subject. The Viscount of Chu had received an enfeoffed rank among the viscounts and barons and was truly a subject of the house of Zhou. Had he admired and adopted the ways of the Hua and abandoned his usurpation, there would have been nothing unacceptable about him. Why, then, did he disdain his enfeoffed rank and refuse to abide by it, arrogating the title of king to magnify himself and presumptuously exalting himself [?] between Fangcheng and the Han River? Did he never consider that, with the insignificance of a barbarian ant, he was claiming a title equal to that of his ruler and father? He had already transgressed the bounds of his station [?]! Moreover, he relied on his strength to throw the Xia into disorder. Could his wickedness ever be adequately punished? Unless he were degraded, the distinction between ruler and subject would disappear. Thus, in recording him under “Chu,” the Annals uses only his state name, tracing his offense to usurpation and correctly identifying him as a barbarian. This is how it utterly repudiates him.
Later, during the reign of our Duke Cheng, Duke Gong of Chu again violently pursued his designs upon the north. Suddenly he assembled commanders against Qi [?], marshaled the army at Yangqiao, and went to Shu to summon the regional lords. He held the ox’s ear to preside over the covenant and bound the assembled ministers to its terms. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals degrade all those at this covenant by calling them “men”? There is a great boundary under Heaven: that between the alien peoples and the Xia. Shu and the various states [?]; Qi and Lu were eminent among the central states, while Zheng and Xu … the troops and envoys of the Xia [?] …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
當從者也嘗或脩怨怒隣危其宗社則戾於義
而不孝矣噫聖人以義制事也君子以義爲尚
也義之於人大矣如之何其不從也故於是役
內則書公外則爵齊蓋予之以示夫義也旣而
剿劍之盟已釋汶陽之田又歸吾意齊魯之好
將生平之不背矣今幽之盟也齊桓主之列國
趨之彼倡此應同心於載書之間我寧爾從攄
誠於約束之下是固同欲之信也春秋何爲諱
公耶蓋信者人君之寶也而從霸事大又國事
===
之重者可不持之以信乎彼齊魯也旣協于柯
之盟又勤于鄄之會意固以孚矣況公於是時
捷歃同事鬼神之不可欺壇坫同登盟誓之不
可背信尤所當守者也無何受其適逆遷違盟
好則乖於信而不義矣噫聖人以信易食也君
子以信易生也信之於人重矣如之何其可□
也故於是盟內諱我公外書同盟蓋悪□□□
夫信也吁因其從義而予之因其背信而□□
聖人欲人爲善之意有如此哉抑嘗因幽之□
punctuated: 當從者也。嘗或脩怨怒隣，危其宗社，則戾於義而不孝矣。噫！聖人以義制事也，君子以義爲尚也。義之於人大矣，如之何其不從也？故於是役，內則書公，外則爵齊，蓋予之以示夫義也。旣而剿劍之盟已釋，汶陽之田又歸，吾意齊魯之好，將生平之不背矣。今幽之盟也，齊桓主之，列國趨之，彼倡此應，同心於載書之間；我寧爾從，攄誠於約束之下。是固同欲之信也，春秋何爲諱公耶？蓋信者，人君之寶也，而從霸事大，又國事之重者，可不持之以信乎？彼齊魯也，旣協于柯之盟，又勤于鄄之會，意固以孚矣。況公於是時，捷歃同事，鬼神之不可欺；壇坫同登，盟誓之不可背，信尤所當守者也。無何，受其適逆，遷違盟好，則乖於信而不義矣。噫！聖人以信易食也，君子以信易生也。信之於人重矣，如之何其可□也？故於是盟，內諱我公，外書同盟，蓋悪□□□夫信也。吁！因其從義而予之，因其背信而□□，聖人欲人爲善之意有如此哉！抑嘗因幽之□
translation_en:
…were those whom one ought to follow. If, however, one nurses grievances, provokes neighboring states, and imperils the ancestral temples and altars of one's state, one violates righteousness and is unfilial. Alas! The sage orders affairs according to righteousness; the gentleman esteems righteousness above all. So great is righteousness in human affairs—how could one fail to follow it? Thus, in recording this campaign, the Spring and Autumn Annals names the duke on the side of our own state and accords the ruler of Qi his rank on the side of the other states. This grants approval in order to make righteousness manifest.

Afterward, the covenant of Jiaojian [?] had been dissolved, and the lands of Wenyang had been returned. I would have thought that the friendship between Qi and Lu would henceforth remain unbroken throughout their lifetimes. Now, at the covenant of You, Duke Huan of Qi presided, and the various states hastened to attend. One called and the others responded, united in purpose through the written covenant; one brought peace and the others followed, expressing their sincerity under its commitments. This surely was the good faith of those sharing a common purpose. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals conceal the duke's participation? Good faith is the treasure of a ruler; following the hegemon and serving a great state are also weighty affairs of state. Could these be conducted without good faith?

Qi and Lu had already reached agreement at the covenant of Ke and had again exerted themselves at the meeting of Juan. Their intentions had surely become mutually trustworthy. Moreover, at this time the duke joined in the blood-sipping rite [?], serving together with the others spirits who could not be deceived. They ascended the covenant platform together, and their sworn pledges could not be broken. Good faith was therefore all the more necessary to uphold. Before long, however, he accepted what came from the other side [?], changed course, and violated the covenant of friendship. Thus he departed from good faith and acted unrighteously.

Alas! The sage would exchange food for good faith; the gentleman would exchange life for good faith. So weighty is good faith in human affairs—how could it be [illegible]? Thus, in recording this covenant, the Annals conceals our own duke's participation internally, while externally recording that the states “covenanted together.” This expresses condemnation [three characters illegible] good faith [?]. Ah! To grant approval for following righteousness, and to [two characters illegible] for betraying good faith—such was the sage's desire that people do good! Yet, considering the [illegible] of You …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導吳　批　〔本治情之效言却足〕
考試官教諭徐　批　〔典而不浮〕
位尊者盡其道位卑者堅其守此大順之世也
盖大臣雖盡其道小臣易虧其守也今焉各無
所歉則國肥矣豈非大順之世哉禮運論聖王
治情而達於順意謂大順之世和氣薫蒸於宇
宙至治浹洽於臣工有所謂大臣焉職秉鈞衡
爲廟廊之綱領位居台鼎作邦國之儀刑其位
高責重盡其道雖矣今則調元贊化以風戚自
===
持論道經邦惟天工是亮入告於內者皆謀猷嘉
猷期一人之有慶居其位思行其道也敷宣於
外者善政善教奠四海於無虞任其職思濟乎
時也大臣之法盖如此有所謂小臣焉膺一官
之寄而分理庶務任一職之事而隊列百司其
位卑祿薄堅其守難矣今則清節是礪而苞苴
之不行惟操是持而簠簋之必飾服勞於官者
躬其事而後其食上不盜君其介如石也職專
於已者正其誼不謀其利下不漁民其心如水
punctuated:
考試官訓導吳批：〔本治情之效言却足〕
考試官教諭徐批：〔典而不浮〕
「位尊者盡其道，位卑者堅其守，此大順之世也。」
盖大臣雖盡其道，小臣易虧其守也。今焉各無所歉，則國肥矣，豈非大順之世哉？《禮運》論聖王治情而達於順，意謂大順之世，和氣薫蒸於宇宙，至治浹洽於臣工。有所謂大臣焉，職秉鈞衡，爲廟廊之綱領；位居台鼎，作邦國之儀刑。其位高責重，盡其道雖矣。今則調元贊化，以風戚自持；論道經邦，惟天工是亮。入告於內者，皆謀猷嘉猷，期一人之有慶，居其位思行其道也；敷宣於外者，善政善教，奠四海於無虞，任其職思濟乎時也。大臣之法盖如此。
有所謂小臣焉，膺一官之寄而分理庶務，任一職之事而隊列百司。其位卑祿薄，堅其守難矣。今則清節是礪，而苞苴之不行；惟操是持，而簠簋之必飾。服勞於官者，躬其事而後其食，上不盜君，其介如石也；職專於已者，正其誼不謀其利，下不漁民，其心如水
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The argument is grounded in the effects of regulating human feelings; its wording is adequate. [?]〕
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical in style without being superficial.〕
“Those in exalted positions fully carry out their Way; those in lowly positions remain firm in their integrity. This is an age of supreme harmony.”
Even when the great ministers fully carry out their Way, lesser ministers can readily compromise their integrity. Now, when neither falls short, the state flourishes. Is this not an age of supreme harmony? The “Evolution of Rites” chapter of the Book of Rites discusses how sage kings regulate human feelings and thereby achieve harmony. Its meaning is that, in an age of supreme harmony, harmonious influences permeate the universe, and perfect government thoroughly imbues the officials. There are those called great ministers: entrusted with the balancing scales of government, they provide the guiding framework of the court; occupying the highest ministerial offices, they serve as models for the realm. Their positions are exalted and their responsibilities weighty; fully carrying out their Way is difficult [?]. Now they harmonize the primal forces and assist the transforming processes, maintaining their conduct through “feng qi” [?]; they deliberate upon the Way and order the realm, assisting Heaven’s work alone. What they submit within the court consists entirely of plans and excellent counsels, intended to secure blessings for the One Man, the sovereign: occupying their positions, they think of putting their Way into practice. What they disseminate beyond the court is good government and good instruction, securing all within the Four Seas against anxiety: holding their offices, they think of meeting the needs of their age. Such is the great ministers’ adherence to proper standards.
There are also those called lesser ministers: entrusted with a particular office, they share responsibility for managing the many affairs of government; charged with the business of a particular post, they take their places among the various offices. Their positions are lowly and their stipends meager; remaining firm in their integrity is difficult. Now they cultivate incorruptible principles, so that gifts offered as bribes do not circulate; they uphold their moral resolve, ensuring that their sacrificial vessels are properly maintained—a figure for official integrity. Those who labor in office attend personally to their duties before taking their pay. Toward those above, they do not rob their ruler; their integrity is firm as stone. Those whose official responsibilities are their own rectify their conduct without seeking personal profit. Toward those below, they do not prey upon the people; their hearts are like water…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也小臣之廉蓋如此夫以大臣爲法則國之肥
在大臣矣小臣爲廉則國之肥在小臣矣非聖
王治情而致大順曷克以臻此哉抑論之盡道
守己人臣皆然也記者於此各專言之何耶蓋
大臣祿厚必廉而責重易至於不法小臣責輕
必法而祿薄易至於不廉此記者所以於法獨
言大臣於廉獨歸小臣也噫言雖各有所專然
亦對舉而並例之此又記者言外意也爲臣者
宜並鑒諸
===
禮樂刑政其極一也所以同民心而出治
道也
姜潤身
同考試官學正林　批　〔出治道處當指禮樂刑政言今只說有知者又不能融會經意〕
而發揮明白是作從容數語而詞旨燦然當
是作
考試官訓導吳　批　題目本正大率以奧僻
求之謬以遠矣是篇命意措詞顧專守
punctuated:
也。小臣之廉，蓋如此。夫以大臣爲法，則國之肥在大臣矣；小臣爲廉，則國之肥在小臣矣。非聖王治情而致大順，曷克以臻此哉？抑論之，盡道守己，人臣皆然也。記者於此各專言之，何耶？蓋大臣祿厚，必廉，而責重，易至於不法；小臣責輕，必法，而祿薄，易至於不廉。此記者所以於法獨言大臣，於廉獨歸小臣也。噫！言雖各有所專，然亦對舉而並例之，此又記者言外意也。爲臣者宜並鑒諸。

禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。

姜潤身

同考試官學正林批：〔出治道處，當指禮樂刑政言，今只說有知者，又不能融會經意〕而發揮明白，是作從容數語，而詞旨燦然，當是作。

考試官訓導吳批：題目本正大，率以奧僻求之，謬以遠矣。是篇命意措詞，顧專守
translation_en:
… so it is. Such, indeed, is the integrity of lesser ministers. When great ministers abide by proper standards, the flourishing of the state rests with them; when lesser ministers maintain their integrity, the flourishing of the state rests with them. Without a sage king ordering human feelings and bringing about great harmony, how could this be achieved? Yet, on reflection, fulfilling the Way and maintaining personal rectitude are duties common to all ministers. Why does the author of the Record here assign each exclusively to one group? Great ministers receive generous stipends and may be expected to maintain their integrity, but their heavy responsibilities make them liable to depart from proper standards. Lesser ministers have lighter responsibilities and may be expected to abide by proper standards, but their meager stipends make them liable to compromise their integrity. This is why the author speaks only of great ministers when discussing standards, and attributes integrity only to lesser ministers. Ah! Although each statement has its particular application, the two are also juxtaposed so that both standards apply to both groups. This, too, is the author's meaning beyond the words. Those serving as ministers should take both as their guide.

“Rites, music, punishments, and government have a single ultimate purpose: they are the means of unifying the people's hearts and bringing forth the way of good government.”

Jiang Runshen

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔The passage about ‘bringing forth the way of good government’ should refer to rites, music, punishments, and government. Here it speaks only of those who possess understanding [?], and also fails to integrate the meaning of the classic.〕 Yet the exposition is clear. With a few unhurried phrases, this composition makes its language and purport shine forth. It should be this composition [?].

Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: The topic itself is upright and grand. To seek its meaning indiscriminately in obscurity and abstruseness is to stray far indeed. In framing its ideas and choosing its words, however, this essay adheres exclusively to …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□此文可□□□
考試官教諭徐　批　此文非識禮樂刑政之道
記者要感人之道同著感人之道大哉禮樂刑
政同一感人之道也然能同民心而出治道則
其道何大哉樂記推先王慎政感人之旨意謂
政以感人雖異效生所感則同誠以先王感人
之政有五禮焉有六樂焉禮樂固異道矣然推
其極致禮以道志樂以和聲同一慎感人之政
也禮之功即樂之功耳有五刑焉有八政焉刑
===
政固殊事矣然原其要歸政以一行刑以防姦
同一慎感人之道也刑之用即政之用耳由是
民心歸於所感喜怒合當然之則一人之心有
以通千萬人之心好惡適同然之情一人之志
有以通千萬人之志天下一家無睽異也中國
一人無間隔也民心之同也何如由是治化咸
於所同好惡平而人道正強弱各安其分而不
爭民心順而和氣應智愚咸得其所而無怨合
敬同愛一道化之宣布也相親相敬一德教之
punctuated:
同考試官□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□此文可□□□。
考試官教諭徐，批：此文非識禮樂刑政之道。
記者要感人之道同，著感人之道大哉！禮樂刑政，同一感人之道也。然能同民心而出治道，則其道何大哉！《樂記》推先王慎政感人之旨，意謂政以感人，雖異效生所感則同，誠以先王感人之政，有五禮焉，有六樂焉。禮樂固異道矣，然推其極致，禮以道志，樂以和聲，同一慎感人之政也。禮之功，即樂之功耳。有五刑焉，有八政焉，刑政固殊事矣，然原其要歸，政以一行，刑以防姦，同一慎感人之道也。刑之用，即政之用耳。由是民心歸於所感，喜怒合當然之則，一人之心有以通千萬人之心；好惡適同然之情，一人之志有以通千萬人之志。天下一家，無睽異也；中國一人，無間隔也。民心之同也何如！由是治化咸於所同，好惡平而人道正，強弱各安其分而不爭；民心順而和氣應，智愚咸得其所而無怨。合敬同愛，一道化之宣布也；相親相敬，一德教之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner: [seventeen illegible characters] This essay may [three illegible characters].
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: This essay does not comprehend the Way of rites, music, punishments, and government.
The author of the Record sums up the unity of the ways of influencing people and reveals how great that way is! Rites, music, punishments, and government share one way of influencing people. Yet if they can unite the people’s hearts and bring forth the Way of good government, how great that way must be! The Record of Music expounds the former kings’ purpose in exercising care over government to influence people. Its meaning is that government influences people: although its effects differ, the influence it produces is the same [?]. Indeed, among the former kings’ measures for influencing people were the five rites and the six forms of music. Rites and music certainly follow different paths. Yet, considered in their ultimate effect, rites guide aspirations and music harmonizes sounds: both belong to the same careful conduct of government to influence people. The achievement of rites is simply the achievement of music. There were also the five punishments and the eight affairs of government. Punishments and government certainly concern different matters. Yet, traced to their essential purpose, government unifies conduct and punishments prevent wrongdoing: both belong to the same careful way of influencing people. The function of punishments is simply the function of government.
Thus the people’s hearts converge under this influence. Their joy and anger accord with the proper standards, so that the heart of one person can communicate with the hearts of countless others. Their likes and dislikes accord with feelings shared by all, so that the will of one person can communicate with the wills of countless others. All under Heaven become one family, without discord; the Central Kingdom becomes one person, without separation. How complete is this unity of the people’s hearts!
Thus the transforming influence of government reaches all through this unity [?]. Likes and dislikes are balanced and the human Way is set right; the strong and the weak are each content with their allotted station and do not contend. The people’s hearts are compliant and harmonious vital energies respond; the wise and the foolish all find their proper place and bear no resentment. United in reverence and sharing in love: this is the dissemination of transformation through a single Way. Cherishing and respecting one another: this is a single moral teaching’s …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
流行也治道之出也何如是則莫難同者人心
也莫難出者治道也今先王慎政感人而能同
之出之如此則感人之道何其大哉抑論之先
王慎政感人豈徒然哉蓋音生於人心之感而
人心哀樂之感由於政治之得失故先王必慎
政感人以和人心而為作樂之本也欲作樂者
能平其政以和民心則和樂興矣此治世之音
安以樂者其政和也書曰予欲聞六律五聲八
音在治忽其此之謂歟後世不究其本徒事其
末遂以治之興替無關於樂是何不思之甚
===
第貳場
論
堯舜所以為聖
陳文燧
同考試官教諭李　批〔以聖人通變宜民之制形諸論議反覆□□□漢雄□遠悉自心胸中流出真佳制也〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔見理真切措詞□□□□〕
□□□□□
punctuated:
流行也。治道之出也何如？是則莫難同者，人心也；莫難出者，治道也。今先王慎政感人，而能同之、出之如此，則感人之道何其大哉！抑論之，先王慎政感人，豈徒然哉？蓋音生於人心之感，而人心哀樂之感，由於政治之得失，故先王必慎政感人，以和人心，而為作樂之本也。欲作樂者，能平其政以和民心，則和樂興矣。此治世之音安以樂者，其政和也。《書》曰：「予欲聞六律、五聲、八音，在治忽。」其此之謂歟？後世不究其本，徒事其末，遂以治之興替無關於樂，是何不思之甚！

第貳場
論
堯舜所以為聖
陳文燧

同考試官教諭李　批〔以聖人通變宜民之制，形諸論議，反覆□□□漢雄□遠，悉自心胸中流出，真佳制也。〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔見理真切，措詞□□□□。〕
□□□□□
translation_en:
…the diffusion of moral instruction. How fully the way of governance thus emerges! Nothing, then, is harder to unite than people’s hearts, and nothing harder to bring forth than the way of governance. Yet the former kings, by exercising care in government and influencing people, could unite those hearts and bring forth that way to such an extent. How great, then, is the way of influencing people!

To consider this further: was it without purpose that the former kings exercised care in government to influence people? Musical sounds arise from the stirring of people’s hearts, and the sorrow and joy stirred in their hearts arise from the successes and failures of government. Thus the former kings invariably exercised care in government to influence people and harmonize their hearts, thereby laying the foundation for making music. If those who wish to make music can make their government equitable and so harmonize the people’s hearts, harmonious music will flourish. This is why the sounds of a well-governed age are peaceful and joyful: its government is harmonious. The Book of Documents says: “I wish to hear the six pitch standards, the five notes, and the eight kinds of instrumental sound, to discern good government or neglect.” Is this not what it means? Later generations failed to investigate the root and attended only to the branches, consequently supposing that the rise and decline of good government had no connection with music. How utterly thoughtless!

Second Session
Discourse
What Made Yao and Shun Sages
Chen Wensui

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭徐　批　場中作者多冗泛無
謂令人厭觀此作一根於理而波瀾洶湧則是
一家機軸真作手也録以爲式
論曰時之極者不容不變也通其變以利
乎民非聖人不能與是焉何邪時之極也
運也自然之數也值夫自然之數當其時
之極而吾將付其變於不聞可乎聖人於
此蓋不能辭其責矣不惟不能政不忍也
不能終辭其責出而爲之圖不□□其變
===
於不聞而亟爲之理變而通之神而明之
蓋財成輔相之道以左右民卒使夫數之
與運不得以梗吾治安之化而吾便業之
盛亦將與天地相爲悠久矣其可以易而
能之乎是孰能之邪聖人能之也此堯舜
之所以爲聖也所謂過此以往而未之或
知也堯舜之民亦安得而知之五峯胡氏
即是爲堯舜所以聖嗚呼五峯其知之矣
請究言之天下道二常與變對變者常之
punctuated:
考試官教諭徐批：場中作者多冗泛無謂，令人厭觀。此作一根於理，而波瀾洶湧，則是一家機軸，真作手也，録以爲式。

論曰：時之極者，不容不變也。通其變以利乎民，非聖人不能與是焉。何邪？時之極也，運也，自然之數也。值夫自然之數，當其時之極，而吾將付其變於不聞，可乎？聖人於此，蓋不能辭其責矣。不惟不能，政不忍也。不能終辭其責，出而爲之圖，不□□其變於不聞，而亟爲之理。變而通之，神而明之，蓋財成輔相之道，以左右民，卒使夫數之與運不得以梗吾治安之化，而吾便業之盛亦將與天地相爲悠久矣。其可以易而能之乎？是孰能之邪？聖人能之也。此堯舜之所以爲聖也。所謂過此以往，而未之或知也。堯舜之民亦安得而知之？五峯胡氏即是爲堯舜所以聖。嗚呼！五峯其知之矣。請究言之：天下道二，常與變對。變者，常之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Xu, an Instructor: Most writers in the examination hall are verbose, vague, and devoid of substance, making their work tiresome to read. This composition is rooted throughout in principle, yet its movement surges like great waves. It thus displays a distinctive method of composition: here is a true master of writing. It is recorded as a model.

The discourse states: When an age reaches its utmost limit, change is unavoidable. Only a sage can master that change to benefit the people. Why is this? An age reaching its limit is a matter of the course of fortune and the natural ordering of things. Encountering this natural ordering, at the moment when the age reaches its limit, could I leave its changes unheeded? Here the sage surely cannot disclaim his responsibility. It is not merely that he cannot: he cannot bear to do so. Unable ultimately to disclaim his responsibility, he comes forward to devise measures, refusing to leave its changes unheeded [?], and urgently brings them into order. He transforms things and makes them work freely; through spiritual insight he makes them clear. This is surely the Way of shaping and completing, assisting and sustaining, so as to guide and support the people. In the end, neither the ordering of things nor the course of fortune can obstruct my transforming influence toward orderly and peaceful government, while the flourishing livelihoods I secure [?] will endure as long as Heaven and Earth. Could this be accomplished with ease? Who can accomplish it? The sage can. This is what makes Yao and Shun sages. As the saying goes, “Beyond this, none has yet known.” How could even the people of Yao and Shun have understood it? Hu Wufeng took precisely this to be what made Yao and Shun sages. Ah, Wufeng indeed understood it!

Allow me to explain this fully. The ways of the world are two: constancy and change stand opposite one another. Change is constancy’s …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
伏常者變之倚也時不皆常而世不能以
無變通其變弗滞於常聖人責也聖人之
所以聖也曷爲聖大而化也聖而不可知
也百行之宗也萬物之祖也千萬世之表
極也堯舜之德典謨語之詳矣稽堯舜而
爲聖雖五尺童子無或焉至於堯舜所以
聖其孰得而知之哉何也變而通之聖人
之能事也非聖人不能而堯舜能之此堯
舜所以爲聖也嘗觀之天地矣二氣之循
===
環四時之運行萬物之終始紛紜轇轕
推相盪而不可窮窦極而燠承炎極而凉
至歸根之木及春乃生咸俯之蟲陽啓而
鳴氣之爲也數之序也天地莫而四時成
也事成而極極則必變物盈而傾傾則必
革勢之不容已也知天地之道則知堯舜
通天下之變矣通天下之變利天下之民
也變之以其時革之以其數也故曰廣大
配天地變通配四時非聖人其孰能與於
punctuated:
伏，常者變之倚也。時不皆常，而世不能以無變。通其變，弗滞於常，聖人責也，聖人之所以聖也。曷爲聖？大而化也，聖而不可知也，百行之宗也，萬物之祖也，千萬世之表極也。堯舜之德，《典》《謨》語之詳矣。稽堯舜而爲聖，雖五尺童子無或焉。至於堯舜所以聖，其孰得而知之哉？何也？變而通之，聖人之能事也。非聖人不能，而堯舜能之，此堯舜所以爲聖也。
嘗觀之天地矣：二氣之循環，四時之運行，萬物之終始，紛紜轇轕，推相盪而不可窮。窦極而燠承，炎極而凉至。歸根之木，及春乃生；咸俯之蟲，陽啓而鳴。氣之爲也，數之序也，天地莫而四時成也。事成而極，極則必變；物盈而傾，傾則必革，勢之不容已也。知天地之道，則知堯舜通天下之變矣。通天下之變，利天下之民也。變之以其時，革之以其數也。故曰：「廣大配天地，變通配四時。」非聖人，其孰能與於
translation_en:
…lie latent; constancy is that upon which change rests. Times are not always constant, and the world cannot be without change. To respond effectively to change without becoming confined by constancy is the sage’s responsibility; it is what makes a sage a sage. What is meant by sageliness? It is greatness transformed; it is sageliness beyond comprehension. It is the source of all conduct, the progenitor of all things, and the supreme standard for countless generations. The virtues of Yao and Shun are described in detail in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents. That Yao and Shun, when examined, were sages is something even a child five feet tall would not doubt [?]. But who can know what made Yao and Shun sages? Why is this so? To transform things and enable them to proceed freely is the sage’s consummate accomplishment. None but sages can do this, yet Yao and Shun could: this is what made them sages.
I have observed this in Heaven and Earth: the cycling of the two vital forces, the movement of the four seasons, and the endings and beginnings of all things are multitudinous and intertwined, impelling and stirring one another without exhaustion. When [cold?] reaches its extreme, warmth follows; when heat reaches its extreme, coolness arrives. Trees that have returned to their roots grow again when spring comes; insects that all lie dormant [?] begin to call when the yang force awakens. This is the working of vital force and the ordered sequence of cosmic cycles: Heaven and Earth remain silent [?], yet the four seasons accomplish their course. Affairs reach their culmination upon completion, and at that culmination they must change; things become full and topple, and when they topple they must be renewed. The tendency of things permits no stopping. To understand the Way of Heaven and Earth is thus to understand how Yao and Shun responded effectively to the changes of the world. Responding effectively to the changes of the world benefits its people. They changed things according to the appropriate time and renewed them according to their appointed cycles. Thus it is said: “In breadth and greatness, it matches Heaven and Earth; in change and adaptation, it matches the four seasons.” Who but a sage could participate in…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
斯粵自邃古之初伏羲氏作為八卦以前
民用制為網罟以佃以漁神農氏出乃為
耒耜以教民耕日中為市以貿遷有無黃
帝繼之始立制度作算數造律呂舉封禪
之禮三聖人者無非所以開物成務相時
之變而為之也此其聖之所以為盛也然
而混沌初判風氣未融世尚鴻荒民惟顓
蒙法有所未備文有所未著禮有所未詳
運也數之自然也勢也堯舜於此豈能辭
===
其責哉抑亦不忍也堯舜何容心哉時也
時其變而為之通因其數而為之革於是
乎斷脩斷於洞庭禽封豨於桑林殺□四凶
於裔夷四時未正也吾則命羲和以正四
時五辰未順也吾則命百工以順五辰七
政未齊也吾則璣衡以齊七政水未通以
禹火通以益工通以垂樂通以夔五教通
以契刑通以皐陶禮通以伯夷稼穡通以
稷曆通以羲和病民之衣皮而未知織絍
punctuated: 斯？粵自邃古之初，伏羲氏作為八卦，以前民用；制為網罟，以佃以漁。神農氏出，乃為耒耜，以教民耕；日中為市，以貿遷有無。黃帝繼之，始立制度，作算數，造律呂，舉封禪之禮。三聖人者，無非所以開物成務，相時之變而為之也。此其聖之所以為盛也。然而混沌初判，風氣未融，世尚鴻荒，民惟顓蒙，法有所未備，文有所未著，禮有所未詳。運也，數之自然也，勢也。堯舜於此，豈能辭其責哉？抑亦不忍也。堯舜何容心哉？時也。時其變而為之通，因其數而為之革。於是乎斷脩斷於洞庭，禽封豨於桑林，殺□四凶於裔夷。四時未正也，吾則命羲和以正四時；五辰未順也，吾則命百工以順五辰；七政未齊也，吾則璣衡以齊七政。水未通以禹，火通以益，工通以垂，樂通以夔，五教通以契，刑通以皐陶，禮通以伯夷，稼穡通以稷，曆通以羲和。病民之衣皮而未知織絍
translation_en: …in this? From the very beginning of remote antiquity, Fuxi devised the eight trigrams to guide the people's practical activities, and made nets for hunting and fishing. Shennong arose and made plows to teach the people cultivation; he established markets at midday so that goods could be exchanged between those who had them and those who lacked them. Huangdi succeeded him, first establishing institutions and regulations, devising arithmetic, creating the musical pitch standards, and performing the feng and shan sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Everything these three sages did served to open up the potential of things and bring affairs to completion, responding to changes in their times. This was what made their sagacity so abundant. Yet primordial chaos had only just been divided, civilizing influences had not yet permeated the world, the age was still uncultivated, and the people remained ignorant. Laws were not yet fully provided, cultural forms not yet manifest, and rites not yet elaborated. Such was the course of events, the natural working of allotted cycles, and the force of circumstances. Could Yao and Shun, in these circumstances, shirk their responsibility? Nor could they bear to do so. What room was there for personal intent on Yao's and Shun's part? It was the times. They responded at the proper moment to changing circumstances, opening ways forward, and instituted reforms in accordance with the allotted cycles. Thus they cut down the long serpent [?] at Dongting, captured the great boar at Sanglin, and killed □ the Four Evildoers among the distant border peoples [?]. If the four seasons were not correctly determined, they would command Xi and He to rectify them; if the five celestial markers were not in due order, they would command the various officials to bring them into order; if the seven celestial regulators were not aligned, they would use the jade astronomical instrument and sighting tube to align them. Waters not yet flowing freely were given passage through Yu; the use of fire was advanced through Yi, craftsmanship through Chui, music through Kui, the five teachings through Xie, punishments through Gao Yao, ritual through Bo Yi, agriculture through Ji, and calendrical reckoning through Xi and He. Troubled that the people wore skins and did not yet know how to weave…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
以禦寒也於是乎作衣裳病民之疲於負
荷而艱於致遠也於是乎作輪轝病民之
穴居野處而或阽於危也於是乎作宮室
病民之出入而厄於徒涉也於是乎作舟
楫病民之虞於竊攘而跡於防禦也於是
乎作門柝病民之死無以葬而掩於藁裡
也於是乎作棺槨病民之無以自衛而憂
於譸嗔也於是乎作弧矢病民之窮於結
繩而相欺無已也於是乎作書契病民之
===
知有耕耨而未知有舂揄也於是乎作杵
臼預為之防過為之備化而裁之推而行
之舉而措之於天下範圍天地而不過曲
成萬物而不遺盡財成輔相之道以左右
民黃帝之所未及為者蓋已悉為之矣堯
舜何容心哉極者變之漸也盈者革之初
也時也數也運也勢之不容已也天固不
虛生聖人也向使堯舜於此委其變而莫
之為其得謂之聖耶知委其責之不得為
punctuated: 以禦寒也，於是乎作衣裳；病民之疲於負荷而艱於致遠也，於是乎作輪轝；病民之穴居野處而或阽於危也，於是乎作宮室；病民之出入而厄於徒涉也，於是乎作舟楫；病民之虞於竊攘而跡於防禦也，於是乎作門柝；病民之死無以葬而掩於藁裡也，於是乎作棺槨；病民之無以自衛而憂於譸嗔也，於是乎作弧矢；病民之窮於結繩而相欺無已也，於是乎作書契；病民之知有耕耨而未知有舂揄也，於是乎作杵臼。預為之防，過為之備，化而裁之，推而行之，舉而措之於天下，範圍天地而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，盡財成輔相之道以左右民。黃帝之所未及為者，蓋已悉為之矣。堯舜何容心哉？極者，變之漸也；盈者，革之初也。時也，數也，運也，勢之不容已也。天固不虛生聖人也。向使堯舜於此委其變而莫之為，其得謂之聖耶？知委其責之不得為
translation_en:
…to ward off the cold, and so they made upper and lower garments. Troubled that the people were exhausted by carrying burdens and found it difficult to transport things far, they made wheeled vehicles. Troubled that the people lived in caves and in the open, sometimes exposed to danger, they built houses. Troubled that the people, in their comings and goings, suffered from having to ford waters on foot, they made boats and oars. Troubled that the people feared theft and plunder and were hampered in defending themselves [?], they made gates and watchmen’s clappers. Troubled that the people had no means of burying their dead and merely covered them in straw wrappings, they made inner and outer coffins. Troubled that the people had no means of defending themselves and were distressed by deception and anger [?], they made bows and arrows. Troubled that the people were limited by the use of knotted cords and endlessly deceived one another, they made written documents and contracts. Troubled that the people knew how to plow and weed but did not yet know how to pound and remove grain from the mortar [?], they made pestles and mortars.
They took precautions in advance and made ample provision. They adapted and regulated transformations, extended these measures and put them into practice, and applied them throughout the realm. They encompassed Heaven and Earth without exceeding their bounds and brought all things to fulfillment in every particular without omission. They fully exercised the Way of regulating and assisting the workings of nature, thereby aiding the people. All that Huangdi had not had time to accomplish, they had now accomplished. What deliberate personal purpose could Yao and Shun have had in this? Reaching an extreme marks the approach of change; reaching fullness marks the beginning of renewal. These are matters of timing, allotted cycles, and the course of events—the momentum of circumstances permits no stopping. Heaven certainly does not bring forth sages in vain. Had Yao and Shun, in these circumstances, left these changes unattended and done nothing, could they have been called sages? To know that, by abandoning their responsibilities, they could not have become …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖則知堯舜之所以聖而在於通時之變
不誣矣堯舜之道何道也天地之道也堯
舜之心何心也伏犧神農黃帝之心也堯
舜道天地之道而輔其不及心伏犧神農
黃帝三大聖人之心而不違焉孰謂堯舜
所以為聖顧不在是也邪夾考其時九族
既睦矣五品遜矣百工釐矣庶績熙矣庶
明勵翼矣百姓昭明矣萬邦協和矣四方
風動矣百谷登矣草木蕃廡矣鳥獸魚鱉
===
咸若矣通變之效至是彰矣堯舜之心至
是始少慰矣問之在朝在朝不知問之在
野在野不知其不知者不容知也智周萬
物道濟天下蕩蕩乎無能名焉巍巍乎雖
甚盛德蔑以加矣竊口備物致用立成器
以為天下利莫大於聖人其堯舜之謂與
彼徒以盡性為說者是豈知堯舜之聖哉
雖然未可盡非也盡性善者堯舜之聖也
通其變於未窮者堯舜之所以為聖也要
punctuated: 聖，則知堯舜之所以聖，而在於通時之變，不誣矣。堯舜之道何道也？天地之道也。堯舜之心何心也？伏犧、神農、黃帝之心也。堯舜道天地之道而輔其不及，心伏犧、神農、黃帝三大聖人之心而不違焉，孰謂堯舜所以為聖，顧不在是也邪？夾考其時，九族既睦矣，五品遜矣，百工釐矣，庶績熙矣，庶明勵翼矣，百姓昭明矣，萬邦協和矣，四方風動矣，百谷登矣，草木蕃廡矣，鳥獸魚鱉咸若矣。通變之效至是彰矣，堯舜之心至是始少慰矣。問之在朝，在朝不知；問之在野，在野不知。其不知者，不容知也。智周萬物，道濟天下，蕩蕩乎無能名焉，巍巍乎雖甚盛德蔑以加矣。竊口，備物致用，立成器以為天下利，莫大於聖人，其堯舜之謂與？彼徒以盡性為說者，是豈知堯舜之聖哉？雖然，未可盡非也。盡性善者，堯舜之聖也；通其變於未窮者，堯舜之所以為聖也。要
translation_en:
…a sage, then one knows that it is no false claim that Yao and Shun were sages because they responded effectively to the changes of their times. What was the Way of Yao and Shun? It was the Way of Heaven and Earth. What was the heart of Yao and Shun? It was the heart of Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi. Yao and Shun followed the Way of Heaven and Earth and supplemented what it did not accomplish; they took as their own the heart of the three great sages, Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi, without departing from it. Who could say that this was not precisely what made Yao and Shun sages?

Examining their times [?], the nine degrees of kinship were already harmonious; the five human relationships were duly observed; the hundred offices were well ordered; all undertakings flourished; the many worthy men diligently lent their aid; the people were enlightened; the myriad states were brought into concord; the four quarters responded as though moved by the wind; the hundred grains ripened; plants and trees grew luxuriantly; and birds, beasts, fish, and turtles all flourished according to their natures. The effects of responding effectively to change were now manifest, and only now were the hearts of Yao and Shun somewhat at ease. Ask those at court, and they did not know; ask those outside the court, and they did not know. Their failure to know arose because this lay beyond their capacity to comprehend. Their wisdom encompassed all things, and their Way brought benefit to all under Heaven. So vast was it that none could name it; so lofty that even the most abundant virtue could add nothing to it.

I venture to say [?]: in preparing things for use and establishing finished implements for the benefit of all under Heaven, none are greater than the sages. Does this not refer to Yao and Shun? Those who explain their achievement solely in terms of fully realizing one's nature—how could they understand the sagehood of Yao and Shun? Nevertheless, their view cannot be rejected entirely. Fully realizing the goodness of their nature constituted the sagehood of Yao and Shun; responding effectively to change before possibilities were exhausted was what made Yao and Shun sages. To sum up…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之通變之道自盡性始能盡其性夫然後
能盡人物之性可以贊化育參天地矣此
聖人之極功也子思子之說也胡五峯言
外意也堯舜不可及也求可以當是者其
惟我
聖祖高皇帝乎易之革曰文明以說大亨以正
革而當傳曰通其變使民不倦神而化之
謹誦是以對越
在天之靈
===
表
擬宋以李綱爲江西安撫制置大使兼知
洪州謝表
劉喁
同考試官教諭李　批〔麗而有則且不失宋人體製可謂善於四六者録之〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔訓表中能寓忠君愛國之意殆知伯紀之心事者乎〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔麗則可取〕
punctuated:
之，通變之道自盡性始。能盡其性，夫然後能盡人物之性，可以贊化育、參天地矣。此聖人之極功也，子思子之說也，胡五峯言外意也。堯舜不可及也，求可以當是者，其惟我聖祖高皇帝乎！易之革曰：「文明以說，大亨以正，革而當。」傳曰：「通其變，使民不倦，神而化之。」謹誦是以對越在天之靈。

表
擬宋以李綱爲江西安撫制置大使兼知洪州謝表
劉喁
同考試官教諭李批〔麗而有則，且不失宋人體製，可謂善於四六者，録之。〕
考試官訓導吳批〔訓表中能寓忠君愛國之意，殆知伯紀之心事者乎？〕
考試官教諭徐批〔麗則可取。〕
translation_en:
…in sum, the way of comprehending change begins with fully realizing one’s nature. Only after fully realizing one’s own nature can one fully realize the natures of other people and things, assist in the transforming and nourishing processes, and form a triad with Heaven and Earth. This is the sage’s ultimate achievement, the teaching of Master Zisi, and the meaning implicit in Hu Wufeng’s words. Yao and Shun are beyond reach. If we seek someone worthy of this description, could it be any other than our Sagely Progenitor, Emperor Gao? The Changes says of the hexagram Revolution: “Civilized illumination joined with joy; great success through correctness; change that is fitting.” The Commentary says: “Comprehend its changes, so that the people do not grow weary; transform them in a spirit-like manner.” I reverently recite these words to honor his spirit in Heaven.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks in the voice of Li Gang of the Song upon his appointment as Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Military Control of Jiangxi, concurrently Prefect of Hongzhou.
By Liu Yong.
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Elegant yet disciplined, and faithful to the literary form of Song writers. He may be called adept at four-and-six parallel prose. Selected.〕
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Within this memorial [?], he conveys loyalty to the ruler and love of the country. Might he be someone who understands the innermost concerns of Boji [Li Gang]?〕
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔Its elegance and discipline merit selection.〕

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
臣綱言紹興五年某月日荷蒙
詔賜褒諭除臣為江西安撫制置大使兼知
洪州者臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首伏以
寄隆分閫秉二節之嚴崇任重專城固一
方之保障欲副兵民之託須歸文武之才
况逢國步之多艱正若邊隅之告急在吾
肖之經營斯濟雖孔明之籌策猶難詎意
凡庸叨膺
選拔自
===
天申命無地措躬恭惟
○○○○
秦道方隆乾元獨運
聰明建極
知哲能官養德性於純融凝道心於淵靜
恩懷北狩遙瞻朔漠之雲志在中興載揭
神州之日以江西湖東之地近輔臨安念安
撫制置之官宜兼州牧二千石之禄秩儼
斯過矣數千里之封壤才何以堪伏念臣
punctuated:
臣綱言：紹興五年某月日，荷蒙詔賜褒諭，除臣為江西安撫制置大使兼知洪州者。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。伏以寄隆分閫，秉二節之嚴崇；任重專城，固一方之保障。欲副兵民之託，須歸文武之才。况逢國步之多艱，正若邊隅之告急。在吾肖之經營斯濟，雖孔明之籌策猶難。詎意凡庸，叨膺選拔，自天申命，無地措躬。
恭惟○○○○，秦道方隆，乾元獨運，聰明建極，知哲能官。養德性於純融，凝道心於淵靜。恩懷北狩，遙瞻朔漠之雲；志在中興，載揭神州之日。以江西湖東之地近輔臨安，念安撫制置之官宜兼州牧。二千石之禄秩，儼斯過矣；數千里之封壤，才何以堪？伏念臣
translation_en:
Your servant Gang states: On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Shaoxing, I received with gratitude an imperial edict bestowing praise and encouragement and appointing me Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Military Planning in Jiangxi, concurrently Prefect of Hongzhou. In utmost fear and trepidation, I bow my head and knock my forehead upon the ground. I humbly consider that a regional military command is a lofty trust, carrying the solemn dignity of two credentials of authority; sole charge of a prefecture is a weighty responsibility, securing the defenses of an entire region. To fulfill the trust of caring for soldiers and people requires talent in both civil and military affairs. Moreover, the fortunes of the state now face many difficulties, just as urgent alarms arise along the frontiers. Success depends upon management by one such as myself [?], yet even Kongming’s strategic resourcefulness would find this difficult. How could I have imagined that an ordinary mediocrity like me would undeservedly receive selection? With this renewed command descending from Heaven, I can find no place to compose myself.
I respectfully reflect that ○○○○: the Way of Qin [?] is flourishing, and the primal power of Heaven operates alone. Through clear perception you establish the supreme standard; through wisdom you appoint capable officials. You nurture your virtuous nature in purity and harmony and concentrate your moral mind in profound stillness. Your loving concern rests with those on the northern hunt, and you gaze afar toward the clouds over the northern deserts; intent upon dynastic restoration, you raise anew the sun over the Divine Land. Since the lands of Jiangxi and Hudong closely support Lin’an, you consider it fitting that the official responsible for pacification and military planning should also serve as prefect. The salary rank of two thousand shi is assuredly more than I deserve; how could my abilities suffice for a territory extending several thousand li? I humbly consider that I, your servant…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
郡武倅邵之寀儒政和初年之進士歷官
留守薦拜尚書荷
先皇賜以玉帶金魚賴
今上改為宮提舉學曾陳三策防禦即付三省
施行寀
天兵累敗于敵仇恥國恥可雪於昕夕臣謂勿
以將帥屢捷為可賀而當以軍政未備士
氣未振為可虞又謂勿以東南偏處為可
安而思以中原未復外境未寧為可恥臯
===
二帝之還上慰
而請彼河朔轉劉豫而肆諸市朝西迎
伐之威四野勤民期致萬箱之富協岳飛
鴻私寢食不違憂勤是切三時講武大振六
彈駑劣上答
牛桓霸失遠不棄毀蹟之馬也臣敢不下
聖慈曲全愚直是何異齊王愛物過釁鐘之
丹詔忽臨仰荷
囊爾上
punctuated: 郡武倅邵之寀儒，政和初年之進士，歷官留守，薦拜尚書。荷先皇賜以玉帶金魚，賴今上改為宮提舉。學曾陳三策，防禦即付三省施行。寀天兵累敗于敵，仇恥國恥可雪於昕夕。臣謂勿以將帥屢捷為可賀，而當以軍政未備、士氣未振為可虞；又謂勿以東南偏處為可安，而思以中原未復、外境未寧為可恥。臯二帝之還，上慰，而請彼河朔轉劉豫而肆諸市朝，西迎伐之威。四野勤民，期致萬箱之富，協岳飛鴻私，寢食不違，憂勤是切。三時講武，大振六彈駑劣，上答牛桓霸失遠不棄毀蹟之馬也。臣敢不下聖慈曲全愚直，是何異齊王愛物，過釁鐘之丹詔忽臨，仰荷囊爾上。
translation_en:
…[The opening phrase concerning a prefecture, a deputy, and a scholar is garbled: 郡武倅邵之寀儒, ?]. A metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the early Zhenghe era, [I] served successively as Regent and, upon recommendation, was appointed Minister. I received from the late emperor the favor of a jade belt and gold fish ornament, and through the present emperor was reassigned as a palace [temple?] Superintendent. [The text concerning learning is doubtful, ?.] I once submitted three proposals; those concerning defense were immediately referred to the Three Departments for implementation. [An unclear character, 寀, intervenes.] The imperial armies repeatedly suffered defeat at the enemy’s hands; the humiliation inflicted by the enemy and the humiliation of the state could be washed away within a day. Your servant argued that repeated victories by commanders should not be regarded as grounds for celebration; rather, incomplete military administration and unrevived military morale should be regarded as grounds for apprehension. I further argued that occupying a secluded corner of the southeast should not be regarded as grounds for contentment; rather, the Central Plain remaining unrecovered and the outer territories remaining unsettled should be regarded as grounds for shame.

[The ensuing clauses appear garbled and displaced, ?.] The return of the two emperors would console [Your Majesty] above … and [I] requested that, in Heshuo, Liu Yu be transferred and exposed in the marketplace and court [?]; welcoming westward … the might of punitive warfare [?]. Encouraging the people to labor throughout the countryside, [we] would seek the abundance of ten thousand granaries; cooperating with Yue Fei … great personal favor [?]. Neither sleeping nor eating would [I] depart from [this purpose]; anxious diligence was my pressing concern. Practicing warfare in the three seasons, greatly rousing the six … exerting my inferior abilities, to requite above … the ox, Huan’s hegemony, loss and distance, not abandoning the horse whose tracks were ruined [?]. How would your servant dare not … Your Majesty’s compassionate kindness fully preserves my foolish frankness. How does this differ from the King of Qi’s love for living creatures, passing … the consecration of a bell [with blood] …? The vermilion edict suddenly arrived; looking upward, I gratefully received [it]. [The closing phrase 囊爾上 is unclear, ?] …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
九重之想伏願
仁先父子義正華夷以和議為非心毋切於
胥膽以恢復為是夢不忘於枕戈斡乾轉
坤完
宋室之宗社際天薄海覲漢官之威儀臣無任
瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
張□
同考試官教諭楊　批　場中士子於
是題一策多飽飣成文可厭惟此篇論據詳盡蓋腋膺夫
子憲章之教者健哉健哉
同考試官教授陳　批　能發揚我
punctuated:
九重之想。伏願仁先父子，義正華夷；以和議為非，心毋切於胥膽；以恢復為是，夢不忘於枕戈。斡乾轉坤，完宋室之宗社；際天薄海，覲漢官之威儀。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
張□

同考試官教諭楊　批：場中士子於是題一策，多飽飣成文，可厭。惟此篇論據詳盡，蓋腋膺夫子憲章之教者，健哉！健哉！

同考試官教授陳　批：能發揚我
translation_en:
…the thoughts of the Ninefold Palace. I humbly wish that Your Majesty would give precedence in benevolence to the bond between father and son, and through righteousness set right the distinction between the Chinese and the barbarians; regard peace negotiations as wrong, and let your heart not dwell urgently upon “Xu’s gall” [?]; regard restoration as right, and even in dreams never forget to sleep with your spear as your pillow. Turn Heaven and Earth about and preserve intact the Song dynasty’s ancestral temples and altars of state. To the bounds of heaven and the shores of the seas, let all behold the imposing ceremonial bearing of Han officialdom. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sageliness, cannot contain his intense emotion and utmost trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zhang □

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Among the candidates in the examination hall, many, in their policy essays on this question, have served up a surfeit of ready-made writing: tiresome indeed. This essay alone is thorough in its arguments and supporting evidence. Its author surely takes to heart [?] the Master’s teaching to follow the exemplary institutions of the ancient rulers. Vigorous indeed! Vigorous indeed!

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Professor: He is able to expound and bring glory to our…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖製作之盛可嘉
聖祖製作如雲漢昭回丹青炳若子能伏讀而詳陳之其不虛
考試官訓導吳　批　我
生于太平之世者與
考試官教諭徐　批　士子多為世業所溺而子
能條答殆盡蓋亦卓有定見者與
有帝王之大學術有帝王之大製作學術
其本也製作其末也使學而不原諸心則
徒事口耳之贅而非學之大文而不本於
===
心則何以為大製作而經緯乎天地哉是
故精一執中典謨所以成於堯舜建中建
極訓誥所以作於湯武自是以後此道經
闕漢高祖大風之歌唐文皇威鳳之賦非
藝祖日出之句詞藝雖工於治無補而所
謂心學者漠乎未之聞也他尚何望哉我
太祖高皇帝挺生南服混一區宇
天才英邁
聖質純穆屛聲色之好絕遊畋之娛幾務之暇
punctuated:
聖祖製作之盛，可嘉。
聖祖製作，如雲漢昭回，丹青炳若。子能伏讀而詳陳之，其不虛。
考試官訓導吳，批：我生于太平之世者與！
考試官教諭徐，批：士子多為世業所溺，而子能條答殆盡，蓋亦卓有定見者與！
有帝王之大學術，有帝王之大製作。學術，其本也；製作，其末也。使學而不原諸心，則徒事口耳之贅，而非學之大；文而不本於心，則何以為大製作，而經緯乎天地哉？是故精一執中，典謨所以成於堯舜；建中建極，訓誥所以作於湯武。自是以後，此道經闕。漢高祖大風之歌，唐文皇威鳳之賦，非藝祖日出之句，詞藝雖工，於治無補，而所謂心學者，漠乎未之聞也。他尚何望哉？我太祖高皇帝，挺生南服，混一區宇，天才英邁，聖質純穆，屛聲色之好，絕遊畋之娛，幾務之暇
translation_en:
…the magnificence of the sagely ancestor’s compositions: commendable.
The sagely ancestor’s compositions shine like the celestial River of Stars and glow like brilliant pigments. You have reverently read them and expounded them in detail; surely this has not been in vain [?].
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “I am one born into an age of peace!” [? The transcription appears to displace this attribution and part of the preceding sentence.]
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Candidates are often submerged in their inherited professional studies, yet you have answered point by point, covering almost everything. Surely you possess outstandingly firm judgments of your own!”
There is the great learning of emperors and kings, and there are their great compositions. Learning is the root; compositions are its branches. If learning does not originate in the mind, it merely pursues the superfluities of hearing and recitation, and is not learning in its greatness. If writing is not grounded in the mind, how can it constitute great compositions that give order to Heaven and Earth? Thus, refinement and single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean, brought forth the Canons and Counsels under Yao and Shun; establishing the mean and the supreme standard brought forth the Instructions and Announcements under Tang and Wu. Thereafter, this Way suffered interruption [?]. Han Gaozu’s Song of the Great Wind, Tang Emperor Wen’s Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix, and Yizu’s lines on the rising sun [?]: although accomplished in literary artistry, they contributed nothing to governance. As for what is called the learning of the mind, they had scarcely heard of it. What further hopes could one have?
Our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, arose with exceptional distinction in the southern regions and unified the realm. His natural gifts were outstanding, his sagely disposition pure and serene. He rejected indulgence in music and women and renounced the pleasures of excursions and hunting. In the intervals between affairs of state…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
未嘗不游心乎道學存志乎詩書故其涵
養沖虛造詣純粹足以繼精一執中之傳
發爲
宸翰奎章雄深宏偉可以追典謨訓誥之作愚
嘗莊誦
御製文集而粗得其宏綱大旨矣如
即位之詔則建
國號改正朔以布告天下
皇陵之碑則述艱難明昌運以垂訓後人大祀
===
禮成則曰國家以祀禮爲先祀禮以敬誠
爲本所以勅諭夫中書者切矣丞相除拜
則曰當上美
皇天之昭鑒下契黔黎之仰瞻所以懋迪真功
業者至矣籌謀安民察奸料敵之語簡截
於閱江樓之記則非事遊觀也彝倫攸敘
燮理陰陽之言旁引於遊新菴之記則非
崇異端也至於感舊而征特叙其時艱阻
興之事不得已用兵之故何明正那抗湯
punctuated: 未嘗不游心乎道學，存志乎詩書，故其涵養沖虛，造詣純粹，足以繼精一執中之傳。發爲宸翰奎章，雄深宏偉，可以追典謨訓誥之作。愚嘗莊誦御製文集，而粗得其宏綱大旨矣。如即位之詔，則建國號，改正朔，以布告天下；皇陵之碑，則述艱難，明昌運，以垂訓後人。大祀禮成，則曰：「國家以祀禮爲先，祀禮以敬誠爲本。」所以勅諭夫中書者切矣。丞相除拜，則曰：「當上美皇天之昭鑒，下契黔黎之仰瞻。」所以懋迪真功業者至矣。籌謀安民、察奸料敵之語，簡截於閱江樓之記，則非事遊觀也；彝倫攸敘、燮理陰陽之言，旁引於遊新菴之記，則非崇異端也。至於感舊而征，特叙其時艱阻興之事、不得已用兵之故，何明正那？抗湯
translation_en:
…he never failed to immerse his mind in the learning of the Way and set his aspirations upon the Odes and Documents. Thus his self-cultivation was serene and free of self, and his attainments pure, sufficient to continue the transmission of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the Mean. Expressed in imperial writings of celestial brilliance, these qualities became majestic, profound, expansive, and grand, worthy of emulating the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents. I have reverently recited the Collection of Imperial Writings and gained a rough understanding of its broad outlines and principal meaning.
