For example, the edict of accession established the dynastic name and changed the calendrical reckoning, proclaiming these to all under Heaven. The inscription for the imperial mausoleum recounted hardships and made manifest the dynasty’s flourishing destiny, leaving instruction for later generations. Upon completion of the great sacrificial rites, he declared: “The state gives precedence to sacrificial rites; sacrificial rites take reverence and sincerity as their foundation.” How earnest was his admonition to the Central Secretariat! Upon appointing grand councilors, he declared: “Above, you should honor August Heaven’s luminous scrutiny; below, you should fulfill the expectations of the common people who look up to you.” How thorough was his encouragement and guidance toward genuine achievement!

His words about devising plans to bring peace to the people, detecting treachery, and assessing enemies are succinctly expressed in the Record of Yuejiang Tower: this was no mere pursuit of sightseeing. His words about the proper ordering of human relationships and the harmonizing of yin and yang are broadly adduced in the Record of a Visit to Xin’an Hermitage: this was no exaltation of heterodox teachings. As for recalling the past and campaigning [?], he specifically recounted the hardships of the time and the circumstances of his rise [?], and the reasons he had no choice but to employ troops. How lucid and correct [?]! The passage concerning Tang [?]…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
水旱讒井災間見於累年其說足以破千
古之疑秋宇澄清惟極陰陽交姤之理其
說可以契六經之旨至於黃河良馬必詳
其地里狹直三功八弊之事何詳悉邪昔
露時雪形諸論議蓋覩禎祥而知憂懼處
富貴而思貧賤之心也豈流連光景之謂
乎夫時聖學發為策問慮水旱之傷五穀
念古昔以懷聖賢之意也其詢於芻蕘之
見乎乃若憫旱祈豐仁民愛物之情寓於
===
神龍丹芝嘉瓜之贊非好異也觀人用人
脩德善終之諭形於萌賢啓忠書顏之文
非驕矜也孝慈錄之定喪禮四瀆遷行照
聖錄之示
親三萬世遵守以至建言格式之示羣臣莫
不有序以敷宣其旨焉讀流金飲露之詞
則知鶯囀之賦麗而則誦汗漫汪洋之句
則知四瀆之賦偉而奇本之於精神心術
之微發之於議論文字之著一言之約與
punctuated:
水旱讒井災間見於累年，其說足以破千古之疑。《秋宇澄清》，惟極陰陽交姤之理，其說可以契六經之旨。至於《黃河》《良馬》，必詳其地里狹直、三功八弊之事，何詳悉邪！昔露時雪，形諸論議，蓋覩禎祥而知憂懼，處富貴而思貧賤之心也，豈流連光景之謂乎！夫時聖學，發為策問，慮水旱之傷五穀，念古昔以懷聖賢之意也，其詢於芻蕘之見乎！乃若憫旱祈豐，仁民愛物之情，寓於《神龍》《丹芝》《嘉瓜》之贊，非好異也；觀人用人，脩德善終之諭，形於萌賢啓忠書顏之文，非驕矜也。
《孝慈錄》之定喪禮，四瀆遷行，《照聖錄》之示親三萬世遵守，以至《建言格式》之示羣臣，莫不有序以敷宣其旨焉。讀流金飲露之詞，則知《鶯囀》之賦麗而則；誦汗漫汪洋之句，則知《四瀆》之賦偉而奇。本之於精神心術之微，發之於議論文字之著，一言之約與
translation_en:
…Floods, droughts, and other calamities [?] appeared intermittently over successive years; his explanation suffices to dispel doubts of a thousand ages. In “The Clear Autumn Sky,” he fully explores the principle by which yin and yang encounter one another; his explanation accords with the purport of the Six Classics. As for “The Yellow River” and “Fine Horses,” he invariably details such matters as geographical extent, narrowness and straightness, and the three benefits and eight drawbacks. How exhaustive his treatment is! Dew and timely snow [?] find expression in his discussions: these reveal a heart that, on seeing auspicious signs, knows anxiety and apprehension, and, amid wealth and honor, thinks of poverty and lowliness. How could this be called mere lingering over beautiful scenery? His sagely learning at such times [?] finds expression in policy questions. He worries that floods and droughts will damage the five grains, and reflects upon antiquity with the sages and worthies in mind. Is this not his seeking the views even of grass-cutters and wood-gatherers? Likewise, his compassion in times of drought, his prayers for abundant harvests, and his benevolence toward the people and care for all creatures are embodied in the eulogies “Divine Dragon,” “Vermilion Auspicious Fungus,” and “Excellent Melon”; these do not express a fondness for marvels. His admonitions on judging and employing men, cultivating virtue, and ending well appear in writings concerning encouraging the worthy, awakening loyalty, and inscribing Yan [?]; these do not express arrogance or conceit.
The Record of Filial Piety and Parental Kindness establishes mourning rites; the passage concerning the Four Waterways and removal or implementation is unclear [?]. The Record of Illuminating Sageliness [?] is shown to the imperial princes [?] for observance through ten thousand generations, while the Regulations for Submitting Proposals are shown to the assembled ministers. Each has a preface expounding its purpose. Reading the phrases about flowing gold and drinking dew, one recognizes that the rhapsody “The Oriole’s Warbling” is ornate yet exemplary; reciting the lines of boundless, oceanic breadth, one recognizes that the rhapsody “The Four Waterways” is magnificent and extraordinary. Rooted in the subtle workings of spirit and mind, these find manifest expression in argument and writing. The brevity of a single utterance and…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
肯存焉千言之富渾義寓焉
天葩麗藻照耀簡冊誠與日月並其輝光風雲
同其變化韶濩協其節奏河嶽同其高崇
同視漢唐宋諸君之作蓋不啻霄壤矣是
以翰林學士宋濂等敬錄以成編學士承
旨詹同等固請其鋟梓誠意伯劉基序之
于前而極其揄揚起居郭傳序之于後而
極其贊述也雖然此特
聖製之見於文集者然爾他如
===
皇明祖訓以著一代之家法諸司職掌以貽一
代之治典
大明集禮以備一代之儀文
大明律令以定一代之刑制育才有臥碑之條
教民有榜文之布恤軍士有條例之頒嚴
釋老有清教之錄
大誥三編之作
洪武禮制之脩洪範之註資世之訓立法貽謀
不一而足若此者何莫不本於我
punctuated: 肯存焉，千言之富，渾義寓焉。天葩麗藻，照耀簡冊，誠與日月並其輝光，風雲同其變化，韶濩協其節奏，河嶽同其高崇。同視漢唐宋諸君之作，蓋不啻霄壤矣。是以翰林學士宋濂等敬錄以成編，學士承旨詹同等固請其鋟梓，誠意伯劉基序之于前而極其揄揚，起居郭傳序之于後而極其贊述也。雖然，此特聖製之見於文集者然爾。他如《皇明祖訓》以著一代之家法，《諸司職掌》以貽一代之治典，《大明集禮》以備一代之儀文，《大明律令》以定一代之刑制，育才有臥碑之條，教民有榜文之布，恤軍士有條例之頒，嚴釋老有清教之錄，《大誥》三編之作，《洪武禮制》之脩，《洪範》之註，《資世》之訓，立法貽謀，不一而足。若此者，何莫不本於我
translation_en:
…the essential point is preserved therein [?]; in the abundance of a thousand words, comprehensive meaning resides [?]. These heavenly blossoms and splendid compositions illuminate the written records. Truly, their brilliance equals that of the sun and moon; their transformations match those of winds and clouds; their rhythms accord with the Shao and Huo ceremonial music; and their loftiness equals that of rivers and mountains. Compared with the writings of the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song [?], the difference is indeed greater than that between heaven and earth. Thus Song Lian and other Hanlin Academicians reverently transcribed them into a collection. Zhan Tong and other Academicians-in-Waiting earnestly requested that they be carved on printing blocks. Liu Ji, Earl of Chengyi, supplied a preface offering the fullest praise, while Guo Chuan, the Imperial Diarist, supplied a postface offering the fullest commendation. Yet these are merely the imperial compositions found in the literary collection.

Other works include the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming, which set forth the dynasty’s household rules; the Duties of the Various Offices, which bequeathed a code of administration for the dynasty; the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming, which provided its ceremonial forms; and the Laws and Ordinances of the Great Ming, which established its penal institutions. For nurturing talent there were the provisions of the Recumbent Stele; for instructing the people, posted proclamations; for caring for soldiers, promulgated regulations; and for strictly regulating Buddhism and Daoism, the Record of the Purification of the Teachings. There were also the composition of the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements, the compilation of the Ritual Institutions of the Hongwu Reign, the commentary on the Great Plan, and the instructions of Aid to the World [?]. His establishment of laws and provision of plans for posterity were too numerous to enumerate. Of such works, which did not have its source in our …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖心學之所發哉與時偕曰人之一心檢持
甚難朕覺此心如兩敵然時時防閑尚未
能也則其用功於心學槩可見矣
聖子
神孫是訓是則述哉
皇上繼體守成益篤
前烈寫懷之詩寓對時育物之仁會典之序
盡繼志述事之孝
廷臣之頒賜中外之梓行蓋已人誦而家傳
===
矣繇是而因文以考德則
聖祖之心學可法也繇是而立政以圖治則
聖祖之典謨具在也草茅賤士有懷맛欲揄揚
揚厲有不能盡焉者惟執事進而教之
第二問
同考試官學正魏　批　〔策論心學正所以見我〕
國家一統之盛世答詳盡無遺而不徒以無益無用為訓其忠愛
之意溢於□□表不獨其文之佳也取為何辭
punctuated:
聖祖心學之所發哉！與時偕曰：「人之一心，檢持甚難。朕覺此心如兩敵然，時時防閑，尚未能也。」則其用功於心學，槩可見矣。聖子神孫，是訓是則，述哉！皇上繼體守成，益篤前烈。寫懷之詩，寓對時育物之仁；會典之序，盡繼志述事之孝。廷臣之頒賜，中外之梓行，蓋已人誦而家傳矣。繇是而因文以考德，則聖祖之心學可法也；繇是而立政以圖治，則聖祖之典謨具在也。草茅賤士，有懷맛欲揄揚揚厲，有不能盡焉者，惟執事進而教之。
第二問
同考試官學正魏　批：〔策論心學，正所以見我〕國家一統之盛世。答詳盡無遺，而不徒以無益無用為訓，其忠愛之意溢於□□表，不獨其文之佳也。取為何辭？
translation_en:
…the expression of our sagely founder’s learning of the mind! Keeping pace with the times [?], he said: “The human mind is exceedingly difficult to restrain and maintain. We feel that this mind is like two opposing enemies. Even with constant vigilance, We have not yet succeeded.” From this one can broadly discern the effort he devoted to the learning of the mind. His sagely sons and divine grandsons took this as their instruction and model: how they carried on his legacy! His Majesty has inherited the throne and preserved its achievements, further strengthening the glorious accomplishments of his predecessors. His poem “Expressing My Thoughts” embodies the benevolence of responding to the seasons and nurturing all things; his preface to the Collected Statutes fully expresses the filial devotion of continuing his forebears’ intentions and carrying forward their undertakings. Bestowed upon court officials and printed for circulation within and beyond the capital, these writings are already recited by everyone and transmitted in every household. Thus, if we examine virtue through these writings, the learning of the mind of our sagely founder offers a model to follow; if we establish government in pursuit of good order, his institutions and counsels are all there. I, a humble scholar of the countryside, harbor the desire [?] to extol and celebrate them, yet there is much I cannot fully express. I ask only that you, honored examiners, encourage and instruct me.
Second Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, an Instructor: 〔This policy essay discusses the learning of the mind precisely in order to reveal our〕 state’s flourishing age of unified rule. The answer is thorough and leaves nothing out, and its admonitions are not merely unprofitable and impractical. Its spirit of loyalty and love overflows beyond the □□ [?]; its merit lies in more than fine writing alone. What objection could there be to selecting it?

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導吳　批〔國家一統之盛薄海內外悉主悉臣迥高千古良以聖祖之有 我〕
〔道也此篇能鋪張揚厲之其亦迥出諸作者乎〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔此深荅我〕
朝
〔列聖柔遠之仁御夷之道鋪張殆盡足以覘吾子宏裕之才雄〕
〔博之學矣〕
讀仁者無敵之言則知我
國家得天下之正誦王者無外之說則知我
===
祖宗待夷狄之心蓋三代得天下以仁而
國家亦以仁此其所以無敵也王者馭夷狄
有道而
祖宗亦有道此其所以無外也是以百餘年來
溪蠻海夷文身卉服靡不來庭與國之廣
一統之盛自三代以還皆未有如我
國家者也然則
今日之所以守成業而致盛治者又豈外於
此仁此道也哉請因明問而敬陳之若朝
punctuated:
考試官訓導吳，批〔國家一統之盛，薄海內外，悉主悉臣，迥高千古，良以聖祖之有 我〕〔道也。此篇能鋪張揚厲之，其亦迥出諸作者乎！〕

考試官教諭徐，批〔此深荅我〕朝〔列聖柔遠之仁、御夷之道，鋪張殆盡，足以覘吾子宏裕之才、雄博之學矣。〕

讀仁者無敵之言，則知我國家得天下之正；誦王者無外之說，則知我祖宗待夷狄之心。蓋三代得天下以仁，而國家亦以仁，此其所以無敵也。王者馭夷狄有道，而祖宗亦有道，此其所以無外也。是以百餘年來，溪蠻海夷，文身卉服，靡不來庭。與國之廣、一統之盛，自三代以還，皆未有如我國家者也。然則今日之所以守成業而致盛治者，又豈外於此仁、此道也哉？請因明問而敬陳之。若朝
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“Such is the grandeur of the realm’s unification that throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, all acknowledge its ruler and become his subjects. It far surpasses all antiquity, truly because the Sagely Founder possessed the Way [?].〕〔This essay expounds and celebrates this achievement; does it not likewise far surpass the other compositions!”〕

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔“This profoundly answers concerning our〕 dynasty’s 〔successive sage sovereigns—their benevolence in cherishing distant peoples and their way of governing the barbarians. Its exposition is nearly exhaustive, sufficient to reveal your capacious talent and your formidable and extensive learning.”〕

Reading the saying ‘The benevolent have no enemies,’ we recognize the righteousness with which our dynasty gained All under Heaven; reciting the teaching ‘The true king regards none as outside his realm,’ we recognize the intentions with which our imperial ancestors treated the barbarians. The Three Dynasties gained All under Heaven through benevolence, and our dynasty likewise did so through benevolence: this is why it has no enemies. True kings had a proper way of governing the barbarians, and our imperial ancestors likewise had such a way: this is why none are regarded as outside their realm. Thus, for more than a hundred years, the Man of the mountain streams and the Yi of the seas, with tattooed bodies and garments of plant fibers, have all come to court. In the extent of its allied states [?] and the grandeur of its unification, nothing since the Three Dynasties has equaled our dynasty. How, then, could the means by which we preserve the inherited achievement and bring about flourishing government today lie outside this benevolence and this Way? Allow me respectfully to set forth my views in response to your illuminating question. As for Chao…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
詳初爲箕子之國其主表賀即位則賜以
金印誥命而封高麗國王女直古爲肅慎
之地其主悉境歸附乃建置都司衛所而
皆給與印信古倭奴爲日本之國遣使朝
貢而累受冊封麗麗與爲琉球之國嘗分
爲三而貢獻不絕西蕃即吐蕃也置五衛
門而建官賜印赤斤古西戎也率男婦来
歸而賜以印誥罕東衛出於西戎部落而
有冠帶鈔幣之頒安定衛出於韃靼別部
===
而有鎧甲刀劍之獻哈密乃古伊吾廬之
地改設爲衛而封爲忠順王火州城乃漢
時車師之地遣使朝貢而屢獻馬璞諸物
員外郎陳誠之使其國則亦刀把力也鄯
剌哈非思之貢駝馬則撒馬兒罕也在哈
烈則遣使詔諭而賜織金文綺在于闐則
遣使来朝而貢玉璞諸寶至若古南交之
地非今之安南國乎其主率先歸附因鄰
縣其地而尋復廢之古有越裳氏非今之
punctuated: 詳初爲箕子之國，其主表賀即位，則賜以金印、誥命，而封高麗國王。女直古爲肅慎之地，其主悉境歸附，乃建置都司、衛所，而皆給與印信。古倭奴爲日本之國，遣使朝貢，而累受冊封。麗麗與爲琉球之國，嘗分爲三，而貢獻不絕。西蕃即吐蕃也，置五衛門，而建官賜印。赤斤古西戎也，率男婦来歸，而賜以印誥。罕東衛出於西戎部落，而有冠帶、鈔幣之頒。安定衛出於韃靼別部，而有鎧甲、刀劍之獻。哈密乃古伊吾廬之地，改設爲衛，而封爲忠順王。火州城乃漢時車師之地，遣使朝貢，而屢獻馬璞諸物。員外郎陳誠之使其國，則亦刀把力也。鄯剌哈非思之貢駝馬，則撒馬兒罕也。在哈烈，則遣使詔諭，而賜織金文綺；在于闐，則遣使来朝，而貢玉璞諸寶。至若古南交之地，非今之安南國乎？其主率先歸附，因鄰縣其地，而尋復廢之。古有越裳氏，非今之
translation_en:
…[Chaoxian, or Korea?] was originally the country of Jizi. When its ruler submitted a memorial congratulating the emperor on his accession, he was granted a gold seal and a patent of appointment and invested as King of Gaoli. Nüzhi occupied the ancient territory of Sushen. Its ruler submitted with his entire territory, whereupon a Regional Military Commission, guards, and battalions were established, all furnished with official seals. Ancient Wonu became the country of Riben. It sent envoys to present tribute and repeatedly received formal investiture. “Liliyu” [?] became the country of Liuqiu, which was once divided into three, yet its tribute offerings never ceased. Xifan is Tubo: five guards [?] were established there, officials appointed, and seals bestowed. Chijin belonged to the ancient Western Rong. Its leader brought men and women to submit and was granted a seal and a patent. Handong Guard originated among the Western Rong tribes and received grants of caps and girdles, paper currency, and silks. Anding Guard originated from a separate branch of the Dada and presented armor, sabers, and swords.

Hami occupies the ancient territory of Yiwulu. It was reorganized as a guard, and its ruler was invested as the Prince of Loyalty and Obedience. Huozhou city occupies the territory of Cheshi in Han times. It sent envoys to present tribute and repeatedly offered horses, unworked jade, and other goods. The country to which Vice Director Chen Cheng went as envoy was Yidaobali [?]. The country from which Shanla Hafeisi presented camels and horses was Sama’erhan. In the case of Halie, envoys were dispatched to proclaim an imperial edict, and figured silks woven with gold were bestowed. In the case of Yutian, it sent envoys to court and offered unworked jade and other precious objects. As for the ancient territory of Nanjiao, is it not the present country of Annan? Its ruler took the lead in submitting; its territory was consequently organized into prefectures and counties [?], but this arrangement was soon abolished. In antiquity there was the Yueshang people: are they not today’s …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
占城國乎其主遣使来朝因詔封爲王而
至今如故有因朝貢而詔賜大統曆列女
傳者暹羅國也因来朝而納元所授宣勑
二道者非八哇國乎自率其妻子来朝卒
於南京而詔謚恭順者浡泥國也各率其
妻子頭目来朝而并貢方物者非蘇祿國
乎瑣里國遣使進金字表而并獻其山川
地圖榜葛剌遣使来朝而并獻其麒麟寶
物其他偏方小國輸琛納貢者又不可以
縷數其時則肪於洪武永樂之年其事則
===
載於
大明一統之誌視諸古昔西戎之獻白雉之獻
肅慎氏矢之貢殆同一轍矣是豈我
國家好大喜功勤兵黷武以來遠人之歸哉
蓋我
太祖高皇帝以神武之資乘炎精之運龍飛淮
甸奄有區夏
太宗文皇帝志靖邦家肅清内難建都上游以
punctuated:
占城國乎？其主遣使来朝，因詔封爲王，而至今如故。有因朝貢而詔賜《大統曆》《列女傳》者，暹羅國也。因来朝而納元所授宣勑二道者，非八哇國乎？自率其妻子来朝，卒於南京，而詔謚恭順者，浡泥國也。各率其妻子頭目来朝，而并貢方物者，非蘇祿國乎？瑣里國遣使進金字表，而并獻其山川地圖；榜葛剌遣使来朝，而并獻其麒麟寶物。其他偏方小國輸琛納貢者，又不可以縷數。其時則肪於洪武、永樂之年，其事則載於《大明一統之誌》。視諸古昔西戎之獻、白雉之獻、肅慎氏矢之貢，殆同一轍矣。是豈我國家好大喜功，勤兵黷武，以來遠人之歸哉？
蓋我太祖高皇帝以神武之資，乘炎精之運，龍飛淮甸，奄有區夏。太宗文皇帝志靖邦家，肅清内難，建都上游，以
translation_en:
…the kingdom of Zhancheng? Its ruler sent envoys to court and was accordingly enfeoffed as king by imperial decree; this arrangement has remained unchanged to the present. It was the kingdom of Xianluo that, upon presenting tribute at court, was granted by imperial decree the Grand Concordance Calendar and the Biographies of Exemplary Women. Was it not the kingdom of Bawa [?] that, upon coming to court, surrendered two patents of instruction previously bestowed by the Yuan? It was the kingdom of Boni whose ruler personally brought his wife and children to court, died in Nanjing, and was granted the posthumous title Gongshun, “Respectful and Obedient,” by imperial decree. Was it not the kingdom of Sulu whose rulers each brought their wives, children, and chieftains to court, together with tribute of local products? The kingdom of Suoli sent envoys to present a memorial written in gold characters, together with a map of its mountains and rivers. Banggela sent envoys to court, presenting a qilin and precious objects. The other small kingdoms in remote regions that delivered treasures and presented tribute are too numerous to enumerate individually. These events occurred [?] during the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, and their particulars are recorded in the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming. Compared with the ancient offerings of the Western Rong, the presentation of white pheasants, and the Sushen people's tribute of arrows, they followed virtually the same pattern. Could it have been because our dynasty delighted in grandeur and coveted achievements, exhausting its armies and recklessly resorting to war, that it induced distant peoples to submit?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed with divine martial prowess and borne along by the destiny of the essence of fire, rose like a dragon in the Huai region and came to possess all the Chinese realm. Emperor Taizong Wen resolved to bring peace to the state, quelled internal troubles, and established the capital in a strategically commanding region, in order to…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
扼三邊之吭
列祖相承益隆繼述其始也除殘去暴仁恩覆
冒於海隅其後也内脩外攘德威覃布於
天下故九夷八蠻自梯山航海而至當時
玉璞麒麟之受非寶遠物也所以嘉納其
獻誥印冠幣之賜非市私恩也所以繫屬
其心方今
聖明在上六合同春四夷向背蓋有不足爲重
輕者顧吾所以自治者何如爾必其來也
===
不拒豈其廉觚厚其賞賚以酬其向化之
誠其去也勿追謹其斥堠嚴其封守以防
其譎詐之變干戚抱羽之賢選舞干
房之略養牧收牧之銳守元國萬金之
謀而又脩德立政仁義兼施如此則□□
祖宗基業之盛永保於億萬年矣傳曰王者不
治夷狄書曰無怠無荒四夷來王愚敢請
焉
punctuated: 扼三邊之吭。列祖相承，益隆繼述。其始也，除殘去暴，仁恩覆冒於海隅；其後也，内脩外攘，德威覃布於天下。故九夷八蠻，自梯山航海而至。當時玉璞麒麟之受，非寶遠物也，所以嘉納其獻；誥印冠幣之賜，非市私恩也，所以繫屬其心。方今聖明在上，六合同春，四夷向背，蓋有不足爲重輕者，顧吾所以自治者何如爾。必其來也不拒，豈其廉觚，厚其賞賚，以酬其向化之誠；其去也勿追，謹其斥堠，嚴其封守，以防其譎詐之變。干戚抱羽之賢，選舞干房之略，養牧收牧之銳，守元國萬金之謀，而又脩德立政，仁義兼施，如此則□□祖宗基業之盛，永保於億萬年矣。傳曰：「王者不治夷狄。」書曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」愚敢請焉。
translation_en:
…to hold the three frontier regions by the throat. Successive imperial ancestors inherited this undertaking, ever more fully carrying forward their predecessors’ achievements. At the outset, they eliminated the cruel and violent, and their humane beneficence sheltered even the remotest coastal regions. Thereafter, they cultivated good government within and repelled threats without, spreading their virtue and might throughout the realm. Thus the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples came, scaling mountains and crossing seas. The acceptance of unworked jade and qilin at that time did not mean that exotic objects were prized; it graciously acknowledged their offerings. The bestowal of patents, seals, caps, and silks did not purchase personal gratitude; it bound their hearts in allegiance.

Now our sage and enlightened sovereign reigns above, and all beneath heaven share the spring. Whether the peoples of the four quarters turn toward us or away is hardly sufficient to determine our fortunes. What matters is how we govern ourselves. When they come, we must not reject them; [the phrase concerning their integrity and principles is doubtful: 豈其廉觚]. We should reward them generously to acknowledge their sincerity in turning toward our civilizing influence. When they leave, we should not pursue them. We should exercise care over our reconnaissance posts and maintain strict frontier defenses to guard against sudden acts of deceit. [The following passage is garbled:] worthy men associated with shields, axes, and holding feathers; selecting the strategy of “dancing with shields” and “chambers”; nurturing the fighting strength of “herding and gathering herds”; preserving the “prime state” and a plan worth ten thousand in gold [?]. Furthermore, we should cultivate virtue and establish good government, applying benevolence and righteousness together. In this way, [two illegible characters] the flourishing foundations laid by our imperial ancestors will be preserved for countless ages.

The Commentary says: “The true king does not govern the Yi and Di.” The Book of Documents says: “Be neither idle nor neglectful, and the peoples of the four quarters will come to acknowledge you as king.” I humbly venture to urge this.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第三問
陳文昭
同考試官教諭李　批〔聖賢心學之說故有定論此策能一一陳之剖析詳盡其有得於心學者與他日經綸事業必有出于此也〕
考試官訓導吳　批〔心學最難言此篇剖析明白殆嘗用心是學者〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔心學淵源人所難言者此作略答詳明一洗塲中之腐說蓋嘗有得於心〕
===
學者矣殆非贅于口耳者歟
論心之說莫備於古昔不能無異也學者當
自異而求其同治心之法莫要於古昔不能
皆同也學者當自同而辨其異何也千聖
一心也心同矣宜其論心之皆同間有不
同者言各有攸當爾萬古一道也道同矣
宜其治心之皆同間有不同者見或有所
偏爾學者於此能自異而求其同自同而
辨其異則趨向之機既審而造詣之階可
punctuated:
第三問。
陳文昭。
同考試官教諭李，批〔聖賢心學之說，故有定論。此策能一一陳之，剖析詳盡，其有得於心學者與？他日經綸事業，必有出于此也。〕
考試官訓導吳，批〔心學最難言，此篇剖析明白，殆嘗用心是學者。〕
考試官教諭徐，批〔心學淵源，人所難言者。此作略答詳明，一洗塲中之腐說，蓋嘗有得於心〕學者矣，殆非贅于口耳者歟？
論心之說，莫備於古昔，不能無異也。學者當自異而求其同。治心之法，莫要於古昔，不能皆同也。學者當自同而辨其異。何也？千聖一心也，心同矣，宜其論心之皆同，間有不同者，言各有攸當爾。萬古一道也，道同矣，宜其治心之皆同，間有不同者，見或有所偏爾。學者於此，能自異而求其同，自同而辨其異，則趨向之機既審，而造詣之階可
translation_en:
Third Question
Chen Wenzhao

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The teachings of the sages and worthies on learning of the mind have, of course, established interpretations. This policy essay sets them out one by one, analyzing them thoroughly and exhaustively. Has its author perhaps gained an understanding of learning of the mind? His future achievements in ordering affairs will surely spring from this.”

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Learning of the mind is exceedingly difficult to discuss. This essay analyzes it clearly; its author has probably devoted himself to this learning.”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The origins and transmission of learning of the mind are difficult for people to discuss. This work offers a concise yet detailed and clear answer, sweeping away the stale pronouncements of the examination hall. Its author has evidently gained an understanding of learning of the mind; surely his learning is more than idle words passing between mouth and ear?”

No discussions of the mind are more comprehensive than those of antiquity, yet they cannot be without differences. Students should seek what is common within those differences. No methods of governing the mind are more essential than those of antiquity, yet they cannot all be alike. Students should distinguish their differences within what they share. Why is this? A thousand sages share one mind. Since their minds are the same, their discussions of the mind should all agree. Where they occasionally differ, it is simply because each statement addresses its particular circumstances. Throughout all antiquity there is one Way. Since the Way is the same, their governing of the mind should all agree. Where they occasionally differ, it is simply because their views may be partial. If students can here seek what is common within differences and distinguish differences within what is shared, they will have clearly discerned the crucial point in choosing their direction, and the steps toward attainment may …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
得以是而折天下之理則異同之似舉不
足爲吾惑矣請因明問而縱言之人之身
孰爲大曰心爲大人之學孰爲要曰治心
爲要宜古人亟以爲言而孰事以是業諸
聖學也惜乎心齋坐忘跡之顏子之自得
而近裏著己復愢程子之訓辭無味之言
何足以塵清聽哉雖然言及之而不言可
乎粵自堯之授舜既以允執厥中相訓飭
矣而復繹之以人心道心之言以發明之
===
蘊也以其原於性命之正則名以道心盖
子之所指良心本心得非道心之云乎以
其生於形氣之私則名以人心問程之所
指欲心私心得非人心之云乎易曰復其
見天地之心盖陰極而陽生剝極而復來
天地生物之心著矣是吾之心即天地之
心也傳曰大人者不失其赤子之心盖純
一而無偽擴充而無間大人正己之功成
矣是吾之心即赤子之心也他如心經之
punctuated:
得。以是而折天下之理，則異同之似，舉不足爲吾惑矣。請因明問而縱言之。人之身孰爲大？曰：心爲大。人之學孰爲要？曰：治心爲要。宜古人亟以爲言，而孰事以是業諸聖學也。惜乎心齋坐忘，跡之顏子之自得，而近裏著己，復愢程子之訓辭。無味之言，何足以塵清聽哉？雖然，言及之而不言，可乎？
粵自堯之授舜，既以允執厥中相訓飭矣，而復繹之以人心道心之言，以發明之蘊也。以其原於性命之正，則名以道心。盖子之所指良心、本心，得非道心之云乎？以其生於形氣之私，則名以人心。問程之所指欲心、私心，得非人心之云乎？《易》曰：「復，其見天地之心。」盖陰極而陽生，剝極而復來，天地生物之心著矣。是吾之心，即天地之心也。傳曰：「大人者，不失其赤子之心。」盖純一而無偽，擴充而無間，大人正己之功成矣。是吾之心，即赤子之心也。他如《心經》之
translation_en:
…can be attained. By using this to adjudicate the principles of all things under Heaven, apparent similarities and differences will no longer be enough to bewilder us. Allow me to discuss this at length in response to your illuminating question. What is greatest in a person? The heart-mind. What is most essential in learning? Governing the heart-mind. It is fitting that the ancients repeatedly spoke of this and made it their undertaking in the learning of the sages [?]. Regrettably, “fasting the heart-mind” and “sitting in forgetfulness” are traced to Master Yan’s personal attainment, while “turning inward and applying oneself personally” again invokes Master Cheng’s admonitions [?]. How could such insipid words merit troubling your discerning ears? Nevertheless, since the subject has been raised, can I leave it unaddressed?
When Yao transmitted rule to Shun, he instructed and admonished him with the words “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” This was further expounded through statements about the human heart-mind and the heart-mind of the Way, elucidating its underlying meaning. Insofar as it originates in the correctness of one’s nature and Heaven’s mandate, it is called the heart-mind of the Way. Surely what the Master [?] designated the “good heart-mind” and the “original heart-mind” refers to this heart-mind of the Way? Insofar as it arises from the partiality of bodily form and vital energy, it is called the human heart-mind. Surely what Wen and Cheng [?] designated the “desiring heart-mind” and the “selfish heart-mind” refers to this human heart-mind? The Book of Changes says: “In Return, one sees the heart-mind of Heaven and Earth.” When yin reaches its extreme, yang arises; when Stripping Away reaches its extreme, Return arrives. Thus Heaven and Earth’s heart-mind, which gives life to things, becomes manifest. Our own heart-mind is therefore the heart-mind of Heaven and Earth. The transmitted text says: “The great man is one who does not lose the heart-mind of an infant.” Through purity and unity without falseness, and through uninterrupted extension and development, the great man completes the work of rectifying himself. Our own heart-mind is therefore the heart-mind of an infant. As for other instances, such as that of the Classic of the Heart-Mind (Xinjing)…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
賛命之曰天君固尊之矣横渠以之爲嚴
師非以其可畏而勿褻乎敬齋之箴命之
曰靈臺固神之矣孟子以之爲氣帥非以
其爲至而當持乎爲名雖多端而其理則
一致焉義羲觀舜之禪禹既以人心道心相
告戒矣而復足以惟精惟一之語是闡堯
之秘也精則察之而不雜即孟子盡心之
謂周子之所謂養心亦惟察乎此而不汨
於欲爾一則守之而不離即孟子存心之
===
謂大學之所謂正心亦惟守乎此而不勝
於情爾易曰以此洗心言義文具闡神之
知之理而無私以爲之累蓋性之也若陶
元亮之委心乃不欲仕宋非有發之言乎
書曰以禮制心言殷湯絶聲色貨利之嗜
而有禮以爲之防蓋反之也若佛氏之無
心乃寂滅是崇非無稽之語乎他如玩寧
靜致遠之言則李延平以静坐爲養心之
要宜矣真西山以澄養爲言又明乎程子
punctuated: 賛命之曰天君，固尊之矣。横渠以之爲嚴師，非以其可畏而勿褻乎？敬齋之箴命之曰靈臺，固神之矣。孟子以之爲氣帥，非以其爲至而當持乎？爲名雖多端，而其理則一致焉。義羲觀舜之禪禹，既以人心道心相告戒矣，而復足以惟精惟一之語，是闡堯之秘也。精則察之而不雜，即孟子盡心之謂；周子之所謂養心，亦惟察乎此而不汨於欲爾。一則守之而不離，即孟子存心之謂；大學之所謂正心，亦惟守乎此而不勝於情爾。易曰：「以此洗心。」言義文具闡神之知之理，而無私以爲之累，蓋性之也。若陶元亮之委心，乃不欲仕宋，非有發之言乎？書曰：「以禮制心。」言殷湯絶聲色貨利之嗜，而有禮以爲之防，蓋反之也。若佛氏之無心，乃寂滅是崇，非無稽之語乎？他如玩寧靜致遠之言，則李延平以静坐爲養心之要宜矣。真西山以澄養爲言，又明乎程子
translation_en:
…the Eulogy on the Classic of the Mind calls it the “Heavenly Lord,” thus assuredly honoring it. Hengqu treats it as a stern teacher: is this not because it commands awe and must not be treated irreverently? The Admonition of the Studio of Reverence calls it the “Numinous Terrace,” thus assuredly recognizing its spiritual power. Mengzi treats it as the commander of vital energy: is this not because it is supreme and must be held fast? Though its names are many, the principle underlying them is one.

[?] Consider Shun’s abdication in favor of Yu: he had already admonished him concerning the human mind and the mind of the Way, yet supplemented this with the words “Be discerning; be single-minded.” This disclosed Yao’s secret teaching. To be discerning is to examine the mind without admixture: this is what Mengzi meant by fully realizing one’s mind. What Master Zhou called nourishing the mind likewise means only examining this and not becoming submerged in desires. To be single-minded is to hold fast to it without departing from it: this is what Mengzi meant by preserving the mind. What the Great Learning calls rectifying the mind likewise means only holding fast to this and not being overcome by emotions.

The Book of Changes says, “With this they cleanse their minds.” This speaks of Yi and Wen [?] fully elucidating the principle of spiritual knowing [?], with no selfishness to encumber it: theirs was, indeed, an innate realization of it. As for Tao Yuanliang’s “entrusting himself to his mind,” this meant that he did not wish to serve the Song. Were these not words prompted by a particular circumstance? The Book of Documents says, “Regulate the mind through ritual.” This speaks of Tang of Yin cutting off his taste for music, sensual beauty, goods, and profit, and using ritual as a safeguard: his was, indeed, a return to it through effort. As for the Buddhists’ “no-mind,” they exalt extinction and quiescence. Is this not an unfounded assertion?

Further, if we ponder the saying that through tranquility one reaches far, it is fitting that Li Yanping regarded quiet sitting as the essential means of nourishing the mind. Zhen Xishan spoke of clarifying and nourishing it, further illuminating Master Cheng’s …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
主一之旨也黼扆之銘作聖之訓則范浚以
克念爲箴心之功當矣吳草廬以主敬爲
言又本乎文言直內之意也爲說雖紛無
而其意各有主焉至若心必有所止則不
累於私使一有所縈將惟物是聽無往而
不喪矣心在腔子裏則不馳於欲若聖人
之心固未嘗有在而亦無不在矣玩物喪
志召公之訓不爲不切語取博要之爲賢
者乃論無所用心之不可甚言之詞也豈
===
導人以玩物哉令色鮮仁尼父之戒不爲
不嚴詩取其儀之如一者乃美曹人用心
之如結自然之符也豈教人以令色哉力
救時弊七篇之立論微矣故語心又指山
木以爲喻蓋欲萬章華力指存之功抑以
教後世也欲除意見陸象山之近禪固矣
故語心特借弱論以爲譬蓋欲楊簡華知
頓悟之妙適以誤後學也克廣德心曾人
頌之則心不爍其欲大小心翼翼周人頼
punctuated: 主一之旨也。黼扆之銘、作聖之訓，則范浚以克念爲箴心之功當矣。吳草廬以主敬爲言，又本乎《文言》直內之意也。爲說雖紛無，而其意各有主焉。至若心必有所止，則不累於私；使一有所縈，將惟物是聽，無往而不喪矣。心在腔子裏，則不馳於欲；若聖人之心，固未嘗有在，而亦無不在矣。「玩物喪志」，召公之訓不爲不切；《語》取博要之爲賢者，乃論無所用心之不可，甚言之詞也，豈導人以玩物哉？「令色鮮仁」，尼父之戒不爲不嚴；《詩》取其儀之如一者，乃美曹人用心之如結，自然之符也，豈教人以令色哉？力救時弊，七篇之立論微矣。故語心，又指山木以爲喻，蓋欲萬章華力指存之功，抑以教後世也。欲除意見，陸象山之近禪固矣。故語心，特借弱論以爲譬，蓋欲楊簡華知頓悟之妙，適以誤後學也。「克廣德心」，曾人頌之，則心不爍其欲大；「小心翼翼」，周人頼
translation_en:
…the meaning of concentrating on the one. As for the inscription on the embroidered imperial screen and the teaching about becoming a sage, Fan Jun was right to make mastery of one’s thoughts the work prescribed in his Admonition to the Mind. Wu Caolu’s teaching of maintaining reverence likewise rests upon the idea of making the inner self upright in the Commentary on the Words of the Text of the Changes. Although these explanations are various [?], each has its own central concern.

When the mind has a definite resting place, it is not encumbered by selfishness. Once something entangles it, however, it will obey external things alone, and wherever it goes it will suffer loss. When the mind remains within the breast, it does not race after desires. The sage’s mind, however, has never been confined to any one place, yet there is nowhere it is not present.

“Taking delight in things destroys one’s resolve”: the Duke of Shao’s admonition is certainly earnest. When the Analects commends playing games [?] as preferable, it is discussing the unacceptability of leaving the mind entirely unoccupied; this is emphatic language. How could it be directing people to take delight in mere things? “An ingratiating expression seldom accompanies benevolence”: Father Ni’s warning is certainly strict. When the Book of Poetry commends a person whose deportment is consistent, it praises the people of Cao for minds firmly bound as though in a knot; their deportment is its natural outward sign. How could it be teaching people to assume ingratiating expressions?

Striving to remedy the failings of his age, Mencius developed subtle arguments in his seven books. Thus, when discussing the mind, he also pointed to the trees on a mountain as an analogy. His intention was to have Wan Zhang exert himself in preserving the mind [?], and thereby also to instruct later generations. In seeking to eliminate preconceived opinions, Lu Xiangshan certainly approached Chan Buddhism. Thus, when discussing the mind, he specifically borrowed a discussion of weakness [?] as an illustration. His intention was to have Yang Jian understand the marvel of sudden enlightenment [?], but this served only to mislead later students.

“Capable of enlarging the virtuous mind”: the people of Zeng [?] praised this, indicating that the mind does not … [?] and should be expansive. “Cautious and reverent”: the people of Zhou relied upon …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之則心不難其欲小此横渠孫思邈之言
均於經有見也有主於中則外邪不能入
不亦虛乎中有所主則理義爲甚充不亦
實乎此程氏先後之言供於㮣無背也嗚
呼至哉古人之論心乎要哉古人之治心
乎本於唐虞之授受而散爲六經之格言
詳於孔孟之講明而衍爲諸儒之緒論理
欲攸分而防範爲甚嚴體用具存而知行
爲有則斂之不盈一掬擴之則彌漫乎六
===
合運之不出一腔致之則範圍乎天地在
吾所以用之何如爾愚生跡劣無似自顧
非其人也然不敢不勉謹對
第四問
千思靡
同考試官教諭陳　批〔此策考據詳明評品精確末又知所適從觀此亦可以占吾子之學不獨〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔卽古人心事而辨究之區區於博古也健羨健羨〕
punctuated:
之，則心不難其欲小。此横渠、孫思邈之言，均於經有見也。有主於中，則外邪不能入，不亦虛乎？中有所主，則理義爲甚充，不亦實乎？此程氏先後之言，供於㮣無背也。嗚呼！至哉，古人之論心乎！要哉，古人之治心乎！本於唐虞之授受，而散爲六經之格言；詳於孔孟之講明，而衍爲諸儒之緒論。理欲攸分，而防範爲甚嚴；體用具存，而知行爲有則。斂之不盈一掬，擴之則彌漫乎六合；運之不出一腔，致之則範圍乎天地。在吾所以用之何如爾。愚生跡劣無似，自顧非其人也，然不敢不勉。謹對。

第四問
千思靡

同考試官教諭陳，批〔此策考據詳明，評品精確，末又知所適從。觀此亦可以占吾子之學，不獨〕

同考試官教諭張，批〔卽古人心事而辨究之，區區於博古也。健羨，健羨！〕
translation_en:
…upon it, the mind finds no difficulty in wishing to be small [?]. Thus the statements of Hengqu and Sun Simiao both show insight into the Classics. When there is a master within, external evils cannot enter: is this not emptiness? When the interior has a master, principle and righteousness fill it abundantly: is this not fullness? These earlier and later statements of Master Cheng are broadly consistent [?]. Ah! How consummate were the ancients’ discussions of the mind! How essential was their cultivation of it! Rooted in the transmission between the rulers of Tang and Yu, these teachings spread into the exemplary sayings of the Six Classics. Expounded in detail by Confucius and Mencius, they developed further into the subsequent discussions of the Confucian scholars. Principle and desire are distinguished, and the safeguards are exceedingly strict; substance and function are both present, and knowledge and action have their standards. Gathered in, it does not fill a single cupped handful; expanded, it pervades the six directions. In operation, it does not leave the breast; extended to its fullest reach, it encompasses Heaven and Earth. All depends upon how we employ it. This foolish student’s conduct is deficient and unworthy; examining myself, I see that I am not such a person. Nevertheless, I dare not fail to strive. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Qian Simi

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay is detailed and clear in its examination of evidence, and precise in its assessments. At the end, the writer also knows which course to follow. From this one can judge your learning, which is not merely…〕

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔He examines and discriminates among the thoughts and concerns of the ancients; narrowly occupied with extensive knowledge of antiquity [?]. How admirable, how admirable!〕

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
此格致之學也吾於此策也非見其博古而尚友
之志併於是見之
考試官訓導吳　批〔說得古人心事出胸中可　謂有灼見者□〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔尚友一策答者類能言　之而是篇考據詳明擇所趨向非窮理格物之士　能之乎〕
格物者當求諸自然之理論人者當考其
已然之迹蓋天下之理散見於事物者萬
===
有不齊而行之古人其迹不能以皆同也
不有吾心以權度之則物理之有無人□
之高下莫定而從違取舍難矣豈窮理盡
性之學哉請因明問而陳之夫君親者人
之事也鄒衍事君結憤而六月飛霜孟宗
事親投誠而三冬出笋蓋精誠則天地可
動而孝弟則神明可通一理之感孚耳春
秋者天之序也鄒子吹玉律而寒谷春□
麗娟唱迴風而夏景秋變盖黃鍾為□□
punctuated:
此格致之學也。吾於此策也，非見其博古，而尚友之志併於是見之。

考試官訓導吳　批〔說得古人心事出，胸中可謂有灼見者□〕
考試官教諭徐　批〔尚友一策，答者類能言之，而是篇考據詳明，擇所趨向，非窮理格物之士能之乎？〕

格物者當求諸自然之理，論人者當考其已然之迹。蓋天下之理，散見於事物者萬有不齊，而行之古人，其迹不能以皆同也。不有吾心以權度之，則物理之有無、人□之高下莫定，而從違取舍難矣，豈窮理盡性之學哉？請因明問而陳之。夫君親者，人之事也。鄒衍事君結憤而六月飛霜，孟宗事親投誠而三冬出笋，蓋精誠則天地可動，而孝弟則神明可通，一理之感孚耳。春秋者，天之序也。鄒子吹玉律而寒谷春□，麗娟唱迴風而夏景秋變，盖黃鍾為□□
translation_en:
This is the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge. In this policy essay, I see not merely his extensive knowledge of antiquity, but also his aspiration to befriend the ancients.

Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He brings out the thoughts and concerns of the ancients; he may be said to possess penetrating insight □.〕
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔On this policy question concerning befriending the ancients, most candidates can offer some discussion. But this essay examines the evidence thoroughly and clearly and discriminates among the paths to follow. Could anyone accomplish this without being a scholar who fathoms principles and investigates things?〕

Those who investigate things should seek their inherent principles; those who assess people should examine the traces of their actual deeds. The principles of all under Heaven, manifested throughout affairs and things, differ in countless ways; when the ancients put them into practice, their deeds could not all be alike. Unless we use our own minds to weigh and measure them, we cannot determine whether principles are present in things or absent from them, or rank people's □ [?]; choosing what to follow or reject, accept or discard, then becomes difficult. Could this be the learning that fathoms principles and fully realizes one's nature? Allow me to set forth my views in response to your illuminating question.

Serving one's ruler and parents belongs to human affairs. Zou Yan served his ruler and suffered pent-up indignation, whereupon frost fell in the sixth month. Meng Zong served his parent with utter sincerity, whereupon bamboo shoots emerged in the depths of winter. Perfect sincerity can move Heaven and Earth, and filial piety and fraternal respect can reach the spirits: these are simply instances of the responsive resonance of a single principle. Spring and autumn belong to Heaven's seasonal order. Master Zou blew a jade pitch pipe, and the cold valley became springlike [?]; Lijuan sang “Returning Wind,” and the summer scene changed to autumn. For the Yellow Bell pitch serves as □□ …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之府而商音乃肅殺之聲一氣之招徠耳
莊周悟養生於解牛以其靜而無爲然而
無言也張旭得書法於舞劍以其遒勁鍵
婚盤若龍蛇也程子踏石墱而探升降之
理非以見此身即天地乎因湯瓶而識消
長之機非以明一物亦陰陽乎乃若宜僚
弄丸而解楚王之難陳平戲偶而脫漢帝
之圍此特智小慧僥倖於一時也韓愈貶
潮州而鮫鱷逃形李泌令洛陽而鬼神破
===
膽則忠誠正直積之於平日也捫虱而談
當世之務者非王猛歟而昧見幾而作之
理䙌鱷而輕當世之人者非禰衡歟而失
明哲保身之道竈不卹緯而憂公與野人
食芹而思君者同一過於厚也蹊田而奪
之牛與覆羹而逐其婦者同一過於薄也
以至高悝之焚符傳奕之仆僧其以正止
邪殆與馬公亮之夜書窓手狄仁傑之素
娥見畏者先後一致也邵康節之鼓妖砫
punctuated: 之府，而商音乃肅殺之聲，一氣之招徠耳。莊周悟養生於解牛，以其靜而無爲，然而無言也。張旭得書法於舞劍，以其遒勁鍵婚盤若龍蛇也。程子踏石墱而探升降之理，非以見此身即天地乎？因湯瓶而識消長之機，非以明一物亦陰陽乎？乃若宜僚弄丸而解楚王之難，陳平戲偶而脫漢帝之圍，此特智小慧僥倖於一時也。韓愈貶潮州而鮫鱷逃形，李泌令洛陽而鬼神破膽，則忠誠正直積之於平日也。捫虱而談當世之務者，非王猛歟？而昧見幾而作之理。䙌鱷而輕當世之人者，非禰衡歟？而失明哲保身之道。竈不卹緯而憂公，與野人食芹而思君者，同一過於厚也。蹊田而奪之牛，與覆羹而逐其婦者，同一過於薄也。以至高悝之焚符、傳奕之仆僧，其以正止邪，殆與馬公亮之夜書窓手、狄仁傑之素娥見畏者，先後一致也。邵康節之鼓妖砫
translation_en:
…the repository of it, while the shang tone is the sound of stern killing: these are merely effects elicited by the same vital force, qi. Zhuang Zhou understood the nurturing of life through the cutting up of an ox, because of its stillness and nonaction, yet without words. Zhang Xu acquired the principles of calligraphy from a sword dance, because of its vigorous movements, coiling like dragons and snakes [?]. When Master Cheng stepped on stone stairs and investigated the principle of ascent and descent, was this not to perceive that this very body is itself Heaven and Earth? When he discerned the workings of waning and waxing through a vessel of hot water, was this not to show that a single object likewise embodies yin and yang?

As for Yiliao, who juggled balls and resolved the King of Chu’s difficulty, and Chen Ping, who manipulated puppets and freed the Han emperor from encirclement, these were merely instances of petty cleverness securing a lucky success on one occasion. When Han Yu was banished to Chaozhou and the sharks and crocodiles fled, and when Li Mi served as Magistrate of Luoyang and ghosts and spirits lost their courage, these effects arose from loyalty, sincerity, uprightness, and integrity accumulated in everyday life.

Was it not Wang Meng who picked lice while discussing the affairs of his age? Yet he failed to understand the principle of perceiving the first signs and acting upon them. Was it not Mi Heng who held the men of his age in contempt through [an illegible or garbled action: 䙌鱷]? Yet he lost the way of preserving oneself through wisdom and discernment. The person who neglected weaving out of concern for the duke [?], and the rustic who ate water celery and thought of his ruler, alike erred through excessive generosity of feeling. Taking away someone’s ox because it had trampled a field, and dismissing one’s wife because she had spilled the broth, alike erred through excessive harshness.

Further examples are Gao Kui’s burning of talismans and Chuan Yi’s knocking down a monk [?]. In using rectitude to check evil, these were probably of a piece, though occurring at different times, with Ma Gongliang’s writing at night on a hand at his window [?] and Di Renjie’s being feared by Su’e. Shao Kangjie’s drum demon [砫, unclear]…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
周南之鼠悖其以德勝妖殆與魏元忠之
見倷守火韋叔堅之見犬立廳者今昔一
律也乃若以宰相而錯寫弄麞以學士而
妄爲曳布林甫王緘之闇何足怪哉悟絕
妙好辭之題解獨眠孤館之字曹操丁謂
之慧何可取哉王筠讀郊居賦而恐雌霓
誤段金根又何繆也宋太宗見楊億有越
妾呼筠則誠爲智者矣而韓晁發理史館
景絕塵之稱億固足以當國士矣而高孝
===
基見房玄齡有僕竪昂霄之譽又何宜也
凡此皆事物之理散見於天地古今者是
則然矣其人品之高下吾心之取舍不能
無說焉夫君子之所貴者道德功業文章
而已康節之數學所以發先天之藴者固
爲至極而吾程子續不傳之統於千載之
下斯道之明如日中天其功業豈徒道德
而已哉玄齡之相業所以開貞觀之風者
固爲甚優而昌黎之闢異端大年之不茍
punctuated:
周南之鼠悖，其以德勝妖，殆與魏元忠之見倷守火、韋叔堅之見犬立廳者，今昔一律也。乃若以宰相而錯寫弄麞，以學士而妄爲曳布，林甫、王緘之闇，何足怪哉？悟絕妙好辭之題，解獨眠孤館之字，曹操、丁謂之慧，何可取哉？王筠讀郊居賦而恐雌霓誤段金根，又何繆也？宋太宗見楊億有越妾呼筠，則誠爲智者矣。而韓晁發理史館景絕塵之稱，億固足以當國士矣。而高孝基見房玄齡有僕竪昂霄之譽，又何宜也？
凡此皆事物之理，散見於天地古今者，是則然矣。其人品之高下、吾心之取舍，不能無說焉。夫君子之所貴者，道德、功業、文章而已。康節之數學，所以發先天之藴者，固爲至極；而吾程子續不傳之統於千載之下，斯道之明如日中天，其功業豈徒道德而已哉？玄齡之相業，所以開貞觀之風者，固爲甚優；而昌黎之闢異端、大年之不茍
translation_en:
…Zhou Nan’s disturbance involving mice [?]: his overcoming uncanny manifestations through virtue was much the same, across past and present, as Wei Yuanzhong’s seeing “nai guarding fire” [?] and Wei Shujian’s seeing a dog standing in the hall. As for a chief minister incorrectly writing “playing with a male deer,” or a Hanlin Academician rashly producing “dragging cloth” [?], what is surprising about the ignorance of Linfu and Wang Jian? And what is admirable about the cleverness of Cao Cao and Ding Wei in deciphering the inscription meaning “exquisite, excellent words” and solving the character riddle “sleeping alone in a solitary lodge”? Wang Yun read the Rhapsody on Dwelling in the Suburbs and feared an error concerning “female rainbows”; then there is Duan’s “golden carriage”—what further blunders were these [?]? Emperor Taizong of the Song, on seeing Yang Yi, had “a Yue concubine call Yun” [?]; then he truly was a discerning man. And with the praise attributed to Han and Chao concerning “expounding principles,” the Historiography Institute, and “leaving others far behind” [?], Yi certainly deserved to be considered an outstanding man of the realm. Yet when Gao Xiaoji saw Fang Xuanling and praised him with words about “servants” and “soaring into the clouds” [?], how fitting was this?
All these are principles underlying affairs and things, appearing here and there throughout heaven and earth, past and present. This much is indeed so. Yet something must be said about the relative worth of these men’s characters and about what I accept or reject in my own mind. What the gentleman values is simply moral virtue, achievements in public service, and literary accomplishment. Kangjie’s study of numbers, through which he disclosed the mysteries of the Before-Heaven order, was certainly of the highest attainment. Yet our Master Cheng renewed, a thousand years later, the succession of the Way whose transmission had been broken, making this Way shine as brightly as the sun at noon. Were his achievements in public service merely a matter of moral virtue? Xuanling’s achievements as chief minister, through which he inaugurated the spirit of the Zhenguan reign, were certainly outstanding. Yet Changli’s rejection of heterodox teachings and Danian’s refusal to be careless …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
詔卓然之見確乎之守其道德豈徒文章
而已哉若夫一節一行之士在兼收並蓄
者之所不遺而其過遂惡形身亡國僨者
又不足置之牙頰間也愚生蕞爾之權度
所以爲輕重長短者如此願執事進而教
之
第五問
胡鎧
同考試官學正林　批〔時務一策人皆能言而區畫斟酌之當則未易也此策區處治河弭〕
===
盜之法鑿鑿可行豈非俊傑之士邪
考試官訓導吳　批〔蘇軾云策者所以措置於今之世此問正欲觀其措置爭能援古證〕
今處置得宜其有用之學者與
考試官教諭徐　批〔此卷五策條答無遺不拘拘於問目若而治河禦盜一策尤處置得宜〕
而其要在用人又確論也當道所欲聞者其在
茲乎錄之
punctuated:
詔，卓然之見，確乎之守，其道德豈徒文章而已哉？若夫一節一行之士，在兼收並蓄者之所不遺；而其過遂惡、形身亡國僨者，又不足置之牙頰間也。愚生蕞爾之權度，所以爲輕重長短者如此，願執事進而教之。
第五問
胡鎧
同考試官學正林批〔時務一策，人皆能言，而區畫斟酌之當，則未易也。此策區處治河弭〕盜之法，鑿鑿可行，豈非俊傑之士邪？
考試官訓導吳批〔蘇軾云：「策者，所以措置於今之世。」此問正欲觀其措置，爭能援古證〕今，處置得宜，其有用之學者與？
考試官教諭徐批〔此卷五策，條答無遺，不拘拘於問目。若而治河禦盜一策，尤處置得宜〕，而其要在用人，又確論也。當道所欲聞者，其在茲乎？錄之。
translation_en:
…edicts. With such outstanding discernment and steadfast principles, was their moral excellence merely a matter of literary accomplishment? As for men distinguished by a single act of integrity or exemplary conduct, those who gather talent broadly do not overlook them. But those whose faults culminated in evil, bringing ruin upon themselves and their states [?], are not worth mentioning. Such are the judgments of relative weight and measure reached with the meager scales and ruler of this humble student. May you, honored sir, offer further instruction.
Fifth Question
Hu Kai 胡鎧
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin 林, School Director: Anyone can speak about current affairs in a policy essay, but sound planning and judicious deliberation are not easily achieved. The methods this essay proposes for managing the river and suppressing banditry are concrete and practicable. Is he not a man of outstanding talent?
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Assistant Instructor: Su Shi said, “Policy essays set out how to handle affairs in the world of today.” This question was intended precisely to assess the candidate’s handling of affairs. He can [?] draw upon antiquity to substantiate his arguments about the present, and his proposed measures are appropriate. Is he not a scholar whose learning has practical application?
Comment by Examiner Xu 徐, Instructor: The five policy essays in this script answer every point without omission, yet do not cling narrowly to the wording of the questions. The essay on managing the river and resisting bandits, in particular [?], proposes especially appropriate measures. Moreover, its contention that the essential matter is the employment of the right men is sound. Is this not just what those in authority wish to hear? Include it in the record.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
除害之法欲相其機防害之法欲善其後
夫害之來也除之不力則不可去也害之
去也防之不密則將復生也除之必相其
機防之必善其後黄河之害盜賊之害以
是處之則收功於有事保治於無虞民生
庶幾其有賴乎執事發策秋闈而問及乎
此此誠吾心軫民害之至重且急者也敢
不敬陳其顛末以求所以除之乎夫黄河
發源於星宿之海其來也遠矣禹治水
===
九河既道然後中國可得而食也自漢以
來河患不時有之其時論治河者亦多矣
吾獨有取於漢賈讓元賈魯二君子之所
建白焉讓有治河三策上策徙冀州之民
當水衝者決黎陽遮害亭放河使北入海
中策多穿漕渠於冀州地使民得以溉田
從淇口以東為石隄多張水門以備旱澇
下策則繕完故隄增卑倍薄而已魯有治
河三法有疏有濬有塞釃河之流因而導
punctuated:
除害之法，欲相其機；防害之法，欲善其後。

夫害之來也，除之不力，則不可去也；害之去也，防之不密，則將復生也。除之必相其機，防之必善其後。黄河之害、盜賊之害，以是處之，則收功於有事，保治於無虞，民生庶幾其有賴乎！執事發策秋闈，而問及乎此，此誠吾心軫民害之至重且急者也。敢不敬陳其顛末，以求所以除之乎？夫黄河發源於星宿之海，其來也遠矣。禹治水，九河既道，然後中國可得而食也。自漢以來，河患不時有之，其時論治河者亦多矣。吾獨有取於漢賈讓、元賈魯二君子之所建白焉。讓有治河三策：上策，徙冀州之民當水衝者，決黎陽遮害亭，放河使北入海；中策，多穿漕渠於冀州地，使民得以溉田，從淇口以東為石隄，多張水門，以備旱澇；下策，則繕完故隄，增卑倍薄而已。魯有治河三法：有疏，有濬，有塞。釃河之流，因而導
translation_en:
The method of eliminating harm requires judging the right opportunity; the method of preventing harm requires making sound provision for what follows.

When harm comes, it cannot be removed unless vigorous efforts are made to eliminate it; once it has gone, it will arise again unless preventive measures are thorough. In eliminating it, one must judge the right opportunity; in preventing it, one must make sound provision for what follows. If the dangers posed by the Yellow River and by bandits are dealt with in this way, results can be achieved in times of trouble and good order maintained in times free from anxiety. Might the people then have something on which to depend for their livelihood? You gentlemen have set policy questions for the autumn Provincial Examination and have asked about these matters. These are indeed among the gravest and most urgent harms to the people that trouble my heart. How could I fail respectfully to set forth their circumstances from beginning to end, seeking the means to eliminate them?

The Yellow River rises in Xingxiu Hai, the Sea of Constellations, and its course is long indeed. When Yu brought the waters under control, only after the nine rivers had been channeled could the people of the Central Lands obtain food. Since the Han dynasty, river disasters have occurred from time to time, and many men in those periods have discussed river management. I particularly commend the proposals submitted by two gentlemen: Jia Rang of the Han and Jia Lu of the Yuan. Jia Rang offered three plans for managing the river. The best plan was to relocate those inhabitants of Jizhou who lay directly in the path of the waters, breach the embankment at Zhehai Ting in Liyang, and release the river to flow northward into the sea. The middle plan was to excavate numerous transport canals in Jizhou so that the people could irrigate their fields, build stone embankments eastward from Qikou, and install numerous sluice gates to guard against drought and flooding. The lowest plan amounted merely to repairing the old embankments, raising their low sections and doubling the thickness of their thin sections. Jia Lu had three methods of river management: opening channels, dredging, and blocking. Dividing the river’s flow and thereby guiding it …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之謂之疏去河之淤因而深之謂之濬抑
河之暴因而拒之謂之塞是也觀夫竹落
下石而隄防計日以立疏塞並舉而隄埽
計月而成也氏河濬之不早則水居者數
十縣地六塔河穿之不善則水死者數千
萬人力不能為則徒付瓠子之歌役不以
道則祇應石人之讖蓋治之不善固無足
言而治之善者莫不用魯之三法而實不
出讓之下策也往年
===
朝廷興安平之工合數省之財力而董之以
內外大臣其事重矣近因水勢北侵複
勑大臣以總其事又添府佐以專其職而
申命各省撫巡皆協謀焉然古之治河多為民
患今以轉漕兼為
國計誠尤不可忽也為今之計必也黃陵岡
之三埽所宜急復而河南下流不可不疏
河臺寺之褰隄所宜急築而河流所經不
可不辯而又脩復守隄之法申嚴盜決之
punctuated:
之，謂之疏；去河之淤，因而深之，謂之濬；抑河之暴，因而拒之，謂之塞，是也。觀夫竹落下石，而隄防計日以立；疏塞並舉，而隄埽計月而成。也氏河濬之不早，則水居者數十縣地；六塔河穿之不善，則水死者數千萬人。力不能為，則徒付瓠子之歌；役不以道，則祇應石人之讖。蓋治之不善，固無足言；而治之善者，莫不用魯之三法，而實不出讓之下策也。
往年，朝廷興安平之工，合數省之財力，而董之以內外大臣，其事重矣。近因水勢北侵，複勑大臣以總其事，又添府佐以專其職，而申命各省撫巡皆協謀焉。然古之治河，多為民患；今以轉漕，兼為國計，誠尤不可忽也。為今之計，必也黃陵岡之三埽所宜急復，而河南下流不可不疏；河臺寺之褰隄所宜急築，而河流所經不可不辯；而又脩復守隄之法，申嚴盜決之
translation_en:
…it: this is called channeling. Removing the river’s silt and thereby deepening it is called dredging; restraining the river’s violence and holding it back is called blocking. Such are the three methods. Consider how stones were lowered in bamboo baskets [?], and embankments rose within days; channeling and blocking were undertaken together, and embankments and brushwood barriers were completed within months. Because the Yeshi River [?] was not dredged early enough, water occupied land in several dozen counties [?]; because the Liuta River was inadequately excavated, those who drowned numbered in the tens of millions [?]. When strength proves insufficient for the undertaking, all that remains is the Song of Huzi; when labor is employed without proper methods, it merely fulfills the prophecy of the stone man. Poor river management is, of course, not worth discussing; yet those who managed it well all employed Jia Lu’s three methods, which in fact went no further than Jia Rang’s lowest-ranked proposal.
In past years, the court undertook the works at Anping, pooling the financial resources and manpower of several provinces and placing high officials from the central and regional administrations in charge. This was indeed an undertaking of great importance. Recently, because the waters have been encroaching northward, the court again commanded high officials to take overall charge, added assistant prefectural officials specifically responsible for the work, and reiterated its orders that the grand coordinators and regional inspectors of all the provinces cooperate in planning. In antiquity, however, river management was mostly undertaken because of the harm the river caused the people; today, because of grain transport, it also concerns the state’s finances. It is therefore especially imperative that it not be neglected. The plan for the present must be urgently to restore the three brushwood barriers at Huanglinggang, while also clearing the downstream reaches in Henan; urgently to build the embankment at Hetai Temple [?], while also determining the course through which the river flows; and furthermore to restore the methods of guarding the embankments and enforce more strictly the provisions against secretly breaching them …

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
例庶幾民生可免魚鱉之患
國家得給饋餉之饒視彼河既潰決然後爲
葺脩治以勞民者其功孰爲多哉盜賊潛
跡於閭閻之奸其起也微矣皐陶爲士兼
治寇賊當時所謂不仁者遠矣自秦而後
盜賊無代無之其間論去盜者亦多矣吾
獨有取於宋歐陽脩與秦觀之所數陳焉
脩謂方今禦盜者不過四事一曰州郡置
兵爲備二曰選捕盜之官三曰明賞罰之
===
法四曰去冗官用良吏以撫疲民使不起
爲盜觀謂盜賊平之非難絕之爲難平而
不絕其弊有二招降與窮治是已患莫大
於招降禍莫深於窮治也觀夫顓真寧鷹
贼料兵而人倚爲重諸葛亮信賞必罰而
士樂爲死用一襲遂則百姓無不安用一
岳飛則羣盜無不平漢武立沈命之法而
盜賊寖多元人誤招安之說而國威遂弱
盖慾盜不治固無足言而所以治之是誠
punctuated:
例，庶幾民生可免魚鱉之患，國家得給饋餉之饒。視彼河既潰決，然後爲葺脩治以勞民者，其功孰爲多哉？
盜賊潛跡於閭閻之奸，其起也微矣。皐陶爲士，兼治寇賊，當時所謂不仁者遠矣。自秦而後，盜賊無代無之，其間論去盜者亦多矣。吾獨有取於宋歐陽脩與秦觀之所數陳焉。脩謂方今禦盜者不過四事：一曰州郡置兵爲備，二曰選捕盜之官，三曰明賞罰之法，四曰去冗官、用良吏，以撫疲民，使不起爲盜。觀謂盜賊平之非難，絕之爲難。平而不絕，其弊有二：招降與窮治是已。患莫大於招降，禍莫深於窮治也。觀夫顓真寧鷹贼料兵而人倚爲重，諸葛亮信賞必罰而士樂爲死，用一襲遂則百姓無不安，用一岳飛則羣盜無不平。漢武立沈命之法而盜賊寖多，元人誤招安之說而國威遂弱。盖慾盜不治，固無足言，而所以治之，是誠
translation_en:
…the regulations, so that the people may be spared the calamity of becoming fish and turtles, and the state may have ample supplies for provisioning its forces. Compared with those who wait until the river has breached its embankments before undertaking repairs and burdening the people with labor, whose achievement would be greater?
Bandits conceal their tracks among evildoers in the villages; their beginnings are slight. When Gao Yao served as Minister of Justice, he also dealt with robbers and bandits; thus, as was said at the time, those lacking benevolence kept their distance. Since the Qin, no dynasty has been without bandits, and many have discussed how to eliminate them. I particularly approve of the arguments repeatedly advanced by Ouyang Xiu and Qin Guan of the Song. Xiu said that defending against bandits in his day involved no more than four measures: first, station troops in the prefectures for defense; second, select officials to apprehend bandits; third, make the rules governing rewards and punishments clear; fourth, eliminate superfluous officials and employ good ones to care for the exhausted people, so that they do not rise up as bandits. Guan said that suppressing bandits was not difficult; eradicating them was difficult. Suppression without eradication involved two abuses: soliciting surrender and pursuing investigations to the utmost. No trouble was greater than soliciting surrender, and no disaster more profound than exhaustive prosecution. Consider how [a garbled passage apparently concerning a person’s handling of bandits and troops] won people’s reliance and esteem [?]; Zhuge Liang made rewards trustworthy and punishments certain, and his soldiers gladly died for him. Employing a single Xi Sui [?] brought peace to all the common people; employing a single Yue Fei brought all the bands of robbers under control. Emperor Wu of the Han established the law of collective capital liability for failure to suppress banditry, yet bandits gradually increased. The rulers of the Yuan mistakenly embraced the policy of offering amnesty and accepting submission, and the state’s authority consequently weakened. As for wishing to leave bandits unchecked [?], that scarcely merits discussion; but the means of dealing with them truly lie in…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
在乎四事之必舉而二弊之必去也近年
朝廷除山東之盜合京邊之士馬而督之以
內外大臣其功大矣時以民傷災盜又□
勑大臣以主賑恤復添憲臣以司兵備而更留
大將領邊兵以鎮守焉然吉之兵將多聞
戍邊今以權宜移邊戍內誠恐不可久也
爲今之計必使兵備選練其兵而省城府
重不可不預爲之備守巡撫恤其民而官
吏倉儲不可不嚴爲之防而又增城池之
===
高深豐芻粟之儲積庶幾在我者隱然如
虎豹之在山在民者怡然如赤子之得母
矣視彼盜已縱橫然後倉卒驅迫以棄民
者其計孰爲得哉嗚呼二害既除山東之
民其更生矣雖然興作爲勞民之事養兵
有困民之虞况瘡痍甫定之民尤不可不
加之意者乎當道者於是其將自有所以
處之矣而愚生過慮不敢不申言之焉謹
對
punctuated: 在乎四事之必舉，而二弊之必去也。近年朝廷除山東之盜，合京邊之士馬，而督之以內外大臣，其功大矣。時以民傷災盜，又□勑大臣以主賑恤，復添憲臣以司兵備，而更留大將領邊兵以鎮守焉。然吉之兵將，多聞戍邊，今以權宜移邊戍內，誠恐不可久也。爲今之計，必使兵備選練其兵，而省城府重，不可不預爲之備；守巡撫恤其民，而官吏倉儲，不可不嚴爲之防。而又增城池之高深，豐芻粟之儲積，庶幾在我者隱然如虎豹之在山，在民者怡然如赤子之得母矣。視彼盜已縱橫，然後倉卒驅迫以棄民者，其計孰爲得哉？嗚呼！二害既除，山東之民其更生矣。雖然，興作爲勞民之事，養兵有困民之虞，况瘡痍甫定之民，尤不可不加之意者乎？當道者於是其將自有所以處之矣，而愚生過慮，不敢不申言之焉。謹對。
translation_en:
…lies in ensuring that the four measures are implemented and the two abuses eliminated. In recent years, the court suppressed the bandits of Shandong by combining troops and horses from the capital and the frontier and placing them under the direction of high officials from the central and provincial administrations. Its achievement was great. Because the people were then suffering from disasters and banditry, the court also [illegible character] ordered high officials to oversee relief, appointed additional censorial officials to administer military defense, and retained a senior commander with frontier troops to garrison the region. Yet the troops and commanders of Ji [?] are often said to serve in frontier garrisons. Now that frontier forces have been transferred to garrison the interior as a temporary expedient, I truly fear that this cannot continue for long.

The necessary policy now is to require the military defense officials to select and train their troops, while making advance defensive preparations for the provincial capital and important prefectural seats [?]. The administrative and surveillance circuit intendants must care for and relieve the people, while maintaining strict safeguards concerning officials and granary stores. Furthermore, city walls must be raised and moats deepened, and reserves of fodder and grain increased. Then, perhaps, our forces will possess a quiet strength like tigers and leopards in the mountains, while the people will be content, like infants reunited with their mothers. Compared with those who wait until bandits are already running rampant and only then hastily drive people into action, abandoning them to their fate, whose policy is the sounder?

Alas! Once the two evils are removed, the people of Shandong may live anew. Nevertheless, construction projects toil the people, and maintaining troops risks impoverishing them. How much more care must be taken with people whose wounds have only just begun to heal! Those in authority will surely have their own means of handling these matters. Yet I, an ignorant student, am excessively concerned and dare not refrain from stating this once again. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
合一省之士而試之鄉試也
必三年一舉焉舉必三試之
是故其始試之也有書有經
中試有論有詔有誥有表有
判終試有策
定制也是制也有觀士之道焉
===
是故試之經若書以觀其奉
也見體道之功焉試之論以
觀其辨也見窮理之知焉試
之詔誥以觀其典也見黼黻
之文焉試之表以觀其麗也
見忠愛之心焉試之判以觀
其斷也試之策以觀其博也
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

合一省之士而試之，鄉試也。必三年一舉焉，舉必三試之。是故其始試之也，有書、有經；中試有論、有詔、有誥、有表、有判；終試有策。定制也。是制也，有觀士之道焉。

是故試之經若書，以觀其奉也，見體道之功焉；試之論，以觀其辨也，見窮理之知焉；試之詔誥，以觀其典也，見黼黻之文焉；試之表，以觀其麗也，見忠愛之心焉；試之判，以觀其斷也；試之策，以觀其博也。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

To assemble the scholars of an entire province and examine them is the Provincial Examination. It must be held once every three years, and each time it must comprise three sessions. Thus, the first session includes the Four Books and the Classics; the middle session includes discourses, imperial edicts, proclamations, memorials, and legal judgments; and the final session includes policy essays. This is the established system. Within this system lies a means of assessing scholars.

Thus, they are examined on the Classics and the Four Books to observe their reverent adherence and discern their accomplishments in embodying the Way. They are examined through discourses to observe their powers of discrimination and discern their understanding in fathoming principle. They are examined through imperial edicts and proclamations to observe their command of canonical forms and discern writing as finely patterned as ceremonial robes. They are examined through memorials to observe their literary elegance and discern their hearts of loyalty and devotion. They are examined through legal judgments to observe their decisiveness, and through policy essays to observe the breadth of their learning…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
見適用之才焉五者備而士
之能事具矣故曰是制也有
觀士之道焉夫自三代以降
士無全才漢唐宋之設科也
曰明經曰明法曰射策曰博
學宏辭固若是紛紛也定之
者非一人行之者非一代分
===
途而取或難其人焉由
今制觀之彼所謂四科者固兼之
矣而一人咸備焉其才也不
已全乎是固
國之所以觀於士而求之者也
夫上以是觀之則下以是呈
之上以是求之則下以是應
punctuated:
見適用之才焉。五者備，而士之能事具矣。故曰：是制也，有觀士之道焉。夫自三代以降，士無全才。漢唐宋之設科也，曰明經，曰明法，曰射策，曰博學宏辭，固若是紛紛也。定之者非一人，行之者非一代，分途而取，或難其人焉。由今制觀之，彼所謂四科者，固兼之矣，而一人咸備焉，其才也不已全乎？是固國之所以觀於士而求之者也。

夫上以是觀之，則下以是呈之；上以是求之，則下以是應
translation_en:
…revealing their talent for practical application. When these five are present, the accomplishments expected of a scholar are complete. Thus I say: this system provides a way to assess scholars. Since the Three Dynasties, scholars have lacked comprehensive talents. The Han, Tang, and Song established examination categories called Understanding the Classics (mingjing), Understanding the Law (mingfa), Responding to Drawn Policy Questions (shece), and Broad Learning and Extensive Literary Accomplishment (boxue hongci). These were indeed numerous and varied. They were established by more than one person and implemented over more than one dynasty. Yet, recruiting through separate avenues, they sometimes found it difficult to obtain suitable men. Viewed in light of the present system, those so-called four categories are already encompassed within it, and a single person possesses all their requisite accomplishments. Are his talents not already comprehensive? This is precisely how the state assesses scholars and what it seeks in them.

Now, if those above assess them by these standards, those below present themselves accordingly; if those above seek these qualities in them, those below respond accordingly…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之應之者則非徒以其文而
已也故觀於功也而求之效
焉觀於知也而求之行焉觀
於文也而求之質焉觀於心
也而求之身焉觀於才也而
求之政焉故曰五者備而士
之能事具也正德八年八月
===
甲子山東鄉試錄成而〔彰德〕
也主校也承乏於後不可無
言則猶有感焉蓋〔彰德□東〕
也道出淮楚之墟見□埴者
工者揭圖於市以語於人曰
陶瓬之器吾無不能爲也視
其圖焉則甚駭也就其家而
punctuated:
之。應之者，則非徒以其文而已也。故觀於功也，而求之效焉；觀於知也，而求之行焉；觀於文也，而求之質焉；觀於心也，而求之身焉；觀於才也，而求之政焉。故曰：五者備，而士之能事具也。
正德八年八月甲子，山東鄉試錄成，而〔彰德〕也，主校也，承乏於後，不可無言，則猶有感焉。蓋〔彰德□東〕也，道出淮楚之墟，見□埴者工者揭圖於市，以語於人曰：「陶瓬之器，吾無不能爲也。」視其圖焉，則甚駭也；就其家而
translation_en:
…to it. Those who respond do so through more than their writing alone. Thus, when examining their accomplishments, one seeks actual results; when examining their knowledge, one seeks its practice; when examining their literary refinement, one seeks underlying substance; when examining their minds, one seeks its expression in their personal conduct; and when examining their abilities, one seeks their application in government. Hence it is said: when these five are complete, a scholar possesses the full range of capacities required of him.
On the jiazi day of the eighth month of the eighth year of Zhengde [1513], the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination was completed. I, [annotation: Zhangde], serving as chief examiner [?], have taken up the duty of supplying what comes at the end. I cannot leave it without a word, for there is something that has moved me to reflection. For [annotation: Zhangde □ dong; passage unclear], while passing through the Huai and Chu region, I saw a craftsman who worked clay [?] displaying drawings in the marketplace. He told people: “There is no kind of pottery vessel that I cannot make.” Looking at his drawings, I was greatly astonished; I went to his home and…

title: 正德八年山東鄉試錄
text:
求所謂器焉則無有也則猶
以其爲深藏也則篤求之焉
出其器二三焉則皆苦窳而
無當也予甚笑焉夫士也以
文而登斯錄也固所謂全才
者也其無爲是摶埴之工也
哉
浙江湖州府歸安縣儒學訓
導吳彰德謹序
punctuated:
求所謂器焉，則無有也。則猶以其爲深藏也，則篤求之焉。出其器二三焉，則皆苦窳而無當也。予甚笑焉。夫士也，以文而登斯錄也，固所謂全才者也。其無爲是摶埴之工也哉！
浙江湖州府歸安縣儒學訓導吳彰德謹序。
translation_en:
…when I asked to see the vessels he had spoken of, there were none. Still supposing that he had stored them away out of sight, I pressed him to show them. He brought out two or three vessels, but all were poorly made and unfit for use. I laughed heartily at this. Now, the scholars whose compositions have earned them a place in this record are assuredly what we call men of comprehensive talent. May they never become like this craftsman who molds clay!
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Zhangde, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
